statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), let tr_X be the Poincare duality trace, and put beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(x cup L^{d-r}y) for x,y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then for every x in P^r and every integer n>=1, beta_r(x,F^n x)+(-1)^r q^{mrn} beta_r(x,F^{-n}x)=2 beta_r(x,F^n x).
proof: Let D be the F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor whose untwisted cycle class is xi. We write F also for the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on all cohomology groups; its restriction to H^r is the operator named F in the statement. First we justify the scaling of xi. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_291 with the base prime power q0 := q^m, with the same variety X over F_{q0}, with j := 1, with m0 := 1, and with z := D, which is a codimension-1 cycle on X_{F_{q0}}. In that lemma the q0-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is exactly our F, and cl(D) is the image of the Q_ell(1)-cycle class under the fixed identification Q_ell(1) ~ Q_ell that defines xi in the target. Hence F(xi) = q0 xi = q^m xi. No descent to F_q is used. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, applied with base field F_{q^m} and sigma(c)=c^{q^m}, F is an invertible Q_ell-linear automorphism on every H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell), and F^(-1) is the geometric Frobenius. Functoriality of the cup product for the pullback morphism defining F makes F a ring automorphism of the cohomology ring, with F(1)=1 and F(a cup b)=F(a) cup F(b). For any s>=0 and any y in H^t_et(X_k,Q_ell), L^s y = xi^s cup y, so F(L^s y) = F(xi^s cup y) = F(xi)^s cup F(y) = (q^m xi)^s cup F(y) = q^{ms} L^s F(y). In particular, if M := L^{d-r+1}, then F(M y) = q^{m(d-r+1)} M(F y) for all y in H^r. We now show F and F^(-1) preserve P^r = ker(M). If y in P^r, then M y=0, so 0=F(M y)=q^{m(d-r+1)}M(F y), hence F y in P^r. For F^(-1), put z=F^(-1)(y) in the displayed identity: F(M z)=q^{m(d-r+1)}M(y). If y in P^r, then M(y)=0, so F(M z)=0; since F is injective on H^{2d-r+2}, M z=0, i.e. F^(-1)(y) in P^r. Thus F^n(x) and F^(-n)(x) lie in P^r for every n>=1. Next compute the similitude factor of beta_r under F. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, the Poincare trace is Frobenius equivariant: in the untwisted coordinates of the target, tr_X(Fw)=q^{md} tr_X(w) for w in H^{2d}. Therefore for u,v in H^r, beta_r(Fu,Fv)=tr_X(Fu cup L^{d-r} Fv). Using F(L^{d-r}v)=q^{m(d-r)} L^{d-r}Fv, and since ell != p makes q^{m(d-r)} invertible in Q_ell, we get L^{d-r}Fv = q^(-m(d-r)) F(L^{d-r}v). Hence, by Q_ell-linearity of tr_X, beta_r(Fu,Fv)=q^(-m(d-r)) tr_X(F(u cup L^{d-r}v)) = q^(-m(d-r)) q^{md} tr_X(u cup L^{d-r}v) = q^{mr} beta_r(u,v). Iterating by induction on n gives beta_r(F^n u,F^n v)=q^{mrn} beta_r(u,v). Finally, by Miner/16d24b0281973336/2e4606, for all a,b in P^r one has beta_r(a,b)=(-1)^r beta_r(b,a). Apply this to a=x and b=F^(-n)(x), both in P^r: beta_r(x,F^(-n)(x))=(-1)^r beta_r(F^(-n)(x),x). Apply the iterated similitude with u=F^(-n)(x) and v=x: beta_r(x,F^n x)=beta_r(F^n(F^(-n)(x)),F^n x)=q^{mrn} beta_r(F^(-n)(x),x). Therefore beta_r(F^(-n)(x),x)=q^(-mrn) beta_r(x,F^n x), and hence beta_r(x,F^(-n)(x))=(-1)^r q^(-mrn) beta_r(x,F^n x). Substituting into the left side yields beta_r(x,F^n x)+(-1)^r q^{mrn} [(-1)^r q^(-mrn) beta_r(x,F^n x)] = beta_r(x,F^n x)+beta_r(x,F^n x)=2 beta_r(x,F^n x). This proves the claim.

statement: Let ell be a prime, let V and W be finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, let A:V->W be Q_ell-linear, let T_V:V->V and T_W:W->W be Q_ell-linear automorphisms, and let c in Q_ell^* such that T_W A = c A T_V. If T_V is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then T_W is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on im(A).
proof:
We prove that the restriction T_W|_{im(A)} is diagonalizable over K = overline(Q_ell). All vector spaces are finite-dimensional over Q_ell.

Step 1 (T_W preserves im(A)). For any v in V, T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V v) by the hypothesis T_W A = c A T_V. Since T_V v in V, A(T_V v) in im(A), so T_W(A(v)) in im(A). Hence T_W(im(A)) subseteq im(A), and T_W|_{im(A)}: im(A) -> im(A) is a well-defined Q_ell-linear endomorphism. (In fact it is an automorphism of im(A) since T_W is invertible and preserves im(A), but we only need it to be an endomorphism.) The edge case im(A) = {0} is trivial: the zero endomorphism on the zero space is diagonalizable, so assume im(A) != {0} below if desired; the argument works uniformly.

Step 2 (reduce to base change over K). Let V_K = V tensor_{Q_ell} K and W_K = W tensor_{Q_ell} K, and write A_K, T_{V,K}, T_{W,K} for the base-changed maps. The relation T_W A = c A T_V is Q_ell-linear and involves only scalar multiplication by c, so after tensoring with K we get T_{W,K} A_K = c A_K T_{V,K}. The assumption that T_V is diagonalizable over K means exactly that T_{V,K} is diagonalizable over K. Also, T_W|_{im(A)} is diagonalizable over K if and only if (T_W|_{im(A)}) tensor id_K is diagonalizable over K; and (T_W|_{im(A)}) tensor id_K = T_{W,K}|_{im(A) tensor K}. Finally, since K/Q_ell is a field extension (hence flat), base change preserves images: im(A_K) = im(A) tensor_{Q_ell} K. Indeed, factoring A = j o p with p: V -> im(A) surjective and j: im(A) -> W the inclusion, flatness gives that p_K: V_K -> im(A)_K is surjective, so im(A_K) = image(p_K o j_K) = im(A)_K = im(A) tensor K. Therefore it suffices to prove that T_{W,K} is diagonalizable over K on the subspace im(A_K) of W_K.

Step 3 (decompose V_K into eigenspaces of T_{V,K}). Since T_{V,K} is diagonalizable over K, its spectrum sigma = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_r} is a finite subset of K and V_K = direct sum_{i=1}^r E_{lambda_i} where E_{lambda_i} = ker(T_{V,K} - lambda_i id_{V_K}), a direct sum (eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues of a diagonalizable operator are in direct sum and span the space).

Step 4 (images of eigenspaces land in eigenspaces of T_{W,K}). Fix i and let w = A_K(v) with v in E_{lambda_i}. Then T_{W,K}(w) = T_{W,K} A_K(v) = c A_K T_{V,K}(v) = c A_K(lambda_i v) = c lambda_i A_K(v) = c lambda_i w. Thus A_K(E_{lambda_i}) subseteq ker(T_{W,K} - c lambda_i id_{W_K}) =: F_{c lambda_i}. In particular A_K(E_{lambda_i}) is contained in the eigenspace of T_{W,K} for the eigenvalue c lambda_i.

Step 5 (im(A_K) lies in a direct sum of eigenspaces of T_{W,K}). Since V_K = sum_i E_{lambda_i}, im(A_K) = A_K(V_K) = sum_i A_K(E_{lambda_i) subseteq sum_i F_{c lambda_i}. Because c in Q_ell^* is nonzero, the numbers c lambda_i for i = 1,...,r are pairwise distinct (lambda_i != lambda_j implies c lambda_i != c lambda_j). The eigenspaces F_{c lambda_i} of T_{W,K} for the distinct eigenvalues c lambda_1,...,c lambda_r are in direct sum: if w = sum_i w_i with w_i in F_{c lambda_i} and w = 0, then applying the operator prod_{j != i} (T_{W,K} - c lambda_j id) to w gives 0 = prod_{j != i}(c lambda_i - c lambda_j) w_i, and the scalar prod_{j != i}(c lambda_i - c lambda_j) is nonzero, so w_i = 0. Hence M := sum_i F_{c lambda_i} is a direct sum, and T_{W,K}|_M is diagonalizable (M is a direct sum of eigenspaces of T_{W,K}). We have im(A_K) subseteq M.

Step 6 (a T_{W,K}-stable subspace of a diagonalizable direct sum of eigenspaces is diagonalizable). We use that im(A_K) is T_{W,K}-stable: this is the base change of Step 1, i.e. T_{W,K}(im(A_K)) = T_{W,K}(im(A) tensor K) = (T_W(im(A))) tensor K subseteq im(A) tensor K = im(A_K). Now let U = im(A_K) subseteq M. For each i, the spectral projection P_i: M -> F_{c lambda_i} (projection onto the c lambda_i-eigenspace along the other summands) is a polynomial in T_{W,K}|_M: explicitly P_i = prod_{j != i} (T_{W,K}|_M - c lambda_j id)/(c lambda_i - c lambda_j), a polynomial in T_{W,K}|_M with coefficients in K (the scalars c lambda_j lie in K). Since U is stable under T_{W,K}|_M, U is stable under every polynomial in T_{W,K}|_M, in particular under P_i. Therefore for any u in U, u = sum_i P_i(u) with P_i(u) in U cap F_{c lambda_i}. Hence U = sum_i (U cap F_{c lambda_i}). Because the F_{c lambda_i} are in direct sum, the subspaces U cap F_{c lambda_i} are also in direct sum, so U = direct sum_i (U cap F_{c lambda_i}). On each U cap F_{c lambda_i}, T_{W,K} acts by the scalar c lambda_i, so each U cap F_{c lambda_i} is an eigenspace of T_{W,K}|_U. Thus U = im(A_K) is a direct sum of eigenspaces of T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)}, which means T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)} is diagonalizable over K.

Step 7 (conclusion). From Step 6, T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)} is diagonalizable over K. By the equivalences in Step 2, this is exactly the statement that T_W|_{im(A)} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). This completes the proof.

Remark on the edge cases: if im(A) = {0}, then im(A_K) = {0} and T_{W,K}|_{im(A_K)} is the zero map on the zero space, trivially diagonalizable, so the conclusion holds. If A = 0 this is the same case. No further degeneracy occurs because c != 0 guarantees the eigenvalues c lambda_i remain distinct, keeping the eigenspace decomposition in Step 5 a genuine direct sum.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Suppose F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for 0<=r<d. Then for every integer j>=1 with d-2j>=0, F on L^j P^{d-2j} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Let Q = q^m. Fix an integer j >= 1 with r = d - 2j >= 0. We prove that F on L^j P^r is diagonalizable over Qbar_l. By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/305609, the subspace P^r is stable under F, i.e. F(P^r) = P^r. Now apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable to the prime power Q and to the variety X over F_Q, with the given very ample divisor and its cycle class xi. The Frobenius appearing in that lemma is the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius, which is exactly the operator F in the statement. It gives F L = Q L F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_l). By induction from this relation we obtain F L^j = Q^j L^j F on H^r. The hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n = r gives that L^{2j}: H^r_et(X_k,Q_l) -> H^{d+2j}_et(X_k,Q_l) is an isomorphism, hence injective. If x in P^r satisfies L^j x = 0, then L^{2j} x = L^j(L^j x) = 0, so x = 0. Thus phi = L^j restricted to P^r is an isomorphism from P^r onto L^j P^r. By hypothesis F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_l) is diagonalizable over Qbar_l. Since P^r is F-stable, F|_{P^r} is diagonalizable over Qbar_l: after scalar extension to Qbar_l, write V = H^r_et(X_k,Q_l) tensor Qbar_l and W = P^r tensor Qbar_l; the operator T = F tensor id on V is diagonalizable, so V is the direct sum of its eigenspaces V_lambda; the eigenspace projections are polynomial functions in T and hence preserve the T-stable subspace W, so W is the direct sum of W intersect V_lambda and is spanned by eigenvectors. For y in L^j P^r write y = phi(x) = L^j x with x in P^r. Then F(y) = F(L^j x) = Q^j L^j F(x) = phi(Q^j F(x)), because F(x) lies in P^r. Hence F|_{L^j P^r} = phi (Q^j F|_{P^r}) phi^{-1}. The scalar Q^j is nonzero in Q_l because ell != p, and a nonzero scalar multiple of a diagonalizable operator is diagonalizable over Qbar_l (the same eigenvectors work). Conjugation by an isomorphism preserves diagonalizability. Therefore F|_{L^j P^r} is diagonalizable over Qbar_l. Since j was arbitrary with d - 2j >= 0, the claim follows.

statement: Let ell be a prime, let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C be an embedding, let r>0 be a real number, let V and W be finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, let A:V->W be Q_ell-linear, let T_V:V->V and T_W:W->W be Q_ell-linear automorphisms, and let c in Q_ell^* such that T_W A = c A T_V. If every eigenvalue alpha of T_V satisfies |sigma(alpha)|=r, then every eigenvalue beta of T_W on im(A) satisfies |sigma(beta)|=|sigma(c)| r.
proof:
We prove the statement by pure linear algebra over Q_ell, reducing the scalar-twisted intertwining relation to an ordinary conjugacy on a quotient space, then using the standard fact that the spectrum of an induced quotient operator is contained in the spectrum of the original operator.

SETUP AND NOTATION. Let K = ker(A) \subseteq V. Write S := T_W|_{im(A)} for the restriction of T_W to im(A) (its well-definedness as a map im(A)->im(A) is established in Step 1). All operators below are Q_ell-linear. Eigenvalues are taken in the algebraic closure overline(Q_ell); the given embedding sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C is a field embedding, hence a ring homomorphism, so sigma(xy)=sigma(x)sigma(y) and sigma(x+y)=sigma(x)+sigma(y) for all x,y in overline(Q_ell).

STEP 0 (edge case). If im(A) = {0}, then S is the zero map on the zero vector space, whose characteristic polynomial is 1 (degree 0) and which therefore has no eigenvalues in overline(Q_ell). The assertion 'every eigenvalue beta of T_W on im(A) satisfies |sigma(beta)|=|sigma(c)| r' is then vacuously true. Henceforth assume im(A) != {0}.

STEP 1 (T_W preserves im(A)). Let y in im(A); then y = A(v) for some v in V. By the hypothesis T_W A = c A T_V we have T_W(y) = T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V(v)). Since T_V(v) in V, the element A(T_V(v)) lies in im(A); as im(A) is a Q_ell-subspace of W and c in Q_ell^*, the scalar multiple c A(T_V(v)) also lies in im(A). Thus T_W(im(A)) \subseteq im(A), so the restriction S := T_W|_{im(A)}:im(A)->im(A) is well-defined. Because T_W is an automorphism of W and im(A) is T_W-stable, S is an automorphism of im(A) (its inverse is (T_W^{-1})|_{im(A)}).

STEP 2 (T_V preserves K = ker(A)). Let v in K, so A(v)=0. Applying the intertwining relation to v gives T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V(v)), i.e. T_W(0) = c A(T_V(v)), so c A(T_V(v)) = 0. Since c != 0, A(T_V(v)) = 0, hence T_V(v) in K. Thus T_V(K) \subseteq K, i.e. K is T_V-stable.

STEP 3 (quotient isomorphism). The map A:V->im(A) is surjective by definition of the image, and its kernel is K. By the first isomorphism theorem it induces a Q_ell-linear isomorphism \\bar{A}:V/K -> im(A) given by \\bar{A}(v+K) = A(v). This is well-defined and bijective: well-definedness follows because if v+K = v'+K then v-v' in K so A(v)-A(v')=0; surjectivity is the definition of im(A); injectivity follows because ker(\\bar{A}) = {v+K : A(v)=0} = K/(K) = {0}.

STEP 4 (induced operator on V/K). Since K is T_V-stable (Step 2), T_V induces a Q_ell-linear operator \\bar{T}_V:V/K -> V/K given by \\bar{T}_V(v+K) = T_V(v)+K. This is well-defined: if v+K = v'+K then v-v' in K and T_V(v)-T_V(v') in T_V(K) \subseteq K, so T_V(v)+K = T_V(v')+K. It is an automorphism because T_V is.

STEP 5 (conjugacy). We claim S \\circ \\bar{A} = c \\bar{A} \\circ \\bar{T}_V. For any v+K in V/K: \\bar{A}(\\bar{T}_V(v+K)) = \\bar{A}(T_V(v)+K) = A(T_V(v)). On the other hand S(\\bar{A}(v+K)) = S(A(v)) = T_W(A(v)) = c A(T_V(v)) by the intertwining relation. Hence S\\circ\\bar{A}(v+K) = c A(T_V(v)) = c \\bar{A}(\\bar{T}_V(v+K)), and the claim follows. Since \\bar{A} is an isomorphism, this is equivalent to S = c \\bar{A} \\circ \\bar{T}_V \\circ \\bar{A}^{-1}. Thus S is similar (conjugate) to the operator c\\bar{T}_V on V/K.

STEP 6 (spectrum of S). Similar operators over Q_ell have identical characteristic polynomials, hence identical multisets of eigenvalues in overline(Q_ell) (with multiplicity). Therefore the multiset of eigenvalues of S equals the multiset of eigenvalues of c\\bar{T}_V. For any Q_ell-linear operator N on a finite-dimensional space and any nonzero scalar c in Q_ell, the eigenvalues of cN are exactly {c\\cdot\\lambda : \\lambda an eigenvalue of N}: indeed if Nx = \\lambda x with x != 0 then (cN)x = (c\\lambda)x, and conversely if (cN)x = \\mu x with x != 0 then N x = (\\mu/c) x since c != 0. Equivalently, with \\lambda_1,...,\\lambda_s the eigenvalues of \\bar{T}_V, the characteristic polynomial of c\\bar{T}_V is \\prod_i (t - c\\lambda_i). Consequently every eigenvalue beta of S (equivalently of T_W on im(A)) is of the form beta = c\\cdot\\mu for some eigenvalue \\mu of \\bar{T}_V in overline(Q_ell).

STEP 7 (spectrum of \\bar{T}_V is contained in spectrum of T_V). We prove the general fact that the eigenvalues of the induced operator on the quotient are a subset of the eigenvalues of the original operator, by an explicit block-matrix computation. Let n = dim V and k = dim K. Choose a Q_ell-basis (e_1,...,e_n) of V such that (e_1,...,e_k) is a basis of K. Because K is T_V-stable (Step 2), T_V(e_i) in K for i = 1,...,k, so in this basis the matrix of T_V has block upper-triangular form [T_V] = [[B, C],[0, D]], where B is k x k, C is k x (n-k), 0 is (n-k) x k, and D is (n-k) x (n-k). The block B represents T_V|_K, and the block D represents the induced operator \\bar{T}_V on V/K with respect to the induced basis (e_{k+1}+K,...,e_n+K): indeed for j > k, \\bar{T}_V(e_j+K) = T_V(e_j)+K, and the V/K-component of T_V(e_j) is read off from the last n-k coordinates, which are D times the coordinate vector. Hence \\chi_{\\bar{T}_V}(t) = det(t I_{n-k} - D). The characteristic polynomial of T_V is \\chi_{T_V}(t) = det(t I_n - [T_V]) = det([[tI_k - B, -C],[0, tI_{n-k} - D]]) = det(tI_k - B)\\cdot det(tI_{n-k} - D) = \\chi_{T_V|_K}(t)\\cdot\\chi_{\\bar{T}_V}(t), using that the determinant of a block upper-triangular matrix is the product of the determinants of the diagonal blocks. Thus \\chi_{\\bar{T}_V} divides \\chi_{T_V} in Q_ell[t]. Any eigenvalue \\mu of \\bar{T}_V is a root of \\chi_{\\bar{T}_V} in overline(Q_ell), hence a root of \\chi_{T_V} in overline(Q_ell), hence an eigenvalue of T_V. So Spec(\\bar{T}_V) \\subseteq Spec(T_V).

STEP 8 (conclusion). Let beta be any eigenvalue of T_W on im(A) = im(A), i.e. any eigenvalue of S in overline(Q_ell). By Step 6, beta = c\\cdot\\mu for some eigenvalue \\mu of \\bar{T}_V. By Step 7, \\mu is an eigenvalue of T_V, so by the hypothesis |sigma(\\mu)| = r. Since sigma is a ring homomorphism, sigma(beta) = sigma(c\\cdot\\mu) = sigma(c)\\cdot sigma(\\mu). Taking complex absolute values, |sigma(beta)| = |sigma(c)\\cdot sigma(\\mu)| = |sigma(c)|\\cdot|sigma(\\mu)| = |sigma(c)|\\cdot r. This holds for every eigenvalue beta of T_W on im(A), completing the proof. (The edge case im(A)={0} was handled in Step 0.)

REMARK ON THE ROLE OF THE HYPOTHESES. The assumption that T_V and T_W are automorphisms guarantees S is an automorphism of im(A) (Step 1) and that \\bar{T}_V is an automorphism (Step 4), though only the Q_ell-linearity and the intertwining relation T_W A = c A T_V with c != 0 are used to obtain the conjugacy (Step 5) and the spectral inclusion (Steps 6-7). The condition c in Q_ell^* (nonzero) is used in Steps 2, 6 to divide by c. The number r > 0 and the embedding sigma enter only in the final absolute-value computation of Step 8, where multiplicativity of sigma and of the complex absolute value are the only properties used.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected. Let F_X and F_Y be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^*_et(Y_k,Q_ell), respectively. If F_Y on H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every integer r with 0<=r<d, then F_X on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every integer r with 0<=r<d.
proof: Fix an integer r with 0 <= r < d and let i:Y -> X be the closed immersion. Since Y is a very ample divisor, it is in particular an ample divisor; by hypothesis it is smooth of pure dimension d-1 and geometrically connected. If 0 <= r <= d-2, the injectivity of the restriction map i^*:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) follows from Miner/16d24b0281973336/d35572. If r = d-1, the same injectivity follows from Miner/16d24b0281973336/79a472. Hence, for every integer r with 0 <= r < d, the restriction map i^* is a Q_ell-linear injection. Next, apply Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_283 to the pair (X,Y) over the base field F_{q^m}, i.e. replace the parameter q in that lemma by the prime power q^m. That lemma gives the Gysin long exact sequence for the pair (X,Y), and it states that every map in the sequence commutes with the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms. In particular, the middle map i^* commutes with Frobenius, so on degree r cohomology we have F_Y i^* = i^* F_X. The groups H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces, and F_X and F_Y are Q_ell-linear automorphisms, since they are induced by the arithmetic Frobenius element. Now apply Miner/16d24b0281973336/975459 with V=H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), W=H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell), phi=i^*, T=F_X, and S=F_Y. The map phi is injective, the compatibility S phi = phi T holds by the previous paragraph, and S is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) by the hypothesis on F_Y. Therefore T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Thus F_X is diagonalizable on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since r was arbitrary with 0 <= r < d, this proves the desired conclusion.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let W be the image of i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell), and let tr_Y:H^{2d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell be the Poincare duality trace. Then the Q_ell-bilinear form (a,b)->tr_Y(a cup b) on W is nondegenerate.
proof: Let xi be the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) under the fixed identification Q_ell(1)=Q_ell, and let L be cup product with xi: H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since Y is an ample divisor, the line bundle O_X(Y) is an ample line bundle on X. By the standard hard Lefschetz theorem for smooth projective varieties in ell-adic cohomology, applied to X_k with the ample class xi, for every integer n with 0 <= n <= d the map cup product with xi^{d-n}: H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Taking n = d-1 gives that L is an isomorphism, hence L is injective. Now apply Miner/16d24b0281973336/3385cf. Its hypotheses match the present situation exactly: X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d >= 2 over F_{q^m}, Y is a smooth ample geometrically connected divisor over F_{q^m}, xi is the cycle class of Y, L is cup product with xi, W is the image of i^*: H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell), and tr_Y is the Poincare duality trace. That lemma says that the Q_ell-bilinear form (a,b) -> tr_Y(a cup b) on W is nondegenerate if and only if L is injective. Since L is injective, the form is nondegenerate. This proves the statement.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), let L be cup product with xi, and suppose i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Then the image of the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) equals L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
I found the key lemma. Let me verify the exact statement of the projection formula I need.

The lemma `eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor` states that for a smooth effective divisor $Y \subset X$ with inclusion $i$, the projection formula $i_!(i^*x) = x \cup \xi$ holds for all $x \in H^n(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$.

Now let me verify the hypotheses match. In the target:
- $X$ is over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$, $Y$ is a smooth ample (hence effective) divisor over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$
- $k = \overline{\mathbb{F}_q} = \overline{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}}$
- The projection formula lemma is stated for varieties over a prime power field; I apply it with the prime power $q^m = p^{am}$

The proof is then a short two-line argument using the projection formula plus the isomorphism hypothesis on $i^*$.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/b8e973",
  "cited_lemmas": ["eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that im(i_!) = L·H^{d-2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) by establishing both inclusions.\n\n**Setup and application of the projection formula.** We invoke the Gysin projection formula for a smooth divisor, lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor. To apply it, we note that q^m = p^{am} is a prime power. We view X as a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d ≥ 2 over the field F_{q^m}, and Y as a smooth effective divisor of pure dimension d−1 defined over F_{q^m} (this is immediate from the hypotheses: Y is a smooth ample divisor on the d-dimensional X, hence a smooth effective divisor of dimension d−1). The algebraic closure of F_{q^m} is the same field k = overline(F_q). The identification of Q_ℓ(1) with Q_ℓ is the one fixed in the target statement, and ξ ∈ H²_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) is the cycle class of Y under this identification, with L denoting cup product with ξ. The Gysin map in the projection formula, with n = d−2, is precisely i_!: H^{d−2}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) → H^d_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ), the same map appearing in the target. By the projection formula, for every x ∈ H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ):\n\n    i_!(i^* x) = x ∪ ξ = L(x).   (∗)\n\n**First inclusion: L·H^{d−2}(X_k) ⊆ im(i_!).** Let x ∈ H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) be arbitrary. Since i^* is a map H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{d−2}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ), the element i^*x lies in H^{d−2}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ), and by (∗), L(x) = i_!(i^*x) ∈ im(i_!). Since x was arbitrary, L·H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) ⊆ im(i_!).\n\n**Second inclusion: im(i_!) ⊆ L·H^{d−2}(X_k).** Let y ∈ H^{d−2}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) be arbitrary. By the hypothesis of the target lemma, i^*: H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{d−2}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) is an isomorphism, in particular surjective. Hence there exists x ∈ H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) with i^*x = y. Then by (∗):\n\n    i_!(y) = i_!(i^*x) = L(x) ∈ L·H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ).\n\nSince y was arbitrary, im(i_!) ⊆ L·H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ).\n\n**Conclusion.** The two inclusions together give im(i_!) = L·H^{d−2}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ), as required."
}

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor on X, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer n with 0<=n<=d. For 0<=s<=d put P^s=ker(L^{d-s+1}:H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-s+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If each subspace L^j P^{d-2j} with d-2j>=0 is stable under F and F is diagonalizable on it over overline(Q_ell), then F on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Let V=H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) and let T=F. Since X is smooth projective of pure dimension d, V is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space. The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is induced by the automorphism of the etale site x -> x^{q^m}, hence it is an invertible Q_ell-linear endomorphism of V; thus T is in GL(V). Put j_0=floor(d/2). For each integer j with 0<=j<=j_0, let W_j be the subspace L^j P^{d-2j} of V, i.e. the image of the Q_ell-linear map L^j:P^{d-2j}->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ac7db0, the natural linear map Phi: direct sum_{j=0}^{j_0} W_j -> V, (x_j) -> x_0+...+x_{j_0}, is an isomorphism. In particular, V = W_0 + ... + W_{j_0}. By the hypothesis of the target lemma, for every j with d-2j>=0, equivalently 0<=j<=j_0, the subspace W_j is stable under F and the restriction F|_{W_j} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell); equivalently, each restriction is semisimple. Now apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_230 to the finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space V, the automorphism T=F, and the T-stable Q_ell-subspaces W_0,...,W_{j_0}. Their sum is V, and T|_{W_j} is semisimple for every j. Therefore T is semisimple on V. For a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, semisimplicity of an automorphism is equivalent to diagonalizability over overline(Q_ell). Hence F on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=3, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth effective ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let i_!: H^{2d-3}_{et}(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d-1}_{et}(X_k,Q_ell) be the Gysin homomorphism. Then i_! is an isomorphism.
proof:
We prove that the Gysin map $i_!: H^{2d-3}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to H^{2d-1}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ is an isomorphism.

**Step 1: The Gysin adjunction.** By the Gysin projection formula (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor), the Gysin homomorphism $i_!$ is characterized by the identity
$$\operatorname{tr}_X(i_!(a) \cup b) = \operatorname{tr}_Y(a \cup i^* b)$$
for all $a \in H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ and $b \in H^{2d-2-n}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, where $\operatorname{tr}_X$ and $\operatorname{tr}_Y$ are the Poincaré duality traces.

Taking $n = 2d-3$, we have $2d-2-n = 2d-2-(2d-3) = 1$. Hence for all $a \in H^{2d-3}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ and $b \in H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$:
$$\operatorname{tr}_X(i_!(a) \cup b) = \operatorname{tr}_Y(a \cup i^* b). \quad (\star)$$

**Step 2: Poincaré duality pairings are perfect.** By Poincaré duality (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77), for a smooth projective geometrically connected variety $Z$ of pure dimension $r$, the pairing
$$\beta_Z: H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Z_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \times H^{2r-n}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Z_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to \mathbb{Q}_\ell, \quad (u, v) \mapsto \operatorname{tr}_Z(u \cup v)$$
is a perfect pairing for every $0 \leq n \leq 2r$.

Apply this to $X$ (dimension $d$) with $n = 2d-1$: since $0 \leq 2d-1 \leq 2d$, the pairing
$$\beta_X: H^{2d-1}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \times H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to \mathbb{Q}_\ell, \quad (u, v) \mapsto \operatorname{tr}_X(u \cup v)$$
is perfect.

Apply this to $Y$ (dimension $d-1$) with $n = 2d-3$: since $0 \leq 2d-3 \leq 2(d-1) = 2d-2$ (as $d \geq 3$), the pairing
$$\beta_Y: H^{2d-3}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \times H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to \mathbb{Q}_\ell, \quad (u, v) \mapsto \operatorname{tr}_Y(u \cup v)$$
is perfect.

**Step 3: Identify the adjoint of $i_!$.** Define the adjoint $i_!^\dagger: H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ by the requirement that for all $a \in H^{2d-3}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ and $b \in H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$:
$$\beta_X(i_!(a), b) = \beta_Y(a, i_!^\dagger(b)).$$

By the Gysin adjunction $(\star)$, for all such $a$ and $b$:
$$\beta_X(i_!(a), b) = \operatorname{tr}_X(i_!(a) \cup b) = \operatorname{tr}_Y(a \cup i^* b) = \beta_Y(a, i^* b).$$

Hence $\beta_Y(a, i^* b) = \beta_Y(a, i_!^\dagger(b))$ for all $a \in H^{2d-3}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ and $b \in H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$. Since $\beta_Y$ is perfect (in particular, nondegenerate in the first variable), fixing $b$ and varying $a$, we get $i^* b = i_!^\dagger(b)$ for all $b$. Therefore
$$i_!^\dagger = i^*: H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell). \quad (\star\star)$$

**Step 4: $i^*$ is an isomorphism in degree 1.** By the surjectivity result (Miner/16d24b0281973336/fdc534), for $0 \leq n \leq d-2$, the restriction map $i^*: H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ is surjective. By the injectivity result (Miner/16d24b0281973336/d35572), for $0 \leq n \leq d-2$, the same map is injective.

Since $d \geq 3$, we have $1 \leq d-2$. Taking $n = 1$, both results apply: $i^*: H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ is both surjective and injective, hence an isomorphism.

**Step 5: Conclude $i_!$ is an isomorphism.** We use the following linear algebra fact: Let $V, W, V', W'$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ with perfect pairings $\beta_V: V \times V' \to \mathbb{Q}_\ell$ and $\beta_W: W \times W' \to \mathbb{Q}_\ell$. For a linear map $T: V \to W$, its adjoint $T^\dagger: W' \to V'$ is defined by $\beta_W(T(v), w') = \beta_V(v, T^\dagger(w'))$. Then $T$ is an isomorphism if and only if $T^\dagger$ is an isomorphism.

*Proof of the fact:* We have $\ker(T^\dagger) = \{w' \in W' : T^\dagger(w') = 0\} = \{w' \in W' : \beta_W(T(v), w') = 0 \text{ for all } v \in V\} = \operatorname{im}(T)^\perp$, where $\operatorname{im}(T)^\perp = \{w' \in W' : \beta_W(w, w') = 0 \text{ for all } w \in \operatorname{im}(T)\}$. Since $\beta_W$ is perfect, $\operatorname{im}(T)^\perp = 0$ if and only if $\operatorname{im}(T) = W$. Hence $T^\dagger$ is injective if and only if $T$ is surjective.

Similarly, $\ker(T) = \{v \in V : T(v) = 0\} = \{v \in V : \beta_W(T(v), w') = 0 \text{ for all } w' \in W'\} = \{v \in V : \beta_V(v, T^\dagger(w')) = 0 \text{ for all } w' \in W'\} = \operatorname{im}(T^\dagger)^\perp$. Since $\beta_V$ is perfect, $\operatorname{im}(T^\dagger)^\perp = 0$ if and only if $\operatorname{im}(T^\dagger) = V'$. Hence $T$ is injective if and only if $T^\dagger$ is surjective.

Therefore $T^\dagger$ is an isomorphism (both injective and surjective) if and only if $T$ is both surjective and injective, i.e., $T$ is an isomorphism.

Applying this with $V = H^{2d-3}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, $W = H^{2d-1}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, $V' = H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, $W' = H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, $T = i_!$, and using $(\star\star)$ which gives $T^\dagger = i^*$, we conclude: since $i^*$ is an isomorphism (Step 4), $i_!$ is an isomorphism.

This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Then for every integer n with 0<=n<d-1, the restriction map i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism.
proof:
We prove that for every integer n with 0<=n<d-1 the restriction map i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism.

First, reduce the stated range. Fix an integer n with 0<=n<d-1. Since n and d-1 are integers, the strict inequality n<d-1 is equivalent to n<=(d-1)-1=d-2. Together with n>=0 this gives 0<=n<=d-2. Conversely, every integer n with 0<=n<=d-2 satisfies n<d-1. Hence the set of integers n with 0<=n<d-1 is exactly the set of integers n with 0<=n<=d-2, so it suffices to prove the assertion for 0<=n<=d-2.

Now compare the hypotheses. The present lemma assumes: q=p^a is a prime power, ell!=p is a prime, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, Y is a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and i:Y->X is the inclusion. These are precisely the hypotheses of the two proved lemmas Miner/16d24b0281973336/d35572 and Miner/16d24b0281973336/fdc534. Therefore both lemmas apply to the same X, Y, i, and to every degree n in the range 0<=n<=d-2.

Injectivity. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/d35572, for every integer n with 0<=n<=d-2 the restriction map i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective.

Surjectivity. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/fdc534, for every integer n with 0<=n<=d-2 the restriction map i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is surjective.

Now let n be any integer with 0<=n<d-1, hence 0<=n<=d-2. Let f:=i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). The map f is Q_ell-linear, since etale cohomology is a functor with Q_ell-vector-space values and restriction is induced by the morphism i. By the two lemmas, f is both injective and surjective, hence bijective as a map of sets.

We verify that the set-theoretic inverse of f is Q_ell-linear, so that f is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces. Let g:H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) be the unique set-theoretic inverse of f. For additivity, take y1,y2 in H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). By surjectivity of f there exist v1,v2 in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) with f(v1)=y1 and f(v2)=y2; by injectivity these v1,v2 are unique. Then
  g(y1+y2)=g(f(v1)+f(v2))=g(f(v1+v2))=v1+v2=g(f(v1))+g(f(v2))=g(y1)+g(y2),
using that f is additive. For scalar multiplication, take c in Q_ell and y in H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Choose v in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) with f(v)=y. Then
  g(c y)=g(c f(v))=g(f(c v))=c v=c g(f(v))=c g(y).
Thus g is Q_ell-linear. By construction, f(g(y))=y for all y in H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) and g(f(v))=v for all v in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell), so f and g are mutual inverses. Therefore f is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism.

Since n was arbitrary with 0<=n<d-1, the restriction map i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every such n. QED

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U be the open complement of Y in X, and let i:Y->X and j:U->X be the inclusions. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), let L be cup product with xi, and suppose i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Then the kernel of j^*:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) equals L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof: Let q' = q^m = p^{am}. Then q' is a prime power and ell != p. The field k = overline(F_q) is algebraically closed and contains F_{q'}; hence it is an algebraic closure of F_{q'}. We therefore instantiate the two cited lemmas with q' in place of q and with this same k. First apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement. Its hypotheses are satisfied: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d >= 1 over F_{q'}; Y is a smooth effective divisor on X defined over F_{q'} of pure dimension d-1, because a smooth ample divisor is in particular an effective Cartier divisor and has codimension 1 in the d-dimensional variety X; U is the open complement of Y in X; i and j are the inclusions; and ell != p. The lemma gives a long exact sequence of Q_ell-vector spaces, and the segment at degree d is H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) --i_!--> H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) --j^*--> H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell). By exactness, ker(j^*) = im(i_!). Next apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_550 with the same field instantiation. Its hypotheses are satisfied: d >= 2; X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q'}; Y is a nonempty effective ample Cartier divisor defined over F_{q'} that is smooth of pure dimension d-1, where nonemptiness follows because d-1 >= 1 and Y is a smooth geometrically connected divisor; i is the closed immersion; we have fixed a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identified Tate twists with Q_ell; xi is the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell); and L is cup product with xi. The conclusion is that the image of the Gysin homomorphism i_!: H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) -> H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) equals L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). This i_! is the same standard Gysin homomorphism for the closed immersion i that occurs in the long exact sequence above, so its image is exactly the subspace im(i_!) appearing in the exactness statement. Combining the two equalities gives ker(j^*) = L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). The additional standing hypothesis that i^*: H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism is not needed for this argument. This proves the target statement.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U be the open complement of Y in X, and let i:Y->X and j:U->X be the inclusions. Let F_X, F_Y, and F_U be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1), and H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell), respectively. Then the segment H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) -> H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) with maps i_! and j^* is exact as a sequence of F-modules.
proof: Let Frb_Z denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of Z_k, and let F_Z be the induced automorphism on etale cohomology. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement to X over the finite field F_{q^m} (replace q by q^m in that statement) with the smooth divisor Y and n=d. It gives exactness of the segment H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) -> H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) as a sequence of Q_ell-vector spaces. It remains to check the two maps are F-linear. Since j:U->X is defined over F_{q^m}, j o Frb_U = Frb_X o j; pulling back in etale cohomology gives F_U o j^* = j^* o F_X. For the Gysin map, let F_{Y,d} be the q^m-power Frobenius on H^d(Y_k,Q_ell). Since i:Y->X is defined over F_{q^m}, i o Frb_Y = Frb_X o i, hence i^* o F_X = F_{Y,d} o i^* for i^*:H^d(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d(Y_k,Q_ell). Let <,>_X be the Poincare pairing on H^d(X_k,Q_ell) with values in Q_ell(-d). Let ( , )_Y be the Poincare pairing on H^{d-2}(Y_k,Q_ell) x H^d(Y_k,Q_ell) with values in Q_ell(-(d-1)). By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, <F_X a, F_X b>_X = q^{md}<a,b>_X and (F_{Y,d-2} c, F_{Y,d} z)_Y = q^{m(d-1)}(c,z)_Y, where F_{Y,d-2} is the untwisted Frobenius on H^{d-2}(Y_k,Q_ell). The same lemma with dimension 1 gives that F acts on Q_ell(-1) as multiplication by q^m. Define the twisted pairing [ , ]_Y on H^{d-2}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) x H^d(Y_k,Q_ell) with values in Q_ell(-d) by [x_0 tensor t, z] = (x_0,z)_Y tensor t. If x=x_0 tensor t, then F_Y x = F_{Y,d-2} x_0 tensor q^m t, and therefore [F_Y x, F_{Y,d} z] = q^{m(d-1)} q^m [x,z] = q^{md}[x,z]. The Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)->H^d(X_k,Q_ell) is the Poincare dual of i^*:H^d(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d(Y_k,Q_ell); equivalently, for all x and y, <i_! x, y>_X = [x, i^* y]_Y. This is the standard adjunction formula for the Gysin map of a smooth closed immersion of relative dimension one. Now for x in H^{d-2}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) and y in H^d(X_k,Q_ell), we have <i_! (F_Y x), F_X y>_X = [F_Y x, i^* F_X y]_Y = [F_Y x, F_{Y,d} i^* y]_Y = q^{md}[x, i^* y]_Y = q^{md}<i_! x, y>_X = <F_X i_! x, F_X y>_X. Since <,>_X is perfect by lemma_77, this implies i_! o F_Y = F_X o i_!. Thus both i_! and j^* are F-linear. The underlying sequence is exact by the Gysin sequence lemma, so im(i_!) = ker(j^*) as Q_ell-subspaces. Because i_! and j^* are F-linear, both sides are F_X-stable, and the segment is exact as a sequence of Q_ell[F]-modules.

  "proof": "We prove the result by applying the proved lemma Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_primitive_middle_as_affine_kernel. We verify that every hypothesis of that lemma is satisfied by the present setup.

Hypotheses on X. The cited lemma requires X to be smooth, projective, geometrically connected, of pure dimension d >= 2 over F_{q^m}. This is exactly the hypothesis of the target lemma. (q = p^a, ell != p, m >= 1, k = overline(F_q), d >= 2 all match.)

Hypotheses on Y. The cited lemma requires Y subset X to be a nonempty effective very ample Cartier divisor defined over F_{q^m}, smooth and geometrically connected of pure dimension d-1. We verify each item.

(i) Y is an effective Cartier divisor, defined over F_{q^m}, and O_X(Y) is very ample. By the standard definition of a very ample divisor, Y is an effective Cartier divisor on X such that the associated line bundle O_X(Y) is very ample. Since Y is defined over F_{q^m} (given in the target), the Cartier divisor Y and its associated line bundle are defined over F_{q^m}.

(ii) Y is nonempty. This is the key verification (the defect in the previous attempt was a non sequitur here, which we now fix properly). Suppose for contradiction that Y is empty. Since Y is an effective Cartier divisor, Y is the zero scheme of a global section s of the line bundle L := O_X(Y). If Y is empty, then s is nowhere vanishing on X, so s is a global unit section of L, which trivializes L; i.e., L is isomorphic to O_X. But L is very ample by (i), so O_X would be very ample. We show this is impossible. By the standard characterization of very ample line bundles on a projective scheme (a line bundle is very ample if and only if the morphism to projective space defined by a basis of its global sections is a closed embedding), if O_X were very ample then the morphism phi: X -> P^{h^0(X, O_X) - 1} defined by a basis of H^0(X, O_X) would be a closed embedding. Since X is proper and geometrically connected over F_{q^m}, the ring of global regular functions is H^0(X, O_X) = F_{q^m}, so h^0(X, O_X) = 1, and phi: X -> P^0 is the constant map. A constant map phi: X -> P^0 = Spec(F_{q^m}) is a closed embedding if and only if X is isomorphic to a closed subscheme of Spec(F_{q^m}); the only closed subschemes of Spec(F_{q^m}) are Spec(F_{q^m}) itself and the empty scheme, so this would force X to be a single point. But X is a variety of pure dimension d >= 2, hence X is not a single point (over k = overline(F_q) it has infinitely many closed points). Contradiction. Hence Y is nonempty.

(iii) Y is of pure dimension d - 1. Since X is smooth, X is a regular scheme of pure dimension d. Since Y is a nonempty effective Cartier divisor on X, Y is a closed subscheme of X that is locally (in the Zariski topology) defined by a single non-zero-divisor equation. Let Z be an irreducible component of Y, with generic point eta. There is an open neighborhood V of eta in X and a function f in O_X(V) such that Z cap V = V(f) (the zero scheme of f) and f is a non-zero-divisor in O_X(V). Since X is regular, the local ring O_{X, eta} is a regular local ring, hence a domain, and f is a non-zero-divisor (in fact f != 0) in O_{X, eta}. By the Krull principal ideal theorem, the height of the prime ideal (f) in O_{X, eta} is at most 1; since f != 0 in the domain O_{X, eta}, the ideal (f) is nonzero, so its height is at least 1. Hence the height is exactly 1, meaning the codimension of Z in X is 1. Since X is of pure dimension d, the component Z has dimension d - 1. Since this holds for every irreducible component Z of Y, and Y is nonempty (so it has at least one irreducible component), Y is of pure dimension d - 1.

(iv) Y is smooth and geometrically connected. This is given directly in the target lemma.

Thus Y is a nonempty effective very ample Cartier divisor on X, defined over F_{q^m}, smooth and geometrically connected of pure dimension d - 1, exactly as the cited lemma requires.

Remaining hypotheses. The cited lemma requires: U = X \ Y is the open complement with inclusion j: U -> X (matching the target's 'let U be the open complement of Y in X'); xi in H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell) is the cycle class of Y and L is cup product with xi (matching); P^d = ker(L: H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d+2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)) (matching); L^{d-n}: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-n}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every 0 <= n <= d (this is exactly the hypothesis of the target lemma); and the identification of Tate twists with Q_ell via a fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) (matching). All match.

Application of the cited lemma. By Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_primitive_middle_as_affine_kernel, the restriction j^* restricts to an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules
  P^d --> ker[ H^d_et(U_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) ],
where F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius and the right-hand map is the connecting homomorphism of the Gysin sequence of (X, Y).

By the long exact Gysin sequence of the open complement (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement), the connecting homomorphism in degree n = d is the boundary map partial: H^d_et(U_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1). Under the fixed identification of Tate twists with Q_ell, H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) is identified with H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell), and the Gysin boundary map delta: H^d_et(U_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) of the target is precisely this connecting homomorphism partial. Hence ker(delta) = ker[ H^d_et(U_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) ] under the identification.

Therefore the map P^d -> H^d_et(U_k, Q_ell) induced by inclusion into H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) followed by restriction to U, i.e. j^*|_{P^d}, is an isomorphism of F-modules onto ker(delta), where F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. This is exactly the desired conclusion."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of a F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then the restriction of the quotient map H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)/L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) to P^d is an isomorphism of F-modules.
proof: Set Q=q^m, a prime power. Let V=H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), let W=L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let P=P^d=ker(L:V->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). The cohomology groups are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces (standard finiteness for smooth projective varieties over finite fields). The argument below uses the repaired order: first W intersection P=0, then the dimension formula, and scalar compatibility F(Ly)=Q L(Fy) rather than F(xi)=xi. Pairing. By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, the trace pairing H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell(-d) is perfect for every r with 0<=r<=2d. Under the chosen identification of Tate twists with Q_ell, in particular of Q_ell(-d) with Q_ell, this gives a nondegenerate Q_ell-bilinear form beta:V x V -> Q_ell on V, and also a perfect Q_ell-valued pairing H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell. We continue to write tr for the resulting Q_ell-valued trace pairing. Orthogonality. Put W^perp={x in V: beta(x,w)=0 for every w in W}. We claim P=W^perp. If x in P, then Lx=0. For y in H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell), beta(x,Ly)=tr(x cup L y)=tr((x cup y) cup xi)=tr((xi cup x) cup y)=tr(Lx cup y)=0, using graded commutativity and the fact that xi has degree 2, so xi cup x=(-1)^{2d} x cup xi=x cup xi. Thus P subset W^perp. Conversely, if x in W^perp, then for every y in H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell), 0=beta(x,Ly)=tr(x cup L y)=tr(Lx cup y). By perfectness of the pairing H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell), this implies Lx=0, so x in P. Hence P=W^perp. Trivial intersection. If z in W intersection P, write z=L y with y in H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since z in P, 0=Lz=L(Ly)=L^2 y. The hypothesis gives that L^2:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism (take n=d-2 in L^{d-n}). Therefore y=0 and z=0. Thus W intersection P=0. Sum. Let J:V->V^* be J(x)(w)=beta(x,w). Since beta is nondegenerate, J is an isomorphism. Let W^0={lambda in V^*: lambda|_W=0}. Then W^perp=J^{-1}(W^0), so dim W^perp=dim W^0. The restriction map V^*->W^* is surjective (linear functionals on W extend to V), so dim W^0=dim V-dim W. Therefore dim P=dim W^perp=dim V-dim W, i.e. dim W+dim P=dim V. Since W intersection P=0, dim(W+P)=dim W+dim P-dim(W intersection P)=dim V, hence W+P=V. Thus V=W direct sum P as vector spaces, and the quotient map q:V->V/W restricts to a Q_ell-linear isomorphism q|_P:P->V/W. Frobenius stability. Let F be the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius, Q=q^m. The cited lemmas apply because ell != p, X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d, and the divisor is very ample and defined over F_Q. By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of each cohomology group. Apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable to the base prime power Q=q^m (so its q is Q and its Frobenius is our F). It gives F composed with L = Q L composed with F on every cohomology group. In particular, for y in H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell), F(Ly)=Q L(Fy) in W; hence F(W) subset W, and because F is invertible, F(W)=W. For P, apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/305609, whose hypotheses are exactly the present ones; it gives F(P^d)=P^d. F-module structure. Since F(W) subset W, F induces an automorphism F_{V/W} of V/W, and q is F-equivariant: q(Fv)=F_{V/W}(q(v)) for every v in V. For p in P, q(Fp)=F_{V/W}(q(p)). Therefore q|_P:P->V/W is a bijective F-linear map, hence an isomorphism of F-modules. This proves the lemma.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Let tr_X be the Poincare duality trace, and put beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(x cup L^{d-r}y) for x,y in P^r. Then for every integer r with 0<=r<=d, beta_r is a nondegenerate bilinear form on P^r.
proof:
Fix an integer r with 0 <= r <= d. Put A = P^r and B = L^{d-r} P^r. Thus A is a Q_ell-subspace of H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) and B is a Q_ell-subspace of H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell). Define phi_r: A -> B by phi_r(v) = L^{d-r} v. By the hard Lefschetz hypothesis applied with n = r, the map L^{d-r}: H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Therefore its restriction to A is injective. Its image is, by definition of B, exactly B. Hence phi_r is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces.

Apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/4b7666 with j = 0. The required inequality 0 <= 2j <= r becomes 0 <= 0 <= r, which is true for every r with 0 <= r <= d. The lemma gives that the Q_ell-bilinear form gamma_r(x,b) = tr_X(x cup b) on A x B is nondegenerate. The degrees are compatible: x has degree r, b has degree 2d-r, so x cup b lies in H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell), where tr_X is the Poincare duality trace.

For u,v in A, we have beta_r(u,v) = tr_X(u cup L^{d-r} v) = gamma_r(u, phi_r(v)).

Now take the left radical of beta_r. If u in A satisfies beta_r(u,v)=0 for every v in A, then gamma_r(u, phi_r(v))=0 for every v in A. Since phi_r(A)=B, this says gamma_r(u,b)=0 for every b in B. Nondegeneracy of gamma_r in the first variable forces u=0.

Now take the right radical of beta_r. If v in A satisfies beta_r(u,v)=0 for every u in A, then gamma_r(u, phi_r(v))=0 for every u in A. Nondegeneracy of gamma_r in the second variable forces phi_r(v)=0. Since phi_r is injective, v=0.

Thus both radicals of beta_r are zero, so beta_r is a nondegenerate bilinear form on P^r. The argument used only the hard Lefschetz hypothesis and the cited lemma, and it is uniform in r. In particular it also covers r=0 without any special case and without claiming that P^0 is zero. This removes the erroneous final sentence from the earlier attempt.

statement: Let s=p^a be a prime power, let Y be a smooth projective variety over F_s, let F:Y->Y be the s-power Frobenius endomorphism of Y over F_s, and let Z be the fiber product of the graph of F with the diagonal in Y x_{F_s} Y. Then Z is a finite etale F_s-scheme.
proof: Let k = F_s. The field k is perfect, so c^s = c for every c in k. Let Gamma_F be the graph of F in Y x_k Y and Delta the diagonal. Since Y is a variety over k, it is separated; hence Delta and Gamma_F are closed immersions into Y x_k Y. The projection Z = Gamma_F x_{Y x_k Y} Delta -> Delta identifies Z with the fixed point subscheme of F in Y, and the map Z -> Y is a closed immersion. Choose a closed immersion i: Y -> P^n_k. Let F_P be the s-power Frobenius of P^n_k. On homogeneous coordinates X_0,...,X_n it is [X_0:...:X_n] -> [X_0^s:...:X_n^s]. By functoriality, F_P i = i F. For r = 0,...,n put D_r = D_+(X_r) and U_r = Y intersection D_r. The U_r are affine open subschemes of Y and cover Y. Since Y is closed in P^n_k, U_r is a closed subscheme of D_r. Under the standard identification D_r is isomorphic to A^n_k with coordinates y_1,...,y_n (where y_j = X_j/X_r for j != r), the restriction F_P|_{D_r} is induced by y_j -> y_j^s. If X_r is nonzero, then X_r^s is nonzero, so F_P(D_r) is contained in D_r; hence F(U_r) is contained in U_r. Let V_r be the fixed point scheme of F_P on D_r. Write B_r = k[y_1,...,y_n]. The graph of F_P in D_r x D_r is defined by the equations 1 tensor y_j - y_j^s tensor 1, and the diagonal is defined by 1 tensor y_j - y_j tensor 1. Their fiber product is therefore the closed subscheme of D_r defined by y_j^s - y_j. Thus V_r = Spec B_r/K_r, where K_r is the ideal generated by y_j^s - y_j. The polynomial T^s - T has derivative -1 and splits as a product of linear factors over k, because its roots are exactly the s elements of k. Hence k[T]/(T^s-T) is isomorphic to k^s, and is finite etale over k. Consequently B_r/K_r is isomorphic to k^{s^n}, and is finite etale over k. Now put Z_r = Z x_Y U_r. Since U_r is stable under F, Z_r is the fixed point scheme of the restricted morphism F_r: U_r -> U_r. Write U_r = Spec A_r, where A_r = B_r/I_r. The fact that F(U_r) is contained in U_r says that I_r is stable under the map y_j -> y_j^s, so F_r is induced by A_r -> A_r, a -> a^s. The fixed point scheme of F_r is Spec A_r/J_r, where J_r is the ideal generated by a^s - a. Passing to B_r, A_r/J_r is isomorphic to B_r/(I_r + J_B), where J_B is the ideal generated by b^s - b for b in B_r. The ideal J_B equals K_r. Indeed, K_r is contained in it because y_j^s - y_j is one of the elements b^s - b. Conversely, in B_r/K_r every y_j satisfies y_j^s = y_j, so for every b in B_r we have b^s = b; hence b^s - b lies in K_r. Therefore A_r/J_r is isomorphic to B_r/(I_r + K_r), which is the coordinate ring of the closed subscheme U_r intersection V_r of V_r. Thus Z_r = U_r intersection V_r. Since U_r intersection V_r is a closed subscheme of V_r and V_r is isomorphic to Spec k^{s^n}, it is finite etale over k. Explicitly, ideals in k^{s^n} are products of some of the factors, so a quotient is k^m for some m with 0 <= m <= s^n, and Spec k^m is finite etale over k. The Z_r are open in Z and cover Z. Each Z_r -> Spec k is etale. The property of being etale over a fixed base is local on the source (it is defined by flatness, unramifiedness, and finite presentation, all local on the source), so Z -> Spec k is etale. It remains to show that Z is finite over k. The cover by the Z_r is finite. Each Z_r is finite over k, hence is an Artinian scheme; in particular its underlying topological space is finite and every point is open. Therefore every point of Z is open in Z, and Z has only finitely many points. For a point x in Z choose r with x in Z_r. The singleton {x} is an open subscheme of Z. It is also an open-and-closed subscheme of Z_r; if Z_r = Spec A_r with A_r a finite k-algebra, then {x} = Spec(e A_r) for an idempotent e in A_r, and is finite over k. Thus Z is a finite disjoint union of finite k-schemes, hence is finite over k. Combining the two properties, Z is a finite etale k-scheme.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1 and s>=m be integers with s a multiple of m, put k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective variety over F_{q^m}. Suppose X_{F_{q^s}} is a disjoint union X_1, ..., X_r of smooth projective geometrically connected varieties over F_{q^s}. If for every j=1,...,r and every integer i>=0, the q^s-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et((X_j)_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then for every integer i>=0, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof:
Let n := s/m. Since s is a multiple of m and s >= m, n is an integer with n >= 1. Put k = overline(F_q). Let sigma_m: k -> k be the automorphism x -> x^{q^m} and let sigma_s: k -> k be the automorphism x -> x^{q^s}. Since (q^m)^n = q^{mn} = q^s, we have sigma_s = sigma_m^n, i.e. sigma_m^n(x) = x^{q^s} for all x in k.

Fix an integer i >= 0 and put V := H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell). Let F: V -> V denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, i.e. F = (id_X x sigma_m)^*. We prove that F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).

Step 1 (F is invertible). Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a with the prime power q^m, the scheme X over F_{q^m}, k = overline(F_q), the field automorphism sigma_m, the integer i, and the prime ell != p. It says that the pullback F_ar := (id_X x sigma_m)^* is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell), with inverse F_geo := (id_X x sigma_m^{-1})^*. Hence F is an invertible Q_ell-linear operator on V.

Step 2 (V is finite-dimensional over Q_ell). Since X is projective over F_{q^m}, X is proper over F_{q^m}. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob with the prime power q^m, the proper variety X over F_{q^m}, k = overline(F_q) = overline(F_{q^m}), the prime ell, and K = Q_ell the constant sheaf on X_k, which the lemma equips with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism psi: F_X^* Q_ell -> Q_ell (F_X being the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism on X_k). The lemma concludes that the hypercohomology H^n(X_k, K) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell for every integer n. Taking K = Q_ell gives that H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) = V is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. (Consequently each summand V_j constructed below, being a direct summand of V, is also finite-dimensional over Q_ell.)

Step 3 (decomposition of V into the components). Put X' := X_{F_{q^s}} = X x_{Spec F_{q^m}} Spec F_{q^s}. By hypothesis X' = disjoint union over j=1..r of X_j, each X_j a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_{q^s}. In the disjoint union, each X_j is a closed subscheme of X', and its complement is the union of the other closed subschemes X_l (l != j), hence closed; therefore each X_j is also open, i.e. an open-and-closed subscheme of X'. Open-and-closed is preserved under base change, so each (X_j)_k := X_j x_{Spec F_{q^s}} Spec k is an open-and-closed subscheme of X_k = X' x_{Spec F_{q^s}} Spec k, and X_k = disjoint union over j of (X_j)_k.

The scheme X_k is a separated scheme of finite type over k: X is a variety over F_{q^m}, hence of finite type over F_{q^m}, hence of finite type over F_{q^s}, hence of finite type over k; and X is projective over F_{q^m}, hence separated, and separatedness is preserved under base change. Now apply Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_cohom_open_closed_sum successively to the open-and-closed decomposition: first with U = X_k, V = (X_1)_k, W = (X_2)_(k) union ... union (X_r)_k (which is open-and-closed as a finite union of open-and-closed subschemes), then to W with V = (X_2)_k, W = (X_3)_k union ... union (X_r)_k, and so on, inducting on r. The lemma says at each step that the restriction homomorphisms identify H^b_et(U, Q_ell) with H^b_et(V, Q_ell) direct sum H^b_et(W, Q_ell). Hence for every b (in particular b = i) the restriction maps identify
  V = H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) with the direct sum over j=1..r of V_j,
where V_j := H^i_et((X_j)_k, Q_ell), and the projection of v in V onto its j-th component is res_j(v), where res_j: V -> V_j is the restriction map along the open-and-closed inclusion (X_j)_k -> X_k.

Step 4 (F^n is block-diagonal and its j-th block is the q^s Frobenius on (X_j)_k). First compute F^n. By contravariant functoriality of pullback in etale cohomology, for morphisms f, g: X_k -> X_k one has (g o f)^* = f^* o g^*. Taking f = g = id_X x sigma_m gives F^2 = (id_X x sigma_m^2)^*; by induction on n,
  F^n = ((id_X x sigma_m)^*)^n = (id_X x sigma_m^n)^* = (id_X x sigma_s)^*.

Next, since X_j is defined over F_{q^s} and sigma_s restricts to the identity on F_{q^s} (for x in F_{q^s} one has x^{q^s} = x), the morphism id_X x sigma_s: X_k -> X_k restricts to the open-and-closed subscheme (X_j)_k subset X_k to the morphism id_{X_j} x sigma_s: (X_j)_k -> (X_j)_k. Write Z := (X_j)_k and j_Z: Z -> X_k for the inclusion; then (id_X x sigma_s) o j_Z = j_Z o (id_{X_j} x sigma_s) as morphisms Z -> X_k. Applying the contravariant functor H^i_et(-, Q_ell), which sends a morphism h to the pullback h^* and satisfies (u o v)^* = v^* o u^*, to this equality of composites gives
  j_Z^* o (id_X x sigma_s)^* = (id_{X_j} x sigma_s)^* o j_Z^*.
That is, the square
  V --res_j--> V_j
  | F^n          | (id_{X_j} x sigma_s)^*
  v              v
  V --res_j--> V_j
commutes, where the left vertical arrow is F^n = (id_X x sigma_s)^* (as computed above) and the right vertical arrow is the pullback of the restricted morphism id_{X_j} x sigma_s. Therefore, for v in V with j-th component v_j := res_j(v) in V_j, the j-th component of F^n v is res_j(F^n v) = (id_{X_j} x sigma_s)^* v_j. In words: under the decomposition V = direct sum of V_j of Step 3, the operator F^n is block-diagonal, and its j-th block is (id_{X_j} x sigma_s)^*, which is precisely the q^s-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et((X_j)_k, Q_ell). By hypothesis, this operator is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for each j = 1, ..., r.

Step 5 (F^n is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell)). For each j, the block (id_{X_j} x sigma_s)^* = F^n|_{V_j} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), so there exists a basis B_j of V_j tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) consisting of eigenvectors of F^n|_{V_j} tensor 1. Since the tensor product over Q_ell commutes with finite direct sums,
  V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) = (direct sum of V_j) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) = direct sum of (V_j tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell)).
The union B_1 union ... union B_r is therefore a basis of V tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) consisting of eigenvectors of F^n tensor 1: because F^n is block-diagonal, a vector lying in the j-th summand is sent by F^n tensor 1 to a scalar multiple of itself, again in the j-th summand. Hence F^n is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), i.e. F^n is semisimple on V.

Step 6 (F is diagonalizable). Apply Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/896297 with K = Q_ell (a field of characteristic 0), V (finite-dimensional over Q_ell by Step 2), T = F (invertible by Step 1), and r = n >= 1. Its hypothesis T^r semisimple is exactly Step 5, since T^n = F^n is semisimple on V. The conclusion is that T = F is semisimple on V, i.e. diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of Q_ell, which is overline(Q_ell).

Since i >= 0 was arbitrary, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every integer i >= 0. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be a prime, let m>=1, put k=overline(F_q), let d>=0, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). If F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every integer r with 0<=r<=d, then F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every integer i>=0.
proof: First, by Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing, since X_k is a projective scheme of pure dimension d over the algebraically closed field k, H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)=0 for every i>2d. The zero vector space is trivially diagonalizable, so it is enough to treat 0<=i<=2d. The hypothesis already gives the result for 0<=i<=d. Now assume d>=1 and d<i<=2d, and put n=2d-i; then 0<=n<d. By Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_poincare_duality_smooth_projective_not_connected, applied with the prime power q^m in place of q, there is a Poincare duality trace map tr_X:H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell(-d) such that the pairing H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell(-d), (x,y)->tr_X(x cup y), is a perfect pairing of finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_271, again with the prime power q^m in place of q, to the same X and to the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F. It gives an isomorphism Psi:H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell)->Hom_{Q_ell}(H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell),Q_ell) such that Psi o F_i = q^{md} (F_n^{-1})^vee o Psi, where F_i and F_n are the restrictions of F to H^i and H^n, and (F_n^{-1})^vee is the dual automorphism on the Q_ell-linear dual of H^n. By the hypothesis, F_n is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Since H^n is finite-dimensional, Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_488 implies F_n^{-1} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Then eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_215 implies the dual automorphism (F_n^{-1})^vee is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Multiplication by the nonzero scalar q^{md} preserves diagonalizability, because an eigenbasis of an operator is also an eigenbasis of its nonzero scalar multiple. Hence q^{md}(F_n^{-1})^vee is diagonalizable. Since Psi is an isomorphism, F_i is similar to q^{md}(F_n^{-1})^vee; conjugating a diagonalizing basis by Psi^{-1} gives a diagonalizing basis for F_i, so F_i is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). This proves the desired statement for d<i<=2d. Combining this with the hypothesis for 0<=i<=d and the vanishing for i>2d proves the lemma for every integer i>=0.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let r be an integer, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let beta be a nondegenerate bilinear form with beta(y,x)=(-1)^r beta(x,y), let c in K^*, and let T in GL(V) satisfy beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y). Let U be the unipotent part of T. Then for every n>=1 and x,y in V, G_n(Ux,Uy)=G_n(x,y), where G_n(x,y)=beta(x,T^n y)+(-1)^r c^n beta(x,T^{-n}y).
proof:
Both lemmas are confirmed and apply directly. Now I can assemble the complete proof:

1. **Commutativity:** By `df0feb`, $U = P(T)$ for some polynomial $P \in K[t]$, so $U$ commutes with $T$, hence with $T^n$ and $T^{-n}$.
2. **Isometry property:** By `b33e4d` (applied with $F = T$), since $ eta$ is nondegenerate and $ eta(Tx,Ty) = c\, eta(x,y)$, the unipotent part $U$ satisfies $ eta(Ux, Uy) =  eta(x,y)$ for all $x, y$.
3. **Conclusion:** Then $G_n(Ux, Uy) =  eta(Ux, UT^n y) + (-1)^r c^n  eta(Ux, UT^{-n} y) =  eta(x, T^n y) + (-1)^r c^n  eta(x, T^{-n} y) = G_n(x,y)$.

Note that the symmetry condition $ eta(y,x) = (-1)^r  eta(x,y)$ is part of the hypothesis but is not actually needed for this particular conclusion — only nondegeneracy is used.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/071062",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/b33e4d", "Miner/16d24b0281973336/df0feb"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let beta:V x V -> K be a nondegenerate bilinear form with beta(y,x)=(-1)^r beta(x,y), let c in K^*, and let T in GL(V) satisfy beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y) for all x,y in V. Let U be the unipotent part of T in the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition T = S U = U S (with S semisimple and U unipotent). We must show that for every n>=1 and all x,y in V, G_n(Ux,Uy)=G_n(x,y), where G_n(x,y)=beta(x,T^n y)+(-1)^r c^n beta(x,T^{-n}y).

Step 1: U commutes with T. Since char K = 0, V is finite-dimensional, and T is invertible, the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/df0feb applies: there exists a polynomial P in K[t] such that U = P(T). Therefore U commutes with T, and consequently U commutes with every integral power of T, in particular with T^n and T^{-n} for every integer n. Thus T^n U = U T^n and T^{-n} U = U T^{-n} for all n>=1.

Step 2: U is an isometry of beta. The proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/b33e4d states: for a field K of characteristic 0, a finite-dimensional K-vector space V, a nondegenerate bilinear form beta, an operator F in GL(V), and c in K^* with beta(Fx,Fy)=c beta(x,y) for all x,y, the unipotent part U of F in the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition satisfies beta(Ux,Uy)=beta(x,y) for all x,y in V. All hypotheses of that lemma are satisfied here with F=T (nondegeneracy of beta, T in GL(V), and beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y) are exactly our assumptions; the symmetry condition beta(y,x)=(-1)^r beta(x,y) is not needed for this lemma). Hence beta(Ux,Uy)=beta(x,y) for all x,y in V. In particular, for every z in V, beta(Ux,U z)=beta(x,z) for all x in V.

Step 3: Computation of G_n(Ux,Uy). Fix an integer n>=1 and vectors x,y in V. By the definition of G_n:
G_n(Ux,Uy) = beta(Ux, T^n (Uy)) + (-1)^r c^n beta(Ux, T^{-n} (Uy)).
Using Step 1 (T^n U = U T^n and T^{-n} U = U T^{-n}), this becomes
G_n(Ux,Uy) = beta(Ux, U(T^n y)) + (-1)^r c^n beta(Ux, U(T^{-n} y)).
Now apply Step 2 with z = T^n y in the first term and z = T^{-n} y in the second term:
beta(Ux, U(T^n y)) = beta(x, T^n y) and beta(Ux, U(T^{-n} y)) = beta(x, T^{-n} y).
Substituting these identities gives
G_n(Ux,Uy) = beta(x, T^n y) + (-1)^r c^n beta(x, T^{-n} y) = G_n(x,y),
which is exactly the desired identity.

This completes the proof for every n>=1 and all x,y in V."
