tr(F(z)) = q^{md} * tr(z) in Q_ell(-d).
Under the fixed identification Q_ell(-d) = Q_ell, this reads
tr_X(F(z)) = q^{md} * tr_X(z) in Q_ell
for every z in H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Step 3 (F is a ring homomorphism). The arithmetic Frobenius F: X_k -> X_k is a morphism of schemes. By the functoriality of the cup product in etale cohomology, for any x in H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) and y in H^j_et(X_k, Q_ell),
F(x cup y) = F(x) cup F(y) in H^{i+j}_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Step 4 (Main computation). Let x, y in P^r. By hypothesis, F(P^r) is contained in P^r, so Fx, Fy in P^r subset H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell).

We compute beta_r(Fx, Fy) step by step.

First, since 0 <= r <= d, we have d - r >= 0, so L^{d-r} is a well-defined cup-product map H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, Q_ell). By Step 1 with s = d - r,
L^{d-r}(Fy) = q^{-m(d-r)} F(L^{d-r}(y)).

Therefore,
beta_r(Fx, Fy) = tr_X(Fx cup L^{d-r}(Fy))
= tr_X(Fx cup q^{-m(d-r)} F(L^{d-r}(y)))
= q^{-m(d-r)} tr_X(Fx cup F(L^{d-r}(y))).

By Step 3, Fx cup F(L^{d-r}(y)) = F(x cup L^{d-r}(y)). Here x in H^r and L^{d-r}(y) in H^{2d-r}, so x cup L^{d-r}(y) in H^{2d}, and F(x cup L^{d-r}(y)) in H^{2d}. Thus,
beta_r(Fx, Fy) = q^{-m(d-r)} tr_X(F(x cup L^{d-r}(y))).

By Step 2,
tr_X(F(x cup L^{d-r}(y))) = q^{md} tr_X(x cup L^{d-r}(y)).

Combining,
beta_r(Fx, Fy) = q^{-m(d-r)} * q^{md} * tr_X(x cup L^{d-r}(y))
= q^{-m(d-r) + md} * beta_r(x, y)
= q^{m(d - d + r)} * beta_r(x, y)
= q^{mr} * beta_r(x, y).

This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. With Tate twists identified with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and for 0<=j<=floor(d/2) put W_j=L^j P^{d-2j}. Let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then the restriction of beta to W_j x W_j is nondegenerate for every j.
proof: Fix an integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(d/2). Then 0 <= 2j <= d. Let tr_X be the Poincare duality trace H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell after the chosen identification of Tate twists with Q_ell. With this identification, the Poincare duality pairing beta on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the bilinear form (x,y) -> tr_X(x cup y). Apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/4b7666 with r = d. Its hypotheses are exactly those in the present statement: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, xi is the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L is cup product with xi, and L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer n with 0 <= n <= d. The lemma says that, because 0 <= 2j <= d, the bilinear form (x,y) -> tr_X(x cup y) on L^j P^{d-2j} x L^{d-d+j} P^{d-2j} is nondegenerate. But L^{d-d+j} P^{d-2j} = L^j P^{d-2j} = W_j. Hence the restriction of beta to W_j x W_j is nondegenerate. The argument includes the endpoint j=0, where L^0 is the identity, and also the case in which W_j is zero, where nondegeneracy is vacuous and the cited lemma still applies. Since j was arbitrary, the restriction of beta to W_j x W_j is nondegenerate for every j.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, let k be an algebraic closure of F_q, d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell), let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor in H^2, let L be cup product with xi, let 0<=r<=d and 0<=j<=d-r, and put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose H^r and H^{r+2j} are finite-dimensional over Q_ell, F(P^r) is contained in P^r, L^j:P^r->L^jP^r is an isomorphism, F L^j=q^{mj}L^jF on P^r, and there are an embedding sigma of the algebraic closure of Q_ell into C and a positive definite Hermitian h on H^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma}C with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y) for all x,y. Then there is a positive definite Hermitian h' on L^jP^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma}C with h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(r+2j)}h'(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
We prove the stated lemma, using the explicit finiteness hypothesis. Put K=Q_ell. The finiteness of H^r and H^{r+2j} is assumed; consequently P^r and L^jP^r are finite-dimensional, which is the point needed for the transfer lemma. Since q^m=p^{am} is a prime power, regard X as a scheme over F_{q^m}. By the lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, applied to the base field F_{q^m} and to the degrees i=r and i=r+2j, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^r and of H^{r+2j}; in particular, because these groups are finite-dimensional over Q_ell, F is an invertible Q_ell-linear operator on each of them.

P^r is a Q_ell-subspace of H^r, so P^r is finite-dimensional. Also L^jP^r is a Q_ell-subspace of H^{r+2j}, so L^jP^r is finite-dimensional.

Define T_V=F|_{P^r}. The hypothesis F(P^r) subset P^r makes T_V a well-defined endomorphism of P^r. It is injective because F on H^r is injective. Since P^r is finite-dimensional, an injective endomorphism is surjective; hence T_V is in GL_K(P^r).

Define T_W=F|_{L^jP^r}. For y=L^jx with x in P^r, the relation F L^j = q^{mj} L^j F on P^r gives Fy = q^{mj} L^j(Fx), and Fx is in P^r, so Fy is in L^jP^r. Thus T_W is a well-defined endomorphism of L^jP^r. It is injective because F on H^{r+2j} is injective. Since L^jP^r is finite-dimensional, T_W is surjective; hence T_W is in GL_K(L^jP^r).

Let phi be the restriction L^j|_{P^r}:P^r -> L^jP^r. By hypothesis phi is a K-linear isomorphism. Put c=q^{mj}, which lies in K^*. For every x in P^r, T_W(phi x)=F(L^jx)=q^{mj}L^j(Fx)=c phi(T_Vx), so T_W phi = c phi T_V.

Let h_V be the restriction of the given positive definite Hermitian form h to P^r tensor_{K,sigma} C. The inclusion P^r -> H^r is injective, so its base change to C is injective; hence a nonzero tensor in P^r tensor C is nonzero in H^r tensor C. Therefore h_V is positive definite: if z is nonzero in P^r tensor C, then h_V(z,z)=h(z,z)>0. It is Hermitian because it is the restriction of a Hermitian form. For z,w in P^r tensor C, h_V((T_V tensor id)z,(T_V tensor id)w)=h((F tensor id)z,(F tensor id)w)=q^{mr}h(z,w)=q^{mr}h_V(z,w). Put lambda=q^{mr}, which is a positive real number.

Apply the transfer lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/54dead with the field K, the restriction of sigma to K, V=P^r, W=L^jP^r, T_V, T_W, phi, c, and lambda. It gives a positive definite Hermitian form h_W on W tensor_{K,sigma} C such that h_W((T_W tensor id)u,(T_W tensor id)v)=|sigma(c)|^2 lambda h_W(u,v) for all u,v in W tensor C.

Finally, c=q^{mj} is a positive rational number, hence belongs to the prime field Q inside K. Therefore sigma(c)=q^{mj}, and |sigma(c)|^2 lambda = q^{2mj} q^{mr} = q^{m(r+2j)}. Setting h'=h_W gives the required positive definite Hermitian form on L^jP^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C with the stated transformation law. The argument also covers the edge cases j=0 and r=0, since then L^0 is the identity, c=1, and the same finite-dimensional linear algebra applies.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U be the open complement of Y in X, let i:Y->X and j:U->X be the inclusions, fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d and i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)) and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Then j^*:P^d->H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) is an injective morphism of F-modules.
proof: Let F_n denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^n_et(X_k,Q_l) for each n, and let F_U denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d_et(U_k,Q_l). Write F_X=F_d. We first prove that P^d is stable under F_X. View X as a variety over the finite field F_{q^m}. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, applied with q replaced by q^m, F_X is the pullback by (id_X,sigma), where sigma(t)=t^{q^m}; pullback in etale cohomology is a ring automorphism, so for a in H^r and b in H^s one has F_{r+s}(a cup b)=F_r(a) cup F_s(b). The divisor Y is an effective codimension-one cycle defined over F_{q^m}. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_78, applied with q replaced by q^m and with j=1, and using the fixed identification Q_l(1)=Q_l, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acts on the untwisted cycle class xi by the scalar q^m: F_2(xi)=q^m xi. Therefore, for any r and any y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_l), F_{r+2}(L y)=F_{r+2}(y cup xi)=F_r(y) cup F_2(xi)=q^m F_r(y) cup xi=q^m L(F_r y). In particular, if x in P^d, then L x=0, hence 0=F_{d+2}(L x)=q^m L(F_d x), so L(F_d x)=0. Thus F_d(P^d) is contained in P^d. Also, if x in P^d and z=F_d^{-1}(x), then 0=F_{d+2}(L z)=q^m L(F_d z)=q^m L x=0, and since F_{d+2} is invertible by lemma_6a, L z=0; hence F_d^{-1}(P^d) is contained in P^d. Thus P^d is a Frobenius-stable Q_l-subspace of H^d_et(X_k,Q_l), i.e. a Q_l[F]-submodule. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/9e70fa, the segment H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_l)(-1) -> H^d_et(X_k,Q_l) -> H^d_et(U_k,Q_l) with maps i_! and j^* is exact as a sequence of F-modules. In particular j^* is a morphism of F-modules, i.e. j^* F_X = F_U j^*. Since P^d is F_X-stable, the restriction j^*:P^d -> H^d_et(U_k,Q_l) is a morphism of F-modules. It remains to prove injectivity. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/88b43d, because i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_l)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_l) is an isomorphism, the kernel of j^*:H^d_et(X_k,Q_l)->H^d_et(U_k,Q_l) is L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_l). Let x in P^d with j^* x=0. Then x lies in L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_l), so x=L y for some y in H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_l). Since x in P^d, L x=0. Hence 0=L(L y)=L^2 y. Since d>=2, n=d-2 is allowed in the hard Lefschetz hypothesis, and L^{d-(d-2)}=L^2:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_l)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_l) is an isomorphism. Therefore y=0, and then x=0. Thus the kernel of the restricted map j^*:P^d->H^d_et(U_k,Q_l) is zero. We have shown that this map is an F-module morphism and is injective.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected. Let i:Y->X. Write H^n(Z)=H^n_et(Z_k,Q_ell) for Z=X,Y. With Tate twists identified with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and let i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)(-1)->H^d(X) be the Gysin map. If i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism, then i_! is an isomorphism of F-modules onto L H^{d-2}(X) if and only if L:H^{d-2}(X)->H^d(X) is injective, where F denotes the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on the source and on the target.
proof:
Let \varphi: H^{d-2}(Y) \to H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) denote the canonical \mathbb{Q}_\ell-linear isomorphism arising from the identification \mathbb{Q}_\ell(-1) \cong \mathbb{Q}_\ell. Let F_Y denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-2}(Y)(-1), and let F_X denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d(X). These are precisely the Frobenius operators referred to in the statement as "F on the source" and "F on the target," respectively.

Step 1: Image equality. By the projection formula (lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/1f2e4b), the composition
H^{d-2}(X) \xrightarrow{i^*} H^{d-2}(Y) \xrightarrow{\varphi} H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) \xrightarrow{i_!} H^d(X)
equals L, i.e.\ i_! \circ \varphi \circ i^* = L.
Since i^*: H^{d-2}(X) \to H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism (hypothesis) and \varphi is an isomorphism, the composite \psi := \varphi \circ i^*: H^{d-2}(X) \to H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) is an isomorphism.
From i_! \circ \psi = L we obtain im(L) = im(i_! \circ \psi) \subseteq im(i_!).
For the reverse inclusion, take any y \in H^{d-2}(Y)(-1). Since \psi is surjective, there exists x \in H^{d-2}(X) with \psi(x) = y. Then i_!(y) = i_!(\psi(x)) = L(x) \in L \cdot H^{d-2}(X) = im(L). Hence im(i_!) \subseteq im(L).
Combining both inclusions: im(i_!) = im(L) = L \cdot H^{d-2}(X).

Step 2: F-linearity of i_! and F_X-stability of L \cdot H^{d-2}(X). Let U = X \setminus Y and let j: U \to X be the inclusion. By lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/9e70fa, the segment
H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) \xrightarrow{i_!} H^d(X) \xrightarrow{j^*} H^d(U)
is exact as a sequence of F-modules, where F_Y, F_X, F_U are the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-2}(Y)(-1), H^d(X), H^d(U) respectively. Concretely, this means:
(i) i_! is a map of F-modules: i_! \circ F_Y = F_X \circ i_!.
(ii) j^* is a map of F-modules: j^* \circ F_X = F_U \circ j^*.
(iii) im(i_!) = ker(j^*).
From (ii), the kernel of j^* is F_X-stable: if v \in ker(j^*), then j^*(F_X v) = F_U \, j^*(v) = F_U(0) = 0, so F_X v \in ker(j^*). By (iii), F_X(im(i_!)) = F_X(ker(j^*)) \subseteq ker(j^*) = im(i_!).
By Step 1, im(i_!) = L \cdot H^{d-2}(X), so F_X(L \cdot H^{d-2}(X)) \subseteq L \cdot H^{d-2}(X). Thus L \cdot H^{d-2}(X) is an F_X-submodule of H^d(X), and i_!: H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) \to L \cdot H^{d-2}(X) is a map of F-modules (by (i) and the fact that i_! lands in L \cdot H^{d-2}(X) by Step 1).

Step 3: The equivalence via rank-nullity. All cohomology groups involved are finite-dimensional over \mathbb{Q}_\ell (standard finiteness for smooth projective varieties over finite fields).
Dimension of the source: H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) = H^{d-2}(Y) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell} \mathbb{Q}_\ell(-1), and \mathbb{Q}_\ell(-1) is one-dimensional over \mathbb{Q}_\ell, so dim H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) = dim H^{d-2}(Y). Since i^* is an isomorphism, dim H^{d-2}(Y) = dim H^{d-2}(X). Therefore dim H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) = dim H^{d-2}(X).
Dimension of the image: by Step 1, im(i_!) = L \cdot H^{d-2}(X), so dim(im(i_!)) = dim(L \cdot H^{d-2}(X)) = dim H^{d-2}(X) - dim ker(L), by the rank-nullity theorem applied to L: H^{d-2}(X) \to H^d(X).
Now we chain equivalences:
(a) i_! is an isomorphism of F-modules onto L \cdot H^{d-2}(X) if and only if i_! is bijective. Indeed, by Steps 1 and 2, i_! is already F-linear, its image is exactly L \cdot H^{d-2}(X), and F_X preserves L \cdot H^{d-2}(X); a bijective F-linear map between F-modules has an F-linear inverse: if i_!(v) = w, then i_!(F_Y v) = F_X \, i_!(v) = F_X w, so (i_!)^{-1}(F_X w) = F_Y (i_!)^{-1}(w).
(b) i_! is bijective if and only if dim ker(i_!) = 0, i.e.\ if and only if dim H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) = dim im(i_!), by the rank-nullity theorem applied to i_!.
(c) dim H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) = dim im(i_!) if and only if dim H^{d-2}(X) = dim H^{d-2}(X) - dim ker(L), i.e.\ if and only if dim ker(L) = 0.
(d) dim ker(L) = 0 if and only if L is injective.
Chaining (a), (b), (c), (d): i_! is an isomorphism of F-modules onto L \cdot H^{d-2}(X) if and only if L: H^{d-2}(X) \to H^d(X) is injective. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let S be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and put P^2=ker(L:H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell)->H^4_et(S_k,Q_ell)). Let A be the Q_ell-span in H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell) of the cycle classes of all Cartier divisors on S_k. If A=H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell), then the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on P^2.
proof: Let F denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^2_et(S_k,Q_l). Under the stated identification of Q_l(1) with Q_l, xi is an element of H^2_et(S_k,Q_l). We first prove that F(P^2) is contained in P^2. Since overline(F_q) is also an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}, apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable with the prime power q^m in place of q, to the smooth projective surface S over F_{q^m}, the F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor with class xi, and the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Since ell != p and S has pure dimension 2, the hypotheses are satisfied. In the surface case the lemma gives F L = q^m L F on H^2_et(S_k,Q_l). If x in P^2, then Lx=0, so 0 = F(Lx) = q^m L(Fx). Because q^m is nonzero in Q_l, L(Fx)=0, hence Fx in P^2. Thus F(P^2) subset P^2. Now apply Miner/16d24b0281973336/4ac54e. Its hypotheses are the surface S, the identified Tate twist, xi, L, P^2, A, and the just-proved inclusion F(P^2) subset P^2. Fix an embedding sigma:Qbar_l -> C. The lemma gives a positive definite Hermitian form h on (A cap P^2) tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C such that h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{2m}h(x,y) for all x,y. Since A=H^2_et(S_k,Q_l), we have A cap P^2=P^2, so h is a positive definite Hermitian form on V_sigma=P^2 tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C with the same identity. The etale cohomology group H^2_et(S_k,Q_l) is finite-dimensional over Q_l by the standard finiteness theorem for smooth projective varieties over finite fields, hence P^2 and V_sigma are finite-dimensional; if P^2=0 the conclusion is trivial, and the argument below also covers this case. Define U=(1/q^m)(F tensor id) on V_sigma. Then h(Ux,Uy)=(1/q^{2m})h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=h(x,y) for all x,y, so U is unitary. By the spectral theorem for unitary operators on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, U is diagonalizable over C, and therefore F tensor id=q^m U is diagonalizable over C. It remains to descend from C to Qbar_l. The operator T=F tensor id is defined over sigma(Q_l). Since V_sigma is finite-dimensional and T is diagonalizable over C, it has a finite set Lambda of eigenvalues in C. Each lambda is a root of the characteristic polynomial of T, whose coefficients lie in sigma(Q_l); hence lambda is algebraic over sigma(Q_l) and lies in sigma(Qbar_l), the algebraic closure of sigma(Q_l) in C. The product over lambda in Lambda of (t-lambda) is therefore in sigma(Qbar_l)[t] and annihilates T; the minimal polynomial of T over sigma(Qbar_l) divides it and so splits into distinct linear factors over sigma(Qbar_l). Pulling back by the inverse of sigma, the minimal polynomial of F over Qbar_l splits into distinct linear factors. For a finite-dimensional vector space over Q_l, an endomorphism is diagonalizable over Qbar_l if and only if its minimal polynomial over Qbar_l splits into distinct linear factors; indeed the squarefree factorization gives polynomial projections onto the eigenspaces. Therefore F is diagonalizable over Qbar_l on P^2.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U be the open complement of Y in X, let i:Y->X and j:U->X be the inclusions, fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d and i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) and on L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), then F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof: Let H^n denote H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell). Put W=L H^{d-2} and P^d=ker(L:H^d->H^{d+2}). The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F is Q_ell-linear on each H^n. Since Y is defined over F_{q^m}, its cycle class is fixed by F in H^2(X_k,Q_ell(1)); under the fixed identification Q_ell(1)=Q_ell the coefficient Frobenius contributes the factor q^m, so F(xi)=q^m xi. Hence for every x, F(Lx)=F(x cup xi)=F(x) cup F(xi)=q^m L(Fx). Therefore P^d is F-stable: if Lx=0 then 0=F(Lx)=q^m L(Fx). Also W is F-stable: if w=Ly then F(w)=q^m L(Fy) belongs to W. Step 1: F on P^d is diagonalizable. By lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/987402, j^*:P^d->H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) is an injective morphism of F-modules. Thus j^*(P^d) is an F-stable subspace of H^d(U). If a Q_ell-linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional Q_ell-space is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), its restriction to any invariant subspace is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell): after scalar extension, the projections onto the eigenspaces are polynomials in the endomorphism, so they preserve the invariant subspace. Since j^* identifies P^d with j^*(P^d) as F-modules, F is diagonalizable on P^d. Step 2: H^d is the direct sum of P^d and W. Because Y is ample, O_X(Y) is an ample line bundle. By the standard characterization of ample line bundles, some positive tensor power is very ample; choose N>=1 such that O_X(NY) is very ample. Since O_X(NY) is defined over F_{q^m} and very ample, its complete linear system over F_{q^m} embeds X in projective space; choosing an F_{q^m}-rational hyperplane gives an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor D linearly equivalent to N Y. Let xi_D be its cycle class. Then xi_D=N xi. Put L_D=cup xi_D=N L. Since N is nonzero in Q_ell, L_D^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, and for every r the kernel of L_D^r and the image of L_D^r are the same as those of L^r. For 0<=r<=d define P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}); this is also the kernel of L_D^{d-r+1}. Apply lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/6a1acf to the very ample divisor D and the operator L_D. It gives W=L_D H^{d-2} as the direct sum of the subspaces W_j=L_D^j P^{d-2j} for j=1,...,floor(d/2). Because L_D=N L, each W_j is the same subspace as L^j P^{d-2j}, and P^{d-2j}=ker(L^{2j+1}:H^{d-2j}->H^{d+2j+2}). Apply lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103 to D and L_D. It says that for each j, the restriction of the Poincare duality pairing beta(x,y)=tr_X(x cup y) on H^d to W_j x W_j is nondegenerate. We now prove W_j is orthogonal to W_k whenever j is not equal to k. Let x in W_j and y in W_k. Write x=N^j p cup xi^j with p in P^{d-2j}, and y=N^k q cup xi^k with q in P^{d-2k}. Powers of xi have even degree, so beta(x,y)=N^{j+k} tr_X(p cup q cup xi^{j+k}). If j<k, then p cup xi^{2j+1}=0 and j+k>=2j+1; hence p cup q cup xi^{j+k}=(p cup xi^{2j+1}) cup q cup xi^{j+k-(2j+1)}=0. If j>k, then q cup xi^{2k+1}=0 and j+k>=2k+1; hence p cup q cup xi^{j+k}=p cup (q cup xi^{2k+1}) cup xi^{j+k-(2k+1)}=0. Thus beta(x,y)=0 for all x in W_j and y in W_k with j not equal to k. It follows that beta restricted to W x W is nondegenerate. Indeed, if x in W satisfies beta(x,y)=0 for all y in W, write x=sum_j x_j with x_j in W_j. For fixed k and y in W_k, orthogonality gives beta(x,y)=beta(x_k,y). Since beta|_{W_k x W_k} is nondegenerate, x_k=0 for every k, so x=0. Now apply lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/0af376 to D and L_D. It says that x in P^d if and only if beta(x,L_D y)=0 for every y in H^{d-2}. Since L_D y=N L y and N is nonzero, this is equivalent to beta(x,L y)=0 for every y in H^{d-2}, i.e. x belongs to W^perp={x in H^d: beta(x,w)=0 for all w in W}. Thus P^d=W^perp. The Poincare duality pairing beta is nondegenerate on the finite-dimensional space H^d. Since beta|_{W x W} is nondegenerate, W intersects W^perp trivially: if x in W and beta(x,w)=0 for all w in W, then x=0 by the previous paragraph. Also for a nondegenerate bilinear form on a finite-dimensional vector space, dim W^perp=dim H^d-dim W, because the map H^d to (H^d)^* given by x -> (y -> beta(x,y)) is an isomorphism and W^perp is the annihilator of W. Hence dim(W+W^perp)=dim W+dim W^perp=dim H^d, so W+W^perp=H^d. Therefore H^d=W direct sum W^perp=W direct sum P^d. Step 3: Conclusion. Both P^d and W are F-stable by the relation F L=q^m L F. We have shown F is diagonalizable on P^d, and by hypothesis F is diagonalizable on W. If a finite-dimensional vector space is a direct sum of two F-stable subspaces on which F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then F is diagonalizable on the whole space: after scalar extension to overline(Q_ell), the eigenspace decompositions of the two summands combine to an eigenspace decomposition of the direct sum. Therefore F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). This proves the lemma.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), let d>=2 be even, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)) and beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y). Then the restriction of beta_r to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate.
proof:
Let H^n = H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) for n >= 0, and let tr_X: H^{2d} -> Q_ell be the Poincare duality trace. Since X is geometrically connected, it is of pure dimension d, so the hard Lefschetz hypothesis L^{d-n}: H^n -> H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for every 0 <= n <= d holds as given. Fix an integer r with 0 <= r <= d. We prove that the restriction of beta_r to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate, i.e. that both radicals vanish:
  R_1 = {x in P^r : beta_r(x,y) = 0 for all y in P^r} = {0},
  R_2 = {y in P^r : beta_r(x,y) = 0 for all x in P^r} = {0}.

Step 1 (the map phi). Since L = cup product with xi raises cohomological degree by 2, the power L^{d-r} is the map H^r -> H^{r + 2(d-r)} = H^{2d-r}. Let phi = L^{d-r}|_{P^r}: P^r -> H^{2d-r}, and write phi(P^r) = L^{d-r} P^r for its image, a subspace of H^{2d-r}. We claim phi is an isomorphism P^r -> L^{d-r} P^r. Surjectivity onto the image is tautological, since L^{d-r} P^r is by definition the set of elements of the form L^{d-r} x with x in P^r. For injectivity: the hard Lefschetz hypothesis applied with n = r (which satisfies 0 <= r <= d) says that L^{d-r}: H^r -> H^{2d-r} is an isomorphism, in particular injective. The restriction of an injective linear map to any subspace is injective, and P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r -> H^{2d-r+2}) is a subspace of H^r, so phi is injective. Hence phi: P^r -> L^{d-r} P^r is an isomorphism.

Step 2 (nondegeneracy of the Poincare pairing on P^r x L^{d-r} P^r). Let B: H^r x H^{2d-r} -> Q_ell be the Poincare duality pairing B(u,v) = tr_X(u cup v). We invoke the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/4b7666. Its hypotheses match ours exactly: it requires d >= 1 (we have d >= 2), a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m} (this is X, since a geometrically connected variety is of pure dimension), a fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) with Tate twists identified with Q_ell, the same F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor class xi, the same L = cup product with xi, the same hard Lefschetz hypothesis L^{d-n}: H^n -> H^{2d-n} an isomorphism for 0 <= n <= d, the same definition P^s = ker(L^{d-s+1}: H^s -> H^{2d-s+2}) for 0 <= s <= d, and the same Poincare duality trace tr_X. Taking j = 0 in its conclusion (the side condition 0 <= 2j <= r reads 0 <= 0 <= r, which is automatic for every r >= 0), the lemma gives that the restriction of B to P^r x L^{d-r} P^r is nondegenerate, i.e. both radicals vanish:
  (i)  {u in P^r : B(u,w) = 0 for all w in L^{d-r} P^r} = {0};
  (ii) {w in L^{d-r} P^r : B(u,w) = 0 for all u in P^r} = {0}.

Step 3 (transfer to beta_r). For x, y in P^r, by the definition of beta_r and the functoriality of the cup product,
  beta_r(x,y) = tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y) = B(x, phi(y)).
Left radical: let x in P^r satisfy beta_r(x,y) = 0 for all y in P^r. Then B(x, phi(y)) = 0 for all y in P^r. Since phi is surjective onto L^{d-r} P^r (Step 1), this says B(x,w) = 0 for all w in L^{d-r} P^r. By (i), x = 0. Hence R_1 = {0}.
Right radical: let y in P^r satisfy beta_r(x,y) = 0 for all x in P^r. Then B(u, phi(y)) = 0 for all u in P^r. By (ii), phi(y) = 0. By injectivity of phi (Step 1), y = 0. Hence R_2 = {0}.
Therefore the restriction of beta_r to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate.

Step 4 (uniformity and edge cases, stated correctly). The argument of Steps 1-3 applies uniformly for every r with 0 <= r <= d, with no separate edge-case argument needed, because (a) phi is an isomorphism for every such r, as shown in Step 1 (L^{d-r} is injective on H^r by the hard Lefschetz hypothesis, and its image is by definition L^{d-r} P^r), and (b) Miner/16d24b0281973336/4b7666 with j = 0 gives nondegeneracy of B on P^r x L^{d-r} P^r for every 0 <= r <= d. For completeness we spell out the two endpoints correctly:
 - r = d: here L^{d-r} = L^0 = id, so phi is the identity map P^d -> P^d, where P^d = ker(L: H^d -> H^{d+2}); B is the Poincare duality pairing on H^d; and 4b7666 with j = 0 gives nondegeneracy of B on P^d x P^d. The two-radical argument of Step 3 applies as written.
 - r = 0: since X has pure dimension d and ell != p, etale cohomology with Q_ell coefficients vanishes in degrees > 2d (the etale topos of a smooth variety of pure dimension d over an algebraically closed field has cohomological dimension at most 2d for Q_ell), so H^{2d+2} = 0. Hence P^0 = ker(L^{d+1}: H^0 -> H^{2d+2}) = H^0; note in particular that P^0 = H^0, not 0. The map phi = L^d: P^0 -> L^d P^0 is an isomorphism because the hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n = 0 gives L^d: H^0 -> H^{2d} an isomorphism, so L^d is injective on P^0 = H^0 and L^d P^0 = L^d H^0 = H^{2d}; and 4b7666 with j = 0 gives nondegeneracy of B on P^0 x L^d P^0 = H^0 x H^{2d}, which is the usual Poincare duality pairing. The same two-radical argument applies, and it does not depend on the particular value of dim P^0, only on the isomorphism phi and the nondegeneracy of B on P^0 x L^d P^0.

Step 5 (parity of d). The proof above does not use the parity of d at all; the statement assumes d is even, so the conclusion holds a fortiori.

This completes the proof: for every 0 <= r <= d, the restriction of beta_r(x,y) = tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y) to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), let d>=2 be even, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. With Tate twists identified with Q_ell, put H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell), let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, let 0<=r<=d, put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C be an embedding. If F(P^r) is contained in P^r, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r, and every eigenvalue of F on H^r has absolute value q^{mr/2} under sigma, then there is a positive definite Hermitian form h on P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
All dependencies are confirmed. I now write the final proof, addressing both defects from the feedback: (1) Step 1 cites only the standard finiteness theorem, with the false parenthetical removed; (2) Step 4 uses the correct eigenvalue argument over \(\overline{\mathbb Q_\ell}\) with the injection \(P^r\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q_\ell}\hookrightarrow H^r\otimes\overline{\mathbb Q_\ell}\).

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/880e29",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/ce85e8", "eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_360"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that there is a positive definite Hermitian form h on P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y) for all x,y in P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C.

Setup and notation. Fix the data of the statement: q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2 even, X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}, H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell), xi the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L cup product with xi, with L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, 0<=r<=d, P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}), F the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C an embedding. The hypotheses are: (H1) F(P^r) is contained in P^r; (H2) F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r; (H3) every eigenvalue of F on H^r has absolute value q^{mr/2} under sigma.

Step 1 (Finiteness of dimension). By the standard finiteness theorem for etale cohomology, since X is a smooth projective variety over the finite field F_{q^m}, each group H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. In particular H^r is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. The map L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2} is Q_ell-linear: L is cup product with the fixed class xi in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), cup product is Q_ell-bilinear, and hence every iterate L^j:H^n->H^{n+2j} is Q_ell-linear (for r=0 the target is H^{2d+2}=0, so the map is the zero map to 0 and the statement is a fortiori true). Therefore P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}) is a Q_ell-subspace of H^r, and hence is finite-dimensional over Q_ell.

Step 2 (F is invertible on H^r). By (H2), the overline(Q_ell)-linear map F tensor id:H^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell)->H^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) is diagonalizable; its eigenvalues are precisely the eigenvalues of F on H^r (the characteristic polynomial is unchanged by base change). By (H3), every such eigenvalue alpha satisfies |sigma(alpha)|=q^{mr/2}>0, in particular alpha != 0. A diagonalizable operator is invertible if and only if all its eigenvalues are nonzero: in a basis in which F tensor id is diagonal, the diagonal entries are the eigenvalues, and the operator is invertible exactly when the product of these entries (its determinant) is nonzero. Hence F tensor id is invertible over overline(Q_ell). Consequently F is injective on H^r: if x in H^r satisfies Fx=0, then (F tensor id)(x tensor 1)=0, so x tensor 1=0, so x=0. Since H^r is finite-dimensional over Q_ell (Step 1), the injective Q_ell-linear endomorphism F of H^r is surjective, hence F in GL_{Q_ell}(H^r). In particular F is injective on H^r.

Step 3 (F|_{P^r} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell)). By Step 2, F in GL_{Q_ell}(H^r); by (H2), F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r; and by (H1), P^r is an F-stable Q_ell-subspace of H^r. We apply the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ce85e8 with K=Q_ell, Kbar=overline(Q_ell), V=H^r, T=F, and W=P^r. Its conclusion is that T|_W=F|_{P^r} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Write T:=F|_{P^r}.

Step 4 (Every eigenvalue of T satisfies |sigma(alpha)|^2=q^{mr}). Let alpha be an eigenvalue of T over overline(Q_ell). Since T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) (Step 3), there exists a nonzero vector v in P^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) such that (F tensor id)(v)=alpha v, where F tensor id denotes the induced overline(Q_ell)-linear automorphism of P^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) (equal to T tensor id). The inclusion i:P^r->H^r induces the Q_ell-linear map i tensor id:P^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell)->H^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell). This map is injective: choose a Q_ell-basis (e_1,...,e_s) of P^r and extend it to a Q_ell-basis (e_1,...,e_s,e_{s+1},...,e_n) of H^r (possible because P^r is a Q_ell-subspace of H^r); every element of P^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) is a finite sum sum_{i=1}^s e_i tensor a_i, and its image in H^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) is zero only if all a_i=0, since the e_i are part of a basis of H^r and hence linearly independent over overline(Q_ell). Let w=(i tensor id)(v) in H^r tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell). By injectivity, w != 0; and since i tensor id commutes with F tensor id (both are induced by the same Q_ell-linear map F on the first factor), we have (F tensor id)(w)=alpha w. Thus alpha is an eigenvalue of F on H^r over overline(Q_ell). By (H3), every eigenvalue of F on H^r has absolute value q^{mr/2} under sigma, so |sigma(alpha)|=q^{mr/2}, and therefore |sigma(alpha)|^2=q^{mr}.

Step 5 (T is invertible on P^r). By (H1), F(P^r) is contained in P^r, so T=F|_{P^r} is a well-defined Q_ell-linear endomorphism of P^r. Since F is injective on H^r (Step 2), T is injective on P^r: if x in P^r satisfies Tx=0, then Fx=0 in H^r, so x=0. Because P^r is finite-dimensional over Q_ell (Step 1), the rank-nullity theorem implies that the injective Q_ell-linear endomorphism T of P^r is surjective. Hence T(P^r)=P^r, i.e. T in GL_{Q_ell}(P^r).

Step 6 (Application of the linear algebra lemma). We apply the lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_360 with the following data: ell is the given prime; V=P^r, a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space (Step 1); T=F|_{P^r} in GL(V) (Step 5); sigma the given embedding of the algebraic closure overline(Q_ell) of Q_ell into C; and c=q^{mr}, a positive real number (since q=p^a>1, m>=1, and r>=0, we have q^{mr}>=1>0). The hypotheses of lemma_360 are satisfied: T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) (Step 3), and every eigenvalue alpha of T satisfies |sigma(alpha)|^2=q^{mr}=c (Step 4). Hence there exists a positive definite Hermitian form h on V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C=P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C such that h(T_sigma x,T_sigma y)=c h(x,y) for all x,y in P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C, where T_sigma is the C-linear automorphism of P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C induced by T.

Finally we identify T_sigma with F tensor id on P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. For a simple tensor x=v tensor z with v in P^r and z in C (via sigma), T_sigma(v tensor z)=(Tv) tensor z=(Fv) tensor z=(F tensor id)(v tensor z), because T=F|_{P^r}; by C-linearity the same identity holds for every x in P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. Substituting T_sigma=F tensor id and c=q^{mr} into the conclusion of lemma_360 gives h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr} h(x,y) for all x,y in P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C, with h positive definite Hermitian. This is exactly the desired conclusion."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1 be odd, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Put H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell), let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}), and let tr_X be the Poincare duality trace. Put beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y). Then the restriction of beta_r to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate.
proof:
Both lemmas are confirmed and their hypotheses match the target statement verbatim. The proof is a clean case split: `r < d` is exactly b475d7, and `r = d` reduces to the `j=0` instance of 9d4103 because `L^{d-d} = L^0 = id`, so `β_d` is the Poincaré pairing on `H^d` restricted to `P^d × P^d = W_0 × W_0`.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/c824af",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/b475d7", "Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that for every integer r with 0 <= r <= d, the restriction of beta_r(x,y) = tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y) to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate, where P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r -> H^{2d-r+2}).

First, check that the hypotheses of the two lemmas we invoke are satisfied in our setting. We have q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1 (indeed d odd), X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, xi the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L cup product with xi, and the hard Lefschetz assumption that L^{d-n}: H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d. These are precisely the standing assumptions of both cited lemmas. Note that neither lemma requires d to be odd; the oddness of d in our statement is therefore automatically satisfied and is not needed in the argument.

Case 1: 0 <= r < d. The lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/b475d7 applies to our X, xi, L, and tr_X with this fixed r (its only extra requirement, 0<=r<d, holds in this case). It states that with P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)) — the same subspace as in our statement — the bilinear form (x,y) -> tr_X(x cup L^{d-r} y) on P^r is nondegenerate. This form is exactly beta_r restricted to P^r x P^r. Hence beta_r|_{P^r x P^r} is nondegenerate in this case.

Case 2: r = d. We first identify beta_d. Since L^{d-r} = L^{d-d} = L^0, and L^0 is the identity map on cohomology (cup product with xi^0 = 1, the unit of the cohomology ring), we have for all x,y in H^d:
    beta_d(x,y) = tr_X(x cup L^0 y) = tr_X(x cup y).
Thus beta_d is the Poincare duality pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) (which pairs H^d with H^{2d-d} = H^d via cup product followed by the trace tr_X: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell), restricted to P^d x P^d.
Now apply the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103, whose hypotheses (d>=1, X smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, xi the class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L cup product with xi, hard Lefschetz for 0<=n<=d, and P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r -> H^{2d-r+2})) all hold in our setting. Take j = 0, which is a valid choice since 0 <= 0 <= floor(d/2) (as d >= 1). The lemma defines W_0 = L^0 P^{d-2*0} = P^d and asserts that the restriction of the Poincare duality pairing beta on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) to W_0 x W_0 = P^d x P^d is nondegenerate. Since beta_d = beta|_{P^d x P^d}, this is exactly the desired nondegeneracy for r = d.

Combining Case 1 and Case 2, the restriction of beta_r to P^r x P^r is nondegenerate for every integer r with 0 <= r <= d. This completes the proof."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), let d>=2 be even, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. With Tate twists identified with Q_ell, put H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell), let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, let 0<=r<=d, put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F(P^r) is contained in P^r and F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r, then F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on P^r.
proof:
We prove that F|_{P^r} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). The argument applies the restriction lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ce85e8 with V = H^r, T = F, and W = P^r. We verify its three hypotheses in order. (The hypotheses that d is even, that d >= 2, and that L^{d-n}:H^n -> H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0 <= n <= d are part of the ambient setup of the statement; the argument below uses only the two hypotheses F(P^r) subset P^r and that F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r, together with standard finiteness and linearity facts, so it applies a fortiori in the stated situation.)

Step 1 (Finiteness of H^r). Since X is projective over F_{q^m}, it is proper over F_{q^m}. Put q' = q^m = p^{am}; this is a prime power. Because F_q is contained in F_{q^m} which is contained in k, and k = overline(F_q) is algebraically closed, we have overline(F_{q^m}) = k; hence the base change of X (viewed as a variety over F_{q^m}) to overline(F_{q^m}) is exactly X_k. We apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob with the prime power q' in place of q, with X (a proper variety over F_{q^m}), and with K the constant sheaf Q_ell on X_k. To see that K is an object of D^b_c(X_k, Q_ell): X_k is a variety over k, hence a scheme locally of finite type over k, and the constant sheaf with coefficients Q_ell on a scheme locally of finite type over a field is a constructible Q_ell-sheaf, so K = Q_ell is an object of D^b_c(X_k, Q_ell). The constant sheaf Q_ell on X_k carries its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism psi: F_X^* Q_ell -> Q_ell, where F_X is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism on X_k. By lemma_45_finite_frob, for every integer n the cohomology H^n(X_k, Q_ell) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. In particular, H^r = H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space.

Step 2 (F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^r). We apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a with the prime power q' = q^m in place of q, with X (a scheme over F_{q^m}), k = overline(F_{q^m}) = overline(F_q), and sigma the q^m-power field automorphism of k, sigma(a) = a^{q^m}. By lemma_6a, the pullback map F_ar := (id_X x sigma)^* is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) for every i >= 0, and F_geo := (id_X x sigma^{-1})^* = F_ar^{-1}. The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) is, by definition, the pullback by id_X x sigma, i.e. F = F_ar. Hence F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^r, i.e. F is in GL_{Q_ell}(H^r). (Since H^r is finite-dimensional by Step 1, this also follows from the 'in particular' clause of lemma_6a.)

Step 3 (P^r is an F-stable Q_ell-subspace of H^r). The class xi is the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, so (with Tate twists identified with Q_ell) xi is a fixed element of the Q_ell-vector space H^2 = H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell). The map L^{d-r+1}: H^r -> H^{2d-r+2} is cup product with the fixed Q_ell-class xi^{d-r+1} in H^{2d-2r+2}(X_k, Q_ell). Etale cohomology with Q_ell coefficients carries the structure of a Q_ell-algebra under the cup product: the cup product H^a_et(X_k, Q_ell) x H^b_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{a+b}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is Q_ell-bilinear. Fixing the second factor at the fixed class xi^{d-r+1} therefore gives a Q_ell-linear map H^r -> H^{2d-r+2}. Hence its kernel P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r -> H^{2d-r+2}) is a Q_ell-subspace of H^r. By the hypothesis of the lemma, F(P^r) is contained in P^r, so P^r is F-stable, i.e. a T-stable Q_ell-subspace of V with T = F.

Step 4 (Application of the restriction lemma). We now have: (i) K = Q_ell is a field and Kbar = overline(Q_ell) is an algebraic closure of K; (ii) V = H^r is a finite-dimensional K-vector space (Step 1); (iii) T = F is in GL_K(V) (Step 2) and is diagonalizable over Kbar = overline(Q_ell) (by the hypothesis of the lemma); (iv) W = P^r is a T-stable K-subspace of V (Step 3). By Miner/16d24b0281973336/ce85e8, the restriction T|_W is diagonalizable over Kbar. That is, F|_{P^r} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), which is the desired conclusion.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let S be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}. Put H^s=H^s_et(S_k,Q_ell), let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L:H^0->H^2, L:H^1->H^3, and L^2:H^2->H^4 are isomorphisms. Put P^2=ker(L:H^2->H^4), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, suppose F(P^2) is contained in P^2, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Then P^2 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{2m}h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Q_ell(1) with Q_ell, so that the given divisor class xi is an element of H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell). Let A be the Q_ell-span in H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell) of the cycle classes of all Cartier divisors on S_k. Because S_k is geometrically connected, H^0_et(S_k,Q_ell) is the one-dimensional Q_ell-vector space of constant sections; explicitly H^0_et(S_k,Q_ell)=Q_ell. The map L:H^0_et(S_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell) is cup product with xi, so L(1)=xi. By hypothesis L is an isomorphism. Hence every element v of H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell) is of the form L(c) with c in H^0_et(S_k,Q_ell); since H^0_et(S_k,Q_ell)=Q_ell, c=lambda*1 for a unique lambda in Q_ell, and therefore v=lambda*xi. Thus H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell)=Q_ell xi. The very ample divisor whose class is xi is a Cartier divisor on S_k, so xi belongs to A. Since H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell) is the one-dimensional Q_ell-vector space spanned by xi, it follows that A=H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell). Now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/4ac54e. Its hypotheses are satisfied: S is a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}; xi is the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor; L is cup product with xi; P^2=ker(L:H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell)->H^4_et(S_k,Q_ell)); F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius and by assumption F(P^2) is contained in P^2; and sigma is an embedding of overline(Q_ell) into C. The lemma yields a positive definite Hermitian form h on (A intersect P^2) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C such that h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{2m} h(x,y) for all x,y in that tensor space. Because A=H^2_et(S_k,Q_ell), we have A intersect P^2 = P^2. Hence (A intersect P^2) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C = P^2 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. The form h is therefore a positive definite Hermitian form on P^2 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C satisfying the required Frobenius scaling. This proves the lemma.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let r be an integer, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let beta be a nondegenerate bilinear form with beta(y,x)=(-1)^r beta(x,y), let c in K^*, and let T in GL_K(V) satisfy beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y). For n>=1 put G_n(x,y)=beta(x,T^n y)+(-1)^r c^n beta(x,T^{-n}y). If for every nonzero x in V there exists n>=1 with G_n(x,x)!=0, then T is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K.
proof: Proof. We argue by contrapositive. Suppose T is not diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K. Let m(t) be the minimal polynomial of T over K. If m were square-free, then in characteristic 0 every irreducible factor of m is separable, and distinct irreducible factors have no common root over an algebraic closure; hence the minimal polynomial of T over the algebraic closure would be a product of distinct linear factors, so T would be diagonalizable. Thus m has a repeated irreducible factor. Choose a monic irreducible f in K[t] and an integer e>=2 such that f^e divides m but f^(e+1) does not; write m=f^e g with gcd(f,g)=1. Put A=f(T) and W=ker A^e. Since A commutes with T, W is T-stable. We first show A^(e-1) restricted to W is nonzero. Since m is minimal, no proper divisor of m annihilates T. In particular A^(e-1) g(T) is not zero: if it were, f^(e-1) g would be a proper divisor of m annihilating T. Choose u in V with A^(e-1) g(T) u != 0 and set v=g(T) u. Then A^e v = f(T)^e g(T) u = m(T) u = 0, so v is in W, while A^(e-1) v = A^(e-1) g(T) u != 0. Hence A^(e-1) restricted to W is nonzero. Let S=A^(e-1) W, the image of A^(e-1) restricted to W. Then S is nonzero. For y in S, y=A^(e-1) w with w in W, so A y = A^e w = 0; thus A|_S=0. Since e>=2, y=A^(e-2)(A w), so S is contained in im A. Also T S = A^(e-1) T W = A^(e-1) W = S, so S is T-stable. Define B=f(c T^-1). This is an endomorphism of V because T is invertible. It commutes with A; hence B W is contained in W, because A^e(Bw)=B A^e w=0 for w in W. Therefore B(S) is contained in S. We record the adjoint identity: for all u,v in V, beta(Au,v)=beta(u,Bv). Indeed, from beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y) with y=T^-1 v we get beta(Tu,v)=c beta(u,T^-1 v)=beta(u,c T^-1 v); applying this to the polynomial f(T) gives the displayed identity, and iterating gives beta(A^k u,v)=beta(u,B^k v) for all k>=0. We now choose a nonzero vector x in S orthogonal to all of S. There are two cases. Case 1: B|_S is invertible. If x,y are in S, choose z in S with y=Bz. Then beta(x,y)=beta(x,Bz)=beta(Ax,z)=0, because Ax=0. Thus every nonzero x in S is orthogonal to S. Case 2: B|_S is not invertible. Since S is finite-dimensional, ker(B|_S) is nonzero. Choose nonzero x in S with Bx=0. If y is in S, write y=A^(e-1) w with w in W. Then, using the symmetry beta(p,q)=(-1)^r beta(q,p) and the adjoint identity, beta(x,y)=beta(x,A^(e-1) w)=(-1)^r beta(A^(e-1) w,x)=(-1)^r beta(w,B^(e-1) x)=0. Thus this x is orthogonal to S. In either case we have a nonzero x in S such that beta(x,y)=0 for every y in S. Since S is T-stable, T^n x is in S for every n>=1, and therefore beta(x,T^n x)=0 for every n>=1. It remains to translate this to the given G_n. For n>=1, using beta(T^-n u,T^-n v)=c^-n beta(u,v) (which follows by inverting beta(Tu,Tv)=c beta(u,v)) and the symmetry of beta, we have beta(x,T^-n x)=c^-n beta(T^n x,x)=(-1)^r c^-n beta(x,T^n x). Consequently G_n(x,x)=beta(x,T^n x)+(-1)^r c^n beta(x,T^-n x)=2 beta(x,T^n x). Since char K=0, 2 is nonzero, so G_n(x,x)=0 for every n>=1. This contradicts the hypothesis that every nonzero vector has some n with G_n(x,x) != 0. Hence T must be diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U=X \setminus Y, let j:U->X, let delta:H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) be the Gysin boundary, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose the restriction map j^* restricts to an isomorphism phi:P^d->ker(delta) of Q_ell[F]-modules. Let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d(X), and let beta_U be the bilinear form on ker(delta) defined by beta_U(phi(x),phi(z))=beta(x,z). Then beta_U is nondegenerate.
proof:
We must show that the Q_ell-bilinear form beta_U on ker(delta) (a subspace of H^d(U)) is nondegenerate, i.e. that both its left and right radicals are zero.

Step 1 (the restriction of beta to P^d x P^d is nondegenerate). We apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103. We verify each of its hypotheses in our setting. (i) The parameters q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q) are exactly those of the statement. (ii) The lemma requires d>=1; we have d>=2, so this holds. (iii) X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}; since X is smooth it is equidimensional, hence of pure dimension d, as the lemma requires. (iv) Since Y is a very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, its cycle class xi=[Y] in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, and L is cup product with xi, exactly as in the lemma. (v) The hypothesis of the statement that L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d is precisely the Lefschetz-type hypothesis of the lemma. (vi) For r=d the subspace P^r of the lemma is ker(L^{d-d+1}:H^d(X)->H^{2d-d+2}(X)) = ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), which is exactly our P^d. (vii) Since d>=2, floor(d/2)>=1, so j=0 is an admissible index of the lemma; for this index W_0 = L^0 P^{d-2*0} = P^d. (viii) The pairing beta in the statement is the Poincare duality pairing on H^d(X): the canonical perfect pairing H^d(X) x H^d(X) -> Q_ell(2d), written as a Q_ell-bilinear form via an identification Q_ell(2d) = Q_ell; this is the same pairing denoted beta in the lemma (and in any case any two such Q_ell-valued pairings differ by a nonzero scalar of Q_ell, which does not change the radical of a bilinear form, so the conclusion below is independent of the convention). By the conclusion of Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103, the restriction of beta to W_0 x W_0 = P^d x P^d is nondegenerate. Concretely, we have the two properties: (A) if x in P^d satisfies beta(x,z)=0 for every z in P^d, then x=0; and (B) if x in P^d satisfies beta(z,x)=0 for every z in P^d, then x=0.

Step 2 (well-definedness of beta_U). By hypothesis, phi:P^d -> ker(delta) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules, hence in particular a Q_ell-linear isomorphism of vector spaces. Therefore every u in ker(delta) can be written as u=phi(x) for a unique x in P^d. The rule beta_U(phi(x),phi(z))=beta(x,z) thus defines a well-defined Q_ell-bilinear form on ker(delta): the value at (u,v) is independent of the chosen representations because the preimages x,z are unique, and bilinearity follows from the Q_ell-linearity of phi and the bilinearity of beta.

Step 3 (nondegeneracy of beta_U). Right radical: let u in ker(delta) satisfy beta_U(u,v)=0 for every v in ker(delta). Write u=phi(x) with x in P^d (possible by surjectivity of phi). For every z in P^d the element v=phi(z) lies in ker(delta) (by surjectivity, phi(z) is in the image phi(P^d)=ker(delta)), so 0 = beta_U(phi(x),phi(z)) = beta(x,z). By property (A), x=0, and hence u=phi(0)=0. Left radical: let u in ker(delta) satisfy beta_U(v,u)=0 for every v in ker(delta). Write u=phi(x) with x in P^d. For every z in P^d, taking v=phi(z) in ker(delta) gives 0 = beta_U(phi(z),phi(x)) = beta(z,x). By property (B), x=0, and hence u=0. Both radicals of beta_U are therefore zero, so beta_U is nondegenerate. This completes the proof.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let sigma:overline(K)->C be an embedding, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let beta be a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form on V, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, and let F in GL_K(V) satisfy beta(Fx,Fy)=c beta(x,y). Suppose that for every nonzero x in V tensor_{K} overline(K) there exists n>=1 with beta(x,F^n x)+c^n beta(x,F^{-n}x)!=0, where beta and F are extended to V tensor_{K} overline(K). Then there is a positive definite Hermitian form h on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Proof. Let Kbar = overline(K) and W = V ⊗_K Kbar. Extend beta and F to W. If dim_K V = 0, the zero Hermitian form on the zero C-vector space satisfies the conclusion vacuously, so assume dim V > 0. We use the following elementary observation. Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, every subspace of dimension at least 2 of a k-vector space with a symmetric bilinear form contains a nonzero isotropic vector. Indeed, it is enough to consider a 2-dimensional subspace E0. If the restriction of the form to E0 is degenerate, a nonzero vector in its radical is isotropic. If the restriction is nondegenerate, choose a basis u,v and write the form on t u + v as a t^2 + 2b t + d. If a=0 then b != 0 and t=-d/(2b) works; if a != 0 the discriminant has a square root in k. We also use the following auxiliary fact. Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0, let E be finite-dimensional over k, let b be a symmetric bilinear form (not assumed nondegenerate), and let U in GL_k(E) be unipotent and an isometry for b. If U != id, then there exists 0 != x in ker(U-id) with b(x,x)=0. Proof of the auxiliary fact. Put N=U-id, a nonzero nilpotent endomorphism. Let M=ker N. If dim M >= 2, the elementary observation gives a nonzero isotropic vector in M, and we are done. Assume dim M = 1, say M = k y. If b(y,y)=0 we are done. Suppose b(y,y) != 0. For every u in E, b(Nu,y) = b(Uu-u,y) = b(Uu,y) - b(u,y). Since U is an isometry and U^{-1}y=y (because Uy=y), we have b(Uu,y)=b(u,U^{-1}y)=b(u,y). Hence b(Nu,y)=0 for all u, so im N is contained in y^perp. By rank-nullity, dim im N = dim E - 1. Since b(y,y) != 0, the linear functional z -> b(y,z) is nonzero, so dim y^perp = dim E - 1. Thus im N = y^perp. Also y is not in y^perp, so E = k y ⊕ y^perp. The endomorphism N preserves y^perp because im N is contained in y^perp. It is injective on y^perp: if w in y^perp and Nw=0, then w in ker N = k y, and k y ∩ y^perp = 0. It is surjective on y^perp: if z in y^perp, then z in im N, so z=Nu for some u; write u=alpha y + w with w in y^perp; since Ny=0, z=Nw. Therefore N|_{y^perp} is invertible. But N is nilpotent, so its restriction to y^perp is nilpotent. An invertible nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space forces the space to be zero: if N^m=0 and N is invertible, then I=N^{-m}N^m=0. Hence y^perp=0, so E=k y and N=0, contradicting U != id. This proves the auxiliary fact. By the proved lemma Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/bc7724, the multiplicative Jordan decomposition F = F_s F_u = F_u F_s exists with F_s semisimple and F_u unipotent, and the unipotent part is an isometry: beta(F_u x, F_u y)=beta(x,y) for all x,y in V. Put S=F_s and U=F_u. Since U is invertible and an isometry, S is also a similitude with factor c: for arbitrary x,y choose a,b with x=U a and y=U b; then beta(Sx,Sy)=beta(F a,F b)=c beta(a,b)=c beta(U^{-1}x,U^{-1}y)=c beta(x,y). Extend S and U to W. Since S is semisimple, W decomposes as a direct sum of its eigenspaces W = ⊕_λ E_λ. Since S and U commute, U preserves each E_λ. Suppose U != id. Then for some λ the restriction U_λ=U|_{E_λ} is not the identity. Apply the auxiliary fact to E_λ with the restricted form beta and the unipotent isometry U_λ. We obtain 0 != y in E_λ such that U y = y and beta(y,y)=0. Because y is an S-eigenvector with eigenvalue λ and U y=y, we have F y = S U y = λ y, and hence F^{-1} y = λ^{-1} y. For every n >= 1, beta(y,F^n y) + c^n beta(y,F^{-n} y) = beta(y,λ^n y) + c^n beta(y,λ^{-n} y) = (λ^n + c^n λ^{-n}) beta(y,y) = 0. This contradicts the hypothesis applied to y. Therefore U=id, and F=S is semisimple; in particular F is diagonalizable over Kbar. Now let y be a nonzero eigenvector of F over Kbar with eigenvalue λ. If beta(y,y)=0, then the same computation gives beta(y,F^n y)+c^n beta(y,F^{-n} y)=0 for every n, contradicting the hypothesis. Thus beta(y,y) != 0. From beta(Fy,Fy)=c beta(y,y) we get λ^2 beta(y,y)=c beta(y,y), so λ^2=c. Thus every eigenvalue of F is a root of t^2-c. Let r be a square root of c in Kbar; the only possible eigenvalues are r and -r. For an occurring eigenvalue λ, suppose dim E_λ >= 2. The elementary observation gives a nonzero y in E_λ with beta(y,y)=0, but y is an eigenvector, contradicting the preceding paragraph. Hence dim E_λ = 1 for every occurring eigenvalue. If both r and -r occur, then for y in E_r and z in E_{-r} we have (r(-r)-c) beta(y,z)=0, i.e. -2c beta(y,z)=0. Since c != 0 and char K = 0, beta(y,z)=0. Finally construct h. Identify V_σ = V ⊗_{K,σ} C with W ⊗_{Kbar,σ} C. For each occurring eigenvalue λ choose a nonzero vector e_λ in E_λ. The vectors e_λ ⊗ 1 form a C-basis of V_σ. Write x = Σ_λ a_λ (e_λ ⊗ 1) and y = Σ_λ b_λ (e_λ ⊗ 1) with a_λ,b_λ in C. Define h(x,y) = Σ_λ a_λ overline{b_λ}. This is a Hermitian form: it is C-linear in the first variable, conjugate-linear in the second, and h(y,x)=overline{h(x,y)}. It is positive definite because h(x,x)=Σ_λ |a_λ|^2 vanishes only when all a_λ are zero. The induced action of F on V_σ sends e_λ⊗1 to σ(λ)(e_λ⊗1). Since λ^2=c, we have σ(λ)^2=σ(c)>0; a complex number whose square is a positive real number is real, so |σ(λ)|^2=σ(c). Therefore h(F_σ x,F_σ y) = Σ_λ |σ(λ)|^2 a_λ overline{b_λ} = σ(c) Σ_λ a_λ overline{b_λ} = σ(c) h(x,y). This is the required positive definite Hermitian form.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U=X \setminus Y, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F on H^d(U) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then F on P^d is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Let i:Y->X and j:U->X be the inclusions. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell, so that L is a map H^s(X)->H^{s+2}(X). First we show that H^d(U) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. The variety X is proper over F_{q^m}, and Y is proper over F_{q^m} because it is closed in the projective variety X. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob with the prime power q^m to the proper varieties X and Y, taking K to be the constant sheaf Q_ell; this gives that H^d(X) and H^{d-1}(Y) are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces. Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement with the prime power q^m; for n=d it gives the exact sequence of Q_ell-vector spaces H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) -> H^d(X) -> H^d(U) -> H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) -> H^{d+1}(X). Exactness at H^d(U) gives 0 -> im(H^d(X)->H^d(U)) -> H^d(U) -> im(H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1)) -> 0. The first term is a quotient of the finite-dimensional space H^d(X), and the second term is a subspace of the finite-dimensional space H^{d-1}(Y)(-1); hence H^d(U) is finite-dimensional. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a with the prime power q^m, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^d(U). Next, apply Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_420 to X_k and Y_k. The divisor Y_k is a nonempty smooth very ample, hence ample, Cartier divisor of pure dimension d-1, and d>=2, so d-2<d-1; therefore i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/92549f we have F L = q^m L F on H^*(X). If x in P^d, then Lx=0, so 0=F(Lx)=q^m L(Fx), and since q^m is nonzero in Q_ell, L(Fx)=0; thus F(P^d) is contained in P^d, and F restricts to P^d. Since H^d(X) is finite-dimensional, P^d is finite-dimensional. Now apply Miner/16d24b0281973336/987402, using the given hard Lefschetz isomorphisms L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) for 0<=n<=d and the isomorphism i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) just obtained. It says that j^*:P^d->H^d(U) is an injective morphism of F-modules. Let W=j^*(P^d). Because j^* is a morphism of F-modules, F(W) is contained in W; since W is finite-dimensional and F is injective, F(W)=W. Thus W is an F-stable Q_ell-subspace of H^d(U), and j^*|_{P^d}:P^d->W is an isomorphism of F-modules. By hypothesis, F on H^d(U) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Since H^d(U) is finite-dimensional and W satisfies F(W)=W, Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_440 implies that F|_W is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Finally, diagonalizability is preserved under an isomorphism of F-modules: after extending scalars to overline(Q_ell), a basis of W consisting of eigenvectors for F|_W pulls back via (j^*|_{P^d})^{-1} to a basis of P^d consisting of eigenvectors for F|_{P^d}. Therefore F on P^d is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U=X \setminus Y, let i:Y->X, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism and H^d(X)=L H^{d-2}(X) \oplus P^d as F-stable subspaces. If F on H^d(U) and on H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), then F on H^d(X) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Fix the implicit nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell, so that xi is a class in H^2(X) and L is cup product with xi. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. The cohomology groups involved are finite-dimensional over Q_ell. Since d>=2, the integer d-2 satisfies 0<=d-2<=d. By the assumed hard Lefschetz isomorphisms, L^2:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d+2}(X) is an isomorphism. Hence L:H^{d-2}(X)->H^d(X) is injective: if x in H^{d-2}(X) satisfies Lx=0, then L^2x=L(Lx)=0, and injectivity of L^2 forces x=0. Now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/20f6b1. Its hypotheses are satisfied: X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d, Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor, i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism by assumption, and L is injective as shown. Therefore the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)(-1)->H^d(X) is an isomorphism of F-modules onto L H^{d-2}(X). In particular, L H^{d-2}(X) is an F-stable Q_ell-subspace of H^d(X). By hypothesis, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^{d-2}(Y)(-1). Diagonalizability is preserved under an isomorphism of F-modules: after extending scalars to overline(Q_ell), an eigenbasis of H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) is carried by i_! to an eigenbasis of L H^{d-2}(X), because i_! intertwines the two F-actions. Thus F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on L H^{d-2}(X). The hypothesis also gives that F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d(U). We can now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/09e405. Its assumptions hold: d>=2, X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d, Y is smooth ample (very ample implies ample) and geometrically connected, hard Lefschetz holds for L, i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism, and F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d(U) and on L H^{d-2}(X). The conclusion of that lemma is that F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d(X). This is exactly the desired conclusion. The stated direct-sum decomposition is consistent with the F-stability of L H^{d-2}(X) obtained above; the conclusion follows without using it further.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let D be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, and let i:D->X be the inclusion. With Tate twists identified with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of D and let L be cup product with xi. Let beta_X:H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell be the Poincare duality pairing and let beta_D:H^{d-1}_et(D_k,Q_ell) x H^{d-1}_et(D_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell be the Poincare duality pairing. Then beta_X(Lx,y)=beta_D(i^*x,i^*y) for all x,y in H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
I have everything I need. The cited lemma `eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor` provides both the Gysin characterising identity (with $b$ in the correct degree $H^{2d-2-n}$) and the projection formula $i_!(i^*x)=x\cup\xi$. Specializing at $n=d-1$ and substituting gives the target identity, with the traces matching the declared Poincaré duality pairings under the common Tate-twist identification. I now write the proof, following the reviser's guidance and the verifier's fix (no descent claim; simply instantiate the lemma at the prime power $q^m$).

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/8735d6",
  "cited_lemmas": ["eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove the identity beta_X(Lx,y)=beta_D(i^*x,i^*y) for all x,y in H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l) by a single specialization of the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor (the Gysin projection formula for a divisor).

STEP 1 (Instantiation of the cited lemma). The cited lemma is stated for a prime power q, a smooth projective geometrically connected variety X of pure dimension d>=1 over F_q, a smooth effective divisor Y of pure dimension d-1 defined over F_q, its inclusion i:Y->X, the algebraic closure k=overline(F_q), a prime l!=p, and a fixed nonzero element u in Q_l(1) used to identify Q_l(n) with Q_l via u^n->1. We instantiate it with the prime power q^m = p^{am} in place of its q. Concretely: the base field is F_{q^m}; our X is smooth, projective, geometrically connected, of pure dimension d>=2 (hence >=1) over F_{q^m}; and D is a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, hence in particular a smooth effective divisor of pure dimension d-1 defined over F_{q^m} (a very ample divisor is an effective Cartier divisor, and since X has pure dimension d, the divisor D has pure dimension d-1). All hypotheses of the cited lemma are therefore satisfied by (X,D). The field of constants in the cited lemma is overline(F_{q^m}) = overline(F_q) = k, the very field over which the target computes its cohomology; thus the Gysin map i_!, the cycle class xi, and the traces tr_X and tr_D furnished by the cited lemma all live over the same k, and no descent or base-change statement is needed. Finally, the cited lemma's identification of Tate twists (fix a nonzero u in Q_l(1) and send u^n to 1) is the same data as the target's phrase 'with Tate twists identified with Q_l' (an isomorphism Q_l(1)->Q_l, equivalently a choice of nonzero u in Q_l(1) sent to 1). We take the cited lemma's identification to be exactly the target's. Under this common identification, the cited lemma's xi (the cycle class of D) is the target's xi, the cited lemma's cup product with xi is the target's L, and the cited lemma's traces tr_X, tr_D are the traces that define the target's Poincaré duality pairings beta_X, beta_D, as made precise in Step 4.

STEP 2 (The Gysin characterising identity at n=d-1). The cited lemma characterises the Gysin homomorphism i_!:H^{d-1}_et(D_k,Q_l)->H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_l) (the case n=d-1, which is >=0 since d>=2) by the identity
    tr_X(i_! a cup b) = tr_D(a cup i^* b)
for every a in H^{d-1}_et(D_k,Q_l) and every b in H^{2d-2-(d-1)} = H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l). (Note the correct degree for b is H^{2d-2-n}=H^{d-1}(X_k), not H^{d+1}(X_k).) We take a = i^* x, where x in H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l) (so i^* x in H^{d-1}_et(D_k,Q_l)), and b = y in H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l). Both lie in the required degrees. Substituting gives
    tr_X( i_!(i^* x) cup y ) = tr_D( i^* x cup i^* y ).      (1)
Degree check: i_!(i^* x) lies in H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_l) (i_! raises degree by 2) and y lies in H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l), so i_!(i^* x) cup y lies in H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_l), the top degree on X, on which tr_X is defined. On the right, i^* x cup i^* y lies in H^{2d-2}_et(D_k,Q_l), the top degree on D (dim D = d-1), on which tr_D is defined. Hence (1) is a well-typed equality of elements of Q_l.

STEP 3 (The projection formula). The cited lemma also proves the projection formula i_!(i^* x) = x cup xi for every n>=0 and every x in H^n_et(X_k,Q_l). Applying it with n = d-1 and our x in H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l) gives i_!(i^* x) = x cup xi = L x, where L is cup product with xi. Substituting this into the left-hand side of (1) yields
    tr_X( L x cup y ) = tr_D( i^* x cup i^* y ).              (2)

STEP 4 (Identification of the traces with the declared pairings). Under the common Tate-twist identification, the Poincaré duality pairing on X of type H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_l) x H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l) -> Q_l is the map (alpha,beta) -> tr_X(alpha cup beta), i.e. the cup product into H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_l) followed by the trace tr_X: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_l)->Q_l (the Poincaré duality trace composed with the identification Q_l(d)->Q_l). This is exactly the target's beta_X, whose first slot has degree d+1 and second slot degree d-1. Similarly, the Poincaré duality pairing on D (dimension d-1) is (gamma,delta) -> tr_D(gamma cup delta) with tr_D: H^{2d-2}_et(D_k,Q_l)->Q_l the Poincaré duality trace, which is the sum of the traces on the connected components of D_k (matching the cited lemma's convention and the standard trace on D_k whether or not D_k is connected). This is exactly the target's beta_D. Therefore the two sides of (2) are precisely beta_X(L x, y) and beta_D(i^* x, i^* y): the left side tr_X(L x cup y) is beta_X evaluated on (L x, y) with L x in the first (degree d+1) slot and y in the second (degree d-1) slot, matching the cup-product order L x cup y, so no graded-commutativity sign is introduced; the right side tr_D(i^* x cup i^* y) is beta_D(i^* x, i^* y) with the same ordering. Hence (2) reads
    beta_X(L x, y) = beta_D(i^* x, i^* y).

Since x and y were arbitrary elements of H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_l), the identity holds for all such x,y, which completes the proof."
}

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let sigma:overline(K)->C be an embedding, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, and let F in GL_K(V). Suppose F is diagonalizable over overline(K) and every eigenvalue alpha of F in overline(K) satisfies |sigma(alpha)|=sqrt(sigma(c)). Then V tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Let Kbar denote an algebraic closure of K and put Vbar = V tensor_K Kbar. Since F is K-linear, it induces Fbar on Vbar. By hypothesis Fbar is diagonalizable over Kbar. Let alpha_1,...,alpha_r be the distinct eigenvalues of Fbar in Kbar^*. Then Vbar is the direct sum of the eigenspaces E_alpha_i = ker(Fbar - alpha_i id). Each E_alpha_i is a finite-dimensional Kbar-vector space. The embedding sigma:Kbar -> C induces a natural isomorphism V tensor_{K,sigma} C = (V tensor_K Kbar) tensor_{Kbar,sigma} C. Under this identification, F tensor id corresponds to Fbar tensor id. Since tensoring with C commutes with finite direct sums, V tensor_{K,sigma} C is the direct sum of W_i = E_alpha_i tensor_{Kbar,sigma} C, and on W_i the operator F tensor id acts as multiplication by sigma(alpha_i). Thus F tensor id is diagonalizable over C, with eigenspaces W_i. For each i, choose a positive definite Hermitian form h_i on W_i. Explicitly, if dim_C W_i = n_i > 0, choose a C-basis e_{i,1},...,e_{i,n_i} and define h_i(sum_j a_{i,j} e_{i,j}, sum_j b_{i,j} e_{i,j}) = sum_j a_{i,j} times the complex conjugate of b_{i,j}; if W_i = 0 set h_i = 0. Then h_i is C-linear in the first variable, conjugate-linear in the second, and h_i(x,x) > 0 for every nonzero x in W_i. Define h on V tensor_{K,sigma} C by h(x,y) = sum_i h_i(x_i,y_i), where x = sum_i x_i and y = sum_i y_i are the unique decompositions in the direct sum of the W_i. This is a Hermitian form because each h_i is Hermitian and the summands are mutually orthogonal by construction. It is positive definite: if x is nonzero, then some x_i is nonzero, so h(x,x) = sum_i h_i(x_i,x_i) is a sum of nonnegative terms containing at least one positive term, hence is positive. The case V = 0 is covered by the same formula with an empty sum, giving the zero form, which is positive definite vacuously. Finally, let lambda = sigma(c), which is a positive real number. For every i, the hypothesis gives |sigma(alpha_i)| = sqrt(lambda), so sigma(alpha_i) times the complex conjugate of sigma(alpha_i) equals |sigma(alpha_i)|^2 = lambda. For x = sum_i x_i and y = sum_i y_i, we have (F tensor id)x = sum_i sigma(alpha_i) x_i and similarly for y. Therefore h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sum_i h_i(sigma(alpha_i)x_i, sigma(alpha_i)y_i) = sum_i sigma(alpha_i) times the complex conjugate of sigma(alpha_i) times h_i(x_i,y_i) = sum_i lambda h_i(x_i,y_i) = lambda h(x,y) = sigma(c) h(x,y). This proves the desired identity.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, let U=X \setminus Y, let j:U->X, let delta:H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) be the Gysin boundary, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose the restriction map j^* restricts to an isomorphism phi:P^d->ker(delta) of Q_ell[F]-modules. Let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d(X), let beta_U be the bilinear form on ker(delta) defined by beta_U(phi(x),phi(z))=beta(x,z), and let beta_U also denote its base change to ker(delta) \otimes_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell). If for every nonzero y in ker(delta) \otimes_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) there exists n>=1 such that beta_U(y,F^n y)+(-1)^d q^{mdn} beta_U(y,F^{-n} y) != 0, then the restriction of F to P^d is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof: Put Q = q^m and regard X as a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_Q. Write Qbar_ell for an algebraic closure of Q_ell. We use the standard Q_ell-valued Poincare pairing on H^d(X) obtained from the usual identification of the Tate twist Q_ell(-d) with Q_ell; changing this identification only multiplies the pairing by a nonzero scalar and does not affect the argument. Let W = ker(delta) tensor_{Q_ell} Qbar_ell.
