By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob], instantiated with the prime power Q, applied to the constant sheaf Q_ell on X_k, H^d(X) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell; hence P^d and V = P^d tensor_{Q_ell} Qbar_ell are finite-dimensional. Let beta_P be the restriction of beta to P^d x P^d. The assumed hard Lefschetz, with xi the cycle class of Y, is exactly the hypothesis of [Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103]; taking j = 0 in that lemma gives W_0 = P^d and says that beta_P is nondegenerate. Since phi is an isomorphism, beta_U is nondegenerate on ker(delta), and its base change is nondegenerate on W. For u,v in H^d(X), graded commutativity of the cup product gives u cup v = (-1)^{d^2} v cup u = (-1)^d v cup u; applying the Poincare trace gives beta(v,u) = (-1)^d beta(u,v). Hence beta_V, the base change of beta_P to V, satisfies beta_V(u,v) = (-1)^d beta_V(v,u). By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a], instantiated with Q, the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^d(X). By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable], instantiated with Q, the primitive subspace P^d = ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)) is stable under both F and F^{-1}. Thus T = F|_{P^d} is an element of GL_{Q_ell}(P^d), and T_bar = T tensor id is an element of GL_{Qbar_ell}(V). By [Miner/16d24b0281973336/2be0a7], beta(Fx,Fy) = q^{md} beta(x,y) for all x,y in H^d(X). Since P^d is F-stable, beta_P(Tx,Ty) = q^{md} beta_P(x,y) for all x,y in P^d, and after base change beta_V(T_bar x,T_bar y) = q^{md} beta_V(x,y). Let F_W be the Frobenius on W induced by F. Because phi is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules, its extension phi_bar: V -> W is an isomorphism of Qbar_ell[F]-modules; in particular phi_bar(T_bar x) = F_W(phi_bar(x)) and phi_bar(T_bar^{-n}x) = F_W^{-n}(phi_bar(x)) for every n >= 1. By the definition of beta_U and its base change, for every x in V, with y = phi_bar(x), one has beta_U(y,F_W^n y) + (-1)^d q^{mdn} beta_U(y,F_W^{-n} y) = beta_V(x,T_bar^n x) + (-1)^d q^{mdn} beta_V(x,T_bar^{-n} x). The hypothesis applied to every nonzero y in W therefore implies that for every nonzero x in V there exists n >= 1 such that beta_V(x,T_bar^n x) + (-1)^d (q^{md})^n beta_V(x,T_bar^{-n} x) != 0, where (q^{md})^n = q^{mdn}. Now apply [Miner/16d24b0281973336/ab2720] with K = Qbar_ell, r = d, V, beta = beta_V, c = q^{md}, and T = T_bar. All hypotheses of that lemma are satisfied, so T_bar is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of Qbar_ell, i.e. over Qbar_ell itself. This is exactly the statement that the restriction of F to P^d is diagonalizable over Qbar_ell.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Then every eigenvalue of F on H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{md}.
proof:
Let q=p^a be a prime power, ell != p a prime, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d>=1 over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_{et}(X_k,Q_ell).

Step 1 (Frobenius-equivariant identification of the top cohomology with a Tate twist). Apply part (a) of the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77 to Y=X (with l=ell). Its hypotheses are exactly those at hand: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Part (a) provides a canonical isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces
  tr: H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) --~--> Q_ell(-d),
normalised by tr(cl(x))=[k(x):F_{q^m}] for every closed point x of X, and it states that tr is arithmetic-Frobenius-equivariant, where F acts on Q_ell(-d) as multiplication by the positive rational number q^{md}.

Step 2 (F acts on H^{2d} by the scalar q^{md}). As a Q_ell-vector space, Q_ell(-d) is one-dimensional, so H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is one-dimensional as well. Let 0 != x in H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell). By the Frobenius-equivariance of tr and by the fact that F acts on Q_ell(-d) by the scalar q^{md},
  tr(Fx) = F(tr(x)) = q^{md} tr(x) = tr(q^{md} x),
where the last equality uses the Q_ell-linearity of tr. Since tr is injective, Fx = q^{md} x. Hence F acts on H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) as multiplication by the scalar q^{md}, and the only eigenvalue of F on H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is q^{md}, viewed in overline(Q_ell) via the inclusions Q -> Q_ell -> overline(Q_ell).

Step 3 (Weil absolute value of q^{md}). The number q^{md} is a positive rational number. Let sigma: overline(Q_ell) -> C be any embedding. Every embedding of overline(Q_ell) into C restricts to the identity on Q, so sigma(q^{md}) = q^{md} in R_{>0}, and therefore |sigma(q^{md})| = q^{md}. Since Q(q^{md}) = Q has a single complex embedding, the Weil absolute value of q^{md} is |q^{md}| = q^{md} (this is independent of the normalisation of the Weil absolute value, because the relevant field has degree 1 over Q).

Step 4 (Conclusion). The only eigenvalue of F on H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is q^{md}, and its Weil absolute value is q^{md}. Therefore every eigenvalue of F on H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{md}. QED.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, let 0<=r<=d, put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, suppose F(P^r) is contained in P^r, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y) for all x,y, then the restriction of F to P^r is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
proof:
We work entirely over the base field F_{q^m}; no descent to F_q is performed.

Step 1 (Finite-dimensionality of H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell)). Set q' := q^m = p^{am}, which is a prime power. We have k = overline(F_q) = overline(F_{q'}), since F_{q^m} is a finite subextension of the algebraic closure overline(F_q) and overline(F_q) is already algebraically closed, hence is an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}. The variety X is smooth projective over F_{q'}, hence proper over F_{q'}. We now instantiate eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob with the prime power q' in place of its parameter q: take X (a proper variety over F_{q'}), k = overline(F_{q'}), ell != p, and K = Q_ell (the constant sheaf on X_k) equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius isomorphism psi: F_X^* Q_ell -> Q_ell, where F_X is the q'-power = q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism on X_k. The lemma concludes that for every integer n, the hypercohomology H^n(X_k, Q_ell) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. In particular, H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space.

Step 2 (F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell)). We instantiate eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a with the prime power q' = q^m in place of its parameter q: take X (a scheme over F_{q'}), k = overline(F_{q'}), and sigma: k -> k the q'-power field automorphism sigma(a) = a^{q^m}. The lemma states that for every integer i >= 0 and every prime ell != p, the pullback map F_ar := (id_X x sigma)^* is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell). Taking i = r, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F := F_ar is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Step 3 (P^r is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-subspace). The map L^{d-r+1}: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is cup product with the fixed cohomology class xi^{d-r+1}, and is therefore Q_ell-linear. Hence P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}) is a Q_ell-subspace of H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell). Since H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) is finite-dimensional over Q_ell by Step 1, the subspace P^r is also finite-dimensional over Q_ell.

Step 4 (T := F|_{P^r} lies in GL_{Q_ell}(P^r)). By hypothesis, F(P^r) is contained in P^r. Since F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) by Step 2, the restriction T := F|_{P^r} is a Q_ell-linear endomorphism of P^r. Because F is injective on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell), its restriction T is injective on P^r. Since P^r is finite-dimensional over Q_ell by Step 3, the injective endomorphism T is surjective. Therefore T is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of P^r, i.e. T in GL_{Q_ell}(P^r).

Step 5 (Application of the Hermitian-form diagonalizability criterion). Set c := q^{mr}. Since q >= 2, m >= 1, and r >= 0, we have c = q^{mr} >= 1 > 0, so c in R_{>0}. The hypothesis provides a positive definite Hermitian form h on P^r tensor_{Q_ell, sigma} C satisfying h((F tensor id)x, (F tensor id)y) = q^{mr} h(x,y) = c h(x,y) for all x, y in P^r tensor_{Q_ell, sigma} C. Because F(P^r) subset P^r, on the subspace P^r tensor_{Q_ell, sigma} C the operator F tensor id coincides with T tensor id (since for v in P^r, (F tensor id)(v tensor 1) = Fv tensor 1 = Tv tensor 1 = (T tensor id)(v tensor 1), and both sides are Q_ell-linear and agree on the spanning set). Hence h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = c h(x,y) for all x, y in P^r tensor_{Q_ell, sigma} C.

We now apply Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_408 with the following data: V = P^r (a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space by Step 3), T in GL(V) (by Step 4), sigma: overline(Q_ell) -> C (the given field embedding), and c = q^{mr} in R_{>0}. The hypothesis of lemma_408 is satisfied: h is a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{Q_ell, sigma} C such that h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = c h(x,y) for all x, y. The conclusion of lemma_408 is that T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).

Since T = F|_{P^r}, this means the restriction of F to P^r is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), which is the desired conclusion.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Let 0<=r<=d, 0<=j<=d-r, put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}), let L^j P^r be the image of P^r under L^j, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F(P^r) is contained in P^r and every eigenvalue of F on H^r, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}, then every eigenvalue of F on L^j P^r, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(r+2j)/2}.
proof: Proof. We use the standard identification of Q_l(1) with Q_l obtained by fixing a nonzero element of Q_l(1); under this identification the divisor class xi and the Lefschetz operator L in the statement are the untwisted ones used in the cited lemmas. Let F denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. All cohomology spaces are finite-dimensional. Step 1. F preserves P^r. By hypothesis F(P^r) is contained in P^r. The operator F is induced by the automorphism of X_k, so it is an automorphism of H^r; hence its restriction to P^r is injective and dim(F(P^r))=dim(P^r). Since F(P^r) is a subspace of P^r of the same dimension, F(P^r)=P^r. Step 2. Purity on P^r. The hard Lefschetz hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis of the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/c1a8d4. Applying that lemma with the same X, xi, L, r, and F, we obtain that every eigenvalue of F|_{P^r}, viewed in Q_lbar, has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Step 3. Frobenius shifts Lefschetz powers. By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable, the arithmetic Frobenius satisfies F L = q^m L F on every cohomology group H^s. Iterating this identity gives, for every j>=0 and every x in H^r, F(L^j x)=q^{mj} L^j(F x). Step 4. L^j is injective on P^r. Let v in P^r satisfy L^j v=0. Since j<=d-r, we have L^{d-r} v = L^{d-r-j}(L^j v)=0. By the hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n=r, L^{d-r}:H^r -> H^{2d-r} is an isomorphism, in particular injective. Hence v=0. Thus the map A_j: P^r -> L^j P^r, v -> L^j v, is an isomorphism onto its image. Step 5. Conjugacy and weights. For v in P^r, Step 3 gives F(L^j v)=q^{mj} L^j(F v). Because F v in P^r by Step 1, the right-hand side lies in L^j P^r, so F preserves L^j P^r. For y=L^j v in L^j P^r, F|_{L^j P^r}(y)=q^{mj} A_j(F|_{P^r}(v))=q^{mj} A_j(F|_{P^r}(A_j^{-1}(y))). Thus F|_{L^j P^r} is similar to q^{mj} F|_{P^r}. Consequently the set of eigenvalues of F on L^j P^r, viewed in Q_lbar, is q^{mj} times the set of eigenvalues of F on P^r. Let mu be an eigenvalue of F on L^j P^r. Then mu=q^{mj} lambda for some eigenvalue lambda of F on P^r. By Step 2, for every embedding sigma:Q_lbar -> C, |sigma(lambda)|=q^{mr/2}. Since sigma(q^{mj})=q^{mj}, we get |sigma(mu)|=q^{mj} q^{mr/2}=q^{m(r/2+j)}=q^{m(r+2j)/2}. This is the desired Weil absolute value. The argument includes the boundary cases j=0, r=d (where j=0), and r=0 without modification.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X. If for every 0<=r<=d-1 every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r(Y), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}, then for every 0<=r<=d-1 every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r(X), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.
proof: Fix an integer r with 0 <= r <= d-1. Let F_X and F_Y denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Since Y is very ample, it is ample. If r <= d-2, the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/d35572 gives that i^*:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective. If r = d-1, the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/79a472 gives the same injectivity. Thus i^* identifies H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) with a Q_ell-subspace W of H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell). The immersion i is defined over F_{q^m}; by functoriality of etale cohomology and the definition of the arithmetic Frobenius action, i^* is a morphism of Q_ell[F]-modules, i.e. F_Y i^* = i^* F_X. Hence W is F_Y-stable. Choose a Q_ell-basis of W and extend it to a Q_ell-basis of H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell). In this basis the matrix of F_Y is block upper triangular, with the upper-left block equal to the matrix of F_X under the identification H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) ~ W. Therefore the characteristic polynomial P_X(t) of F_X on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) divides the characteristic polynomial P_Y(t) of F_Y on H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) in Q_ell[t]. Consequently every root of P_X in overline(Q_ell) is a root of P_Y, i.e. every eigenvalue of F_X on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an eigenvalue of F_Y on H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell). By the hypothesis, every eigenvalue of F_Y on H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Therefore every eigenvalue of F_X on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Since r was arbitrary with 0 <= r <= d-1, the lemma is proved.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Put H^s=H^s_et(Y_k,Q_ell), let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If H^{d-2} tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(d-2)}h(x,y) for all x,y, then L H^{d-2} tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h' with h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{md}h'(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Let Q=q^m. Regard Y as a smooth projective variety over F_Q of pure dimension d, and let the divisor defining xi be an F_Q-rational very ample divisor. The operator F in the statement is the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius. First, L:H^{d-2}->H^d is injective. Indeed, the hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n=d-2 says L^2:H^{d-2}->H^{d+2} is an isomorphism, hence injective. If x in H^{d-2} satisfies Lx=0, then L^2 x = L(Lx)=0, so x=0. Put V=H^{d-2} and W=L(V) subset H^d. Then L:V->W is a Q_l-linear isomorphism. By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a applied with Q in place of q, the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius is a Q_l-linear automorphism of H^i_et(Y_k,Q_l) for every i; in particular F_V=F|_V and F|_{H^d} are well-defined automorphisms. By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable applied to Y over F_Q with the same divisor and Frobenius, F L = Q L F on H^{d-2}. Hence for x in V, F(Lx)=Q L(Fx). Thus F(W) subset W, and the restriction F_W=F|_W is a well-defined Q_l-linear map of W. Let L_C:V tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C -> W tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C be the C-linear map induced by L. Since L is a Q_l-linear isomorphism onto W, L_C is a C-linear isomorphism. Define h' on W tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C as follows: for z,w in W tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C, write z=L_C x and w=L_C y uniquely with x,y in V tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C, and set h'(z,w)=h(x,y). This is well-defined because L_C is an isomorphism. It is a Hermitian form because h is Hermitian and L_C is C-linear. It is positive definite: if z=L_C x, then h'(z,z)=h(x,x), which is nonnegative and is zero only when x=0, hence only when z=0. Now verify the required scaling. For x in V tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C, using C-linearity and the identity F_W(Lv)=Q L(Fv) for v in V, we have (F_W tensor id)(L_C x)=L_C(Q F_V x). Here Q=q^m is a positive rational number, so under sigma it is the same positive real number Q in C. Therefore, for z=L_C x and w=L_C y, h'((F_W tensor id)z,(F_W tensor id)w) = h'(L_C(Q F_V x), L_C(Q F_V y)) = h(Q F_V x, Q F_V y) = Q^2 h((F_V tensor id)x,(F_V tensor id)y) = Q^2 q^{m(d-2)} h(x,y) = q^{2m} q^{m(d-2)} h(x,y) = q^{md} h'(z,w). The step h(Q u, Q v)=Q^2 h(u,v) uses that Q is real, so the scalar and its complex conjugate are both Q. Since F_W is the restriction of F to W=L H^{d-2}, this gives a positive definite Hermitian form h' on L H^{d-2} tensor_{Q_l,sigma} C satisfying h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{md}h'(x,y) for all x,y. This proves the lemma.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let 0<=r<=2d be an integer. If every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}, then every eigenvalue of F on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(2d-r)/2}.
proof:
The duality lemma I need is confirmed: **eoinm/ebe471c6ef5b2d01/921283** states that for 0≤n≤2d, if α∈overline(Q_ℓ)^× is an eigenvalue of F on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ℓ), then q^{md}/α is an eigenvalue of F on H^{2d−n}_et(X_k,Q_ℓ). Applying it with n=2d−r gives exactly the direction I need. Following the reviser's fix, I will work embedding-by-embedding with the concrete meaning of the Weil-absolute-value hypothesis, without defining a Weil absolute value for arbitrary algebraic numbers and without invoking any multiplicativity.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/df3b9b",
  "cited_lemmas": ["eoinm/ebe471c6ef5b2d01/921283"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "Proof. Interpretation of the hypothesis. The eigenvalues of F on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), are algebraic numbers (elements of Q^alg subset overline(Q_ell)). To say that such an eigenvalue gamma "has Weil absolute value c" means that gamma is a Weil number of absolute value c, i.e. that for every complex embedding sigma: Q(gamma) -> C one has |sigma(gamma)| = c. The argument below uses only this concrete, embedding-by-embedding content of the hypothesis; no multiplicativity property of any Weil-absolute-value function is invoked, and no definition of a Weil absolute value for arbitrary algebraic numbers is introduced.

Step 1 (duality of eigenvalues). Let alpha be an eigenvalue of F on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell). Since F is the pullback of the automorphism sigma: X_k -> X_k, sigma(c)=c^{q^m} of X_k, F is an automorphism of the finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell); hence alpha != 0, i.e. alpha in overline(Q_ell)^x. Since 0 <= r <= 2d, we have 0 <= 2d-r <= 2d, so the duality lemma eoinm/ebe471c6ef5b2d01/921283 applies with n = 2d-r: beta := q^{md}/alpha is an eigenvalue of F on H^{2d-(2d-r)}_et(X_k,Q_ell) = H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell). In particular beta is an algebraic number and beta != 0.

Step 2 (apply the hypothesis to beta). By the hypothesis, every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Hence beta is a Weil number of absolute value q^{mr/2}: for every complex embedding sigma: Q(beta) -> C, |sigma(beta)| = q^{mr/2}.

Step 3 (equality of number fields). Since q^{md} is a positive rational number, alpha = q^{md}/beta belongs to Q(beta), and beta = q^{md}/alpha belongs to Q(alpha). Hence Q(alpha) = Q(beta).

Step 4 (embedding-by-embedding computation). Let tau: Q(alpha) -> C be any complex embedding. Since Q(alpha) = Q(beta), tau is simultaneously a complex embedding of Q(beta). Using the field operations and q^{md} in Q^x, |tau(alpha)| = |tau(q^{md}/beta)| = q^{md}/|tau(beta)|. By Step 2, |tau(beta)| = q^{mr/2}. Therefore |tau(alpha)| = q^{md}/q^{mr/2} = q^{md - mr/2} = q^{(2md - mr)/2} = q^{m(2d-r)/2}, where the last equality is the elementary computation md - mr/2 = (2md - mr)/2 = m(2d-r)/2.

Step 5 (conclusion). Since tau was arbitrary, every complex embedding of alpha has modulus q^{m(2d-r)/2}. That is, alpha is a Weil number with Weil absolute value q^{m(2d-r)/2}. Since alpha was an arbitrary eigenvalue of F on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), the conclusion follows.

The argument is uniform in r and covers the edge cases r = 0 and r = 2d without modification: in these cases Step 1 applies the duality lemma with n = 2d or n = 0 respectively, both of which lie in the permitted range 0 <= n <= 2d. Q.E.D."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_{q^m}, let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Then H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
We prove that H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=h(x,y) for all x,y.

Step 1 (the field chain and k as an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}). We have the inclusions F_q subset F_{q^m} subset k = overline(F_q). Indeed, since q=p^a and q^m=p^{am} with a dividing am, the field F_q=F_{p^a} is the unique subfield of F_{p^{am}}=F_{q^m} having q elements, hence F_q subset F_{q^m}; and F_{q^m} is a finite extension of F_q, hence a subfield of the algebraic closure overline(F_q)=k. We claim k is an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}. By construction k=overline(F_q) is algebraically closed. To see k is algebraic over F_{q^m}, take any a in k. Since k=overline(F_q), a is algebraic over F_q, so there is a nonzero polynomial f in F_q[t] with f(a)=0. Because F_q subset F_{q^m}, the inclusion of polynomial rings F_q[t] subset F_{q^m}[t] identifies f with a nonzero polynomial of F_{q^m}[t] that still vanishes at a; hence a is algebraic over F_{q^m}. As a was arbitrary, k is algebraic over F_{q^m}. Being algebraically closed and algebraic over F_{q^m}, k is an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}.

Step 2 (X_k is nonempty and connected). Nonempty: X is a variety over F_{q^m}, hence a nonempty scheme of finite type over F_{q^m}. The projection X_k = X x_{F_{q^m}} k -> X is the base change of the morphism Spec k -> Spec F_{q^m}, which is a bijection of single points and therefore surjective; surjectivity is stable under base change, so X_k -> X is surjective, and since X is nonempty, X_k is nonempty. Connected: X is geometrically connected over F_{q^m}, i.e. X x_{F_{q^m}} kbar is connected for kbar an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}. By Step 1, k is an algebraic closure of F_{q^m}; hence X_k = X x_{F_{q^m}} k is connected.

Step 3 (H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the one-dimensional Q_ell-space). The group H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the space of global sections of the constant sheaf Q_ell on the etale site of X_k, i.e. the space of locally constant functions X_k -> Q_ell (Q_ell with the discrete topology). Since X_k is connected (Step 2), every locally constant function X_k -> Q_ell is constant. Hence H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) is canonically isomorphic to Q_ell, a one-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, with the constant function 1 as a basis vector.

Step 4 (F acts as the identity on H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Let F: X_k -> X_k be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius morphism; its action on H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the pullback F^*: H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell). The pullback of the constant sheaf Q_ell under F is again the constant sheaf Q_ell (the stalk at a point x is the stalk Q_ell at F(x), with trivial monodromy in both cases). For a global section s, a locally constant function X_k -> Q_ell, the pullback is F^*s(x) = s(F(x)). In particular, for the constant section 1, F^*1(x) = 1(F(x)) = 1, so F^*1 = 1. Under the identification H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) = Q_ell · 1 of Step 3, F^* is therefore the identity map. Thus F acts as the identity on H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell).

Step 5 (the positive definite Hermitian form). Let phi: H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C -> C be the C-linear isomorphism obtained by composing the isomorphism H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> Q_ell of Step 3 with the standard isomorphism Q_ell tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C -> C given by a tensor c |-> sigma(a) c. Define h(x,y) := phi(x) · overline(phi(y)) for x,y in H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C, where overline(.) is complex conjugation. (i) h is a Hermitian form: it is C-linear in the first variable and conjugate-C-linear in the second, and h(y,x) = phi(y)·overline(phi(x)) = overline(phi(x)·overline(phi(y))) = overline(h(x,y)). (ii) h is positive definite: h(x,x) = phi(x)·overline(phi(x)) = |phi(x)|^2 >= 0, and h(x,x)=0 iff phi(x)=0 iff x=0, since phi is an isomorphism. (iii) h is F-invariant: by Step 4, F acts as the identity on H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell), hence F tensor id acts as the identity on H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C; therefore for all x,y, h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = h(x,y). This completes the proof.

statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, let T be a Q_ell-linear endomorphism of V whose eigenvalues in overline(Q_ell) are algebraic over Q, let W be a T-stable Q_ell-subspace, and let Z=V/W. Suppose T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on W and on Z, and the sets of Weil absolute values of the eigenvalues of T on W and on Z are disjoint. Then T is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on V.
proof:
Let K = Q_ell and let L = Qbar_ell, the algebraic closure of K. Let pi: V -> Z be the quotient map. If V = 0, there is nothing to prove. If W = 0, then Z = V and the hypothesis says T is diagonalizable on Z = V. If Z = 0, then W = V and the hypothesis says T is diagonalizable on W = V. So assume W and Z are nonzero.

First we show that the eigenvalues of T on W and on Z are disjoint. Let Spec_W = { lambda in L : lambda is an eigenvalue of T|_W } and Spec_Z = { mu in L : mu is an eigenvalue of the induced operator T_Z on Z }. Because W is T-stable, after choosing a basis of W and extending it to a basis of V, the matrix of T is block upper triangular with diagonal blocks the matrices of T|_W and T_Z. Therefore the characteristic polynomial of T is the product of the characteristic polynomials of T|_W and T_Z. Hence every element of Spec_W union Spec_Z is an eigenvalue of T on V; by the hypothesis on T, each such element is algebraic over Q. The Weil absolute value is a well-defined function on algebraic numbers (with value 0 at 0), so equal algebraic numbers have equal Weil absolute value. If lambda belonged to Spec_W intersect Spec_Z, then its Weil absolute value would belong simultaneously to the set of Weil absolute values of eigenvalues on W and to the corresponding set for Z, contradicting the assumed disjointness. Therefore Spec_W and Spec_Z are disjoint.

Let m_W be the minimal polynomial of T|_W over L, and let m_Z be the minimal polynomial of T_Z over L. Since T|_W is diagonalizable over L, W tensor_K L decomposes as a direct sum of its eigenspaces; the polynomial product_{lambda in Spec_W} (t - lambda) annihilates T|_W, and any annihilating polynomial must vanish at every eigenvalue, so m_W(t) = product_{lambda in Spec_W} (t - lambda), a product of distinct linear factors. Similarly, m_Z(t) = product_{mu in Spec_Z} (t - mu). Because Spec_W and Spec_Z are disjoint, m_W and m_Z have no common factor in L[t]; in particular gcd(m_W, m_Z) = 1.

Let m_V be the minimal polynomial of T on V over L. We claim that m_V divides m_W m_Z in L[t]. Indeed, m_Z(T_Z) = 0. For v in V, pi(m_Z(T)v) = m_Z(T_Z)pi(v) = 0, so m_Z(T)v lies in W. Applying m_W(T) gives m_W(T)m_Z(T)v = m_W(T|_W)(m_Z(T)v) = 0, because m_Z(T)v is in W and m_W(T|_W)=0. Thus (m_W m_Z)(T)=0, and by minimality of m_V we get m_V | m_W m_Z.

The polynomial m_W m_Z is squarefree: it is a product of distinct linear factors, and the two factors m_W and m_Z are coprime. Any divisor of a squarefree polynomial is squarefree; hence m_V is squarefree in L[t]. Since L is algebraically closed, m_V splits as a product of distinct linear factors, m_V(t) = product_{j=1}^r (t - lambda_j) with the lambda_j distinct.

It remains to note that this implies T is diagonalizable over L. For completeness, let e_j in L[t] be the Lagrange interpolation polynomials satisfying e_j(lambda_j)=1 and e_j(lambda_i)=0 for i != j. The polynomials e_j^2 - e_j, e_i e_j for i != j, and 1 - sum_j e_j vanish at every lambda_i, so they are divisible by m_V. Hence the operators P_j = e_j(T) satisfy P_j^2 = P_j, P_i P_j = 0 for i != j, and sum_j P_j = I. Moreover (T - lambda_j I)P_j = 0, so im(P_j) is contained in the eigenspace ker(T - lambda_j I). The decomposition V = sum_j im(P_j) is therefore a direct sum of subspaces on which T acts by scalars, which means T is diagonalizable over L. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, and let U be the open complement of Y in X. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on P^d and on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1), every eigenvalue of F on P^d has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}, and every eigenvalue of F on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}, then F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell).
proof: Let V = H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) and let delta: V -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) be the Gysin boundary. All cohomology groups involved are finite-dimensional over Q_ell. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement, delta is the boundary map in the long exact Gysin sequence of the smooth pair (X,Y). This sequence is functorial with respect to the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius of the pair (X,Y): the Frobenius endomorphism preserves Y and U, and the maps j^*, delta, i_! are natural. Hence F delta = delta F. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/c93af5, the composite P^d -> H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> V is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules onto ker(delta). Let A = ker(delta). Then A is F-stable, F|_A is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue of F|_A has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}. Let W = im(delta). Since F delta = delta F, W is F-stable and delta induces an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules V/A -> W. By hypothesis, F on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) and all its eigenvalues have Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}. The restriction F|_W is diagonalizable because its minimal polynomial over overline(Q_ell) divides the minimal polynomial of F on the ambient space, which is a product of distinct linear factors. Its eigenvalues are among those of the ambient space, so they have Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}. Therefore the induced action of F on V/A is diagonalizable and has eigenvalues of Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}. Now apply the following linear algebra fact: if T on a finite-dimensional vector space E has a T-stable subspace A such that T|_A and T on E/A are diagonalizable over an algebraic closure and their spectra are disjoint, then T is diagonalizable over that algebraic closure. Indeed, let p_A and p_B be the minimal polynomials of T|_A and of T on E/A. They are products of distinct linear factors. For v in E, p_B(T)v lies in A, because its image in E/A is zero. Then p_A(T)p_B(T)v = 0. Thus the minimal polynomial of T divides p_A p_B. Since the spectra are disjoint, p_A p_B is a product of distinct linear factors, so the minimal polynomial of T is squarefree and split, and T is diagonalizable. Here the eigenvalues on A have Weil absolute value q^{md/2}, and the eigenvalues on V/A have Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}. Since d >= 2 and m >= 1, these two Weil absolute values are different, their ratio being q^{3m/2} > 1. Hence the spectra are disjoint. Therefore F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on V = H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell).

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, 0<=r<=d-2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, i:Y->X, xi the cycle class of Y, L cup product with xi, and assume L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r(X)->H^{2d-r+2}(X)) and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose F(P^r) is contained in P^r, i^*:H^r(X)->H^r(Y) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If H^r(Y) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y), then P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_P with h_P((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h_P(x,y).
proof:
We prove the result by a direct pullback construction. The argument is uniform in $r$ and handles all cases $0 \le r \le d-2$ identically, including $r=0$.

**Setup and notation.** Let $F_X$ denote the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on $H^r(X)$, let $F_Y$ denote the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on $H^r(Y)$, and let $F_P = F_X|_{P^r}$ denote the induced $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear endomorphism of $P^r$ (which is well-defined because the hypothesis gives $F_X(P^r) \subseteq P^r$). Write $\phi := i^*|_{P^r} : P^r \to H^r(Y)$ for the restriction of the pullback map to the subspace $P^r$.

**Step 1: $\phi$ is a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear injection.**
The map $i^* : H^r(X) \to H^r(Y)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell[F]$-modules by hypothesis, so in particular it is a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear isomorphism, hence injective. The restriction $\phi = i^*|_{P^r}$ of an injective linear map to a subspace is again injective: if $x \in P^r$ and $\phi(x) = 0$, then $i^*(x) = 0$, so $x = 0$ by injectivity of $i^*$.

**Step 2: The intertwining relation.**
We claim that $F_Y \circ \phi = \phi \circ F_P$, i.e., for every $x \in P^r$,
$$F_Y(\phi(x)) = \phi(F_P(x)).$$
Indeed, the hypothesis that $i^*$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell[F]$-modules means precisely that $i^* \circ F_X = F_Y \circ i^*$ as endomorphisms of $H^r(Y)$. Now take $x \in P^r$. Since $F_X(P^r) \subseteq P^r$, we have $F_X(x) \in P^r$, so $F_P(x) = F_X(x)$ (the latter being the restriction of the former to $P^r$). Applying the module-isomorphism identity to $x$:
$$F_Y(\phi(x)) = F_Y(i^*(x)) = i^*(F_X(x)) = i^*(F_P(x)) = \phi(F_P(x)).$$
This establishes the intertwining relation $F_Y \circ \phi = \phi \circ F_P$.

**Step 3: Base change to $\mathbb{C}$.**
Let $\Phi := \phi \otimes \mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{C}} : P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C} \to H^r(Y) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$ denote the base change of $\phi$ to $\mathbb{C}$, and let $F_P \otimes \mathrm{id}$ and $F_Y \otimes \mathrm{id}$ denote the base changes of $F_P$ and $F_Y$ respectively. Since $\phi$ is $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear, $\Phi$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear. The intertwining relation $F_Y \circ \phi = \phi \circ F_P$ is a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear identity, and base change to $\mathbb{C}$ (which is exact, as $\mathbb{C}$ is a flat $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-module) preserves it, giving
$$(F_Y \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Phi = \Phi \circ (F_P \otimes \mathrm{id}).$$

**Step 4: $\Phi$ is injective.**
We verify that $\Phi$ is injective. Let $\{e_1, \ldots, e_N\}$ be a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-basis of $P^r$. Then $\{e_1 \otimes 1, \ldots, e_N \otimes 1\}$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-basis of $P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell} \mathbb{C}$. Since $\phi$ is injective, $\{\phi(e_1), \ldots, \phi(e_N)\}$ is $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linearly independent in $H^r(Y)$. We claim $\{\phi(e_1) \otimes 1, \ldots, \phi(e_N) \otimes 1\}$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linearly independent in $H^r(Y) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell} \mathbb{C}$. Suppose $\sum_{i=1}^N c_i (\phi(e_i) \otimes 1) = 0$ with $c_i \in \mathbb{C}$. Write each $c_i$ in terms of a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-basis of $\mathbb{C}$ (viewing $\mathbb{C}$ as a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-vector space); this reduces to checking linear independence over $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$. Concretely: extend $\{\phi(e_1), \ldots, \phi(e_N)\}$ to a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-basis $\{\phi(e_1), \ldots, \phi(e_N), f_{N+1}, \ldots, f_M\}$ of $H^r(Y)$. Then $\{\phi(e_1) \otimes 1, \ldots, \phi(e_N) \otimes 1, f_{N+1} \otimes 1, \ldots, f_M \otimes 1\}$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-basis of $H^r(Y) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell} \mathbb{C}$. In this basis, the vector $\sum c_i (\phi(e_i) \otimes 1)$ has coordinates $(c_1, \ldots, c_N, 0, \ldots, 0)$. If this is zero, then all $c_i = 0$. Hence $\Phi$ is injective.

**Step 5: Definition of $h_P$.**
Define a form $h_P$ on $P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$ by
$$h_P(x, y) := h\big(\Phi(x),\, \Phi(y)\big)$$
for all $x, y \in P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$. This is the pullback of the Hermitian form $h$ along the $\mathbb{C}$-linear map $\Phi$.

**Step 6: $h_P$ is a Hermitian form.**
Since $h$ is a Hermitian form on $H^r(Y) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$, it satisfies: (i) $h$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second; (ii) $h(x, y) = \overline{h(y, x)}$ for all $x, y$. The pullback $h_P = h \circ (\Phi \times \Phi)$ inherits both properties because $\Phi$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear: for $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, $h_P(\lambda x, y) = h(\Phi(\lambda x), \Phi(y)) = h(\lambda \Phi(x), \Phi(y)) = \lambda h(\Phi(x), \Phi(y)) = \lambda h_P(x, y)$, and similarly for conjugate-linearity in the second variable, and $h_P(x, y) = h(\Phi(x), \Phi(y)) = \overline{h(\Phi(y), \Phi(x))} = \overline{h_P(y, x)}$. Thus $h_P$ is a Hermitian form.

**Step 7: $h_P$ is positive definite.**
Let $x \in P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$ with $x \neq 0$. By Step 4, $\Phi$ is injective, so $\Phi(x) \neq 0$ in $H^r(Y) \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$. By the positive definiteness of $h$,
$$h_P(x, x) = h(\Phi(x), \Phi(x)) > 0.$$
This holds for every nonzero $x$, so $h_P$ is positive definite.

**Step 8: The scaling identity.**
We now verify that $h_P$ satisfies the required scaling. For all $x, y \in P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$:
\begin{align}
h_P\big((F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})(x),\, (F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})(y)\big)
&= h\Big(\Phi\big((F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})(x)\big),\, \Phi\big((F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})(y)\big)\Big) \quad \text{[definition of } h_P \text{]}\\
&= h\Big((F_Y \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Phi (x),\, (F_Y \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Phi (y)\Big) \quad \text{[intertwining, Step 3]}\\
&= h\Big((F_Y \otimes \mathrm{id})(\Phi(x)),\, (F_Y \otimes \mathrm{id})(\Phi(y))\Big) \quad \text{[linearity of } \Phi \text{]}\\
&= q^{mr} \, h(\Phi(x), \Phi(y)) \quad \text{[scaling hypothesis on } h \text{]}\\
&= q^{mr} \, h_P(x, y) \quad \text{[definition of } h_P \text{].}
\end{align}

**Conclusion.** The form $h_P$ on $P^r \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$ defined in Step 5 is a positive definite Hermitian form (Steps 6 and 7) satisfying $h_P((F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})x, (F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})y) = q^{mr} h_P(x, y)$ for all $x, y$ (Step 8). This is exactly the required conclusion. The argument is uniform in $r$: when $r = 0$ the factor $q^{mr} = q^0 = 1$ and the scaling identity reads $h_P((F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})x, (F_P \otimes \mathrm{id})y) = h_P(x, y)$, which is precisely what the computation in Step 8 yields (since $F$ acts trivially on $H^0$ and hence on $P^0 = H^0(X)$, though the argument does not require this observation — it follows purely from the formal computation). No special case is needed.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_{q^m}. Write H^1=H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Suppose F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) and every eigenvalue of F on H^1, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}. Then H^1 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^m h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
Let V := H^1_et(C_k, Q_ell). We prove the claim by applying the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ccebfa with K = Q_ell, c = q^m, and the given data. We verify each hypothesis of that lemma in turn.

(0) Finite-dimensionality of V. Since C is a smooth projective curve over F_{q^m}, its first etale cohomology with Q_ell-coefficients is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space; in fact dim_{Q_ell} V = 2g where g is the genus of C (a standard finiteness theorem for etale cohomology of smooth projective varieties over finite fields). In particular V is finite-dimensional over K = Q_ell.

(1) K has characteristic 0. K = Q_ell is a field of characteristic 0.

(2) The embedding. sigma: overline(K) = overline(Q_ell) -> C is the embedding given in the statement.

(3) The scalar c. Set c := q^m. Because q = p^a is a prime power and ell != p, q^m is a nonzero rational number, hence c = q^m lies in Q_ell^*. Since sigma is a field embedding it fixes the prime field Q pointwise, and q^m in Q, so sigma(c) = sigma(q^m) = q^m > 0. Thus c in K^* with sigma(c) > 0, as required.

(4) F is invertible (F in GL_K(V)). We argue from the hypotheses. The eigenvalues of F are the roots in overline(Q_ell) of its characteristic polynomial chi_F(t) in Q_ell[t]. By the hypothesis, every such eigenvalue alpha has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}; in particular |sigma(alpha)| = q^{m/2} > 0, so no eigenvalue is 0. Hence the product of the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) is nonzero. But det(F) equals this product up to the sign (-1)^n (n = dim V), so det(F) != 0, and F is invertible over Q_ell. (Equivalently, and conceptually, F is the action of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, an element of the absolute Galois group Gal(overline(F_q)/F_q), on the etale cohomology V; the Galois group acts on V as a group of Q_ell-linear automorphisms, so F is invertible.) In either case F in GL_{Q_ell}(V).

(5) Diagonalizability. The statement of the target lemma assumes F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) = overline(K). This is exactly the corresponding hypothesis of ccebfa.

(6) The eigenvalue modulus condition. We must show every eigenvalue alpha of F in overline(K) satisfies |sigma(alpha)| = sqrt(sigma(c)). Recall the definition: an algebraic number alpha is said to have Weil absolute value q^{m/2} (relative to q) precisely when |tau(alpha)| = q^{m/2} for every embedding tau: Q(alpha) -> C (equivalently, alpha is a Weil number of weight m). The hypothesis of the target lemma states that every eigenvalue alpha of F, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}; this presupposes each alpha is an algebraic number and, by the definition just recalled, means |tau(alpha)| = q^{m/2} for every embedding tau: Q(alpha) -> C. Now alpha in overline(Q_ell) is an algebraic number, so Q(alpha) is a subfield of overline(Q) subset overline(Q_ell). The restriction sigma|_{Q(alpha)}: Q(alpha) -> C is an embedding, so |sigma(alpha)| = |(sigma|_{Q(alpha)})(alpha)| = q^{m/2}. On the other hand, sqrt(sigma(c)) = sqrt(q^m) = q^{m/2} (the positive square root, since q^m > 0). Therefore |sigma(alpha)| = q^{m/2} = sqrt(sigma(c)) for every eigenvalue alpha. This is exactly the eigenvalue condition in ccebfa.

Having verified all hypotheses (K of characteristic 0; sigma an embedding overline(K)->C; c = q^m in K^* with sigma(c) > 0; V finite-dimensional over K; F in GL_K(V); F diagonalizable over overline(K); and every eigenvalue alpha satisfying |sigma(alpha)| = sqrt(sigma(c))), the lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ccebfa applies and yields: V tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x, (F tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h(x,y) for all x, y in V tensor_{K,sigma} C.

Finally, V tensor_{K,sigma} C = H^1 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C, and sigma(c) = q^m. Hence H^1 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x, (F tensor id)y) = q^m h(x,y) for all x, y. This is exactly the desired conclusion.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y->X. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L_X be cup product with xi, let L_Y be cup product with i^*xi, and let tr_X, tr_Y be the Poincare duality traces. For 0<=r<=d-2, put beta_X^r(x,y)=tr_X(L_X^{d-r}x cup y) and beta_Y^r(a,b)=tr_Y(L_Y^{d-1-r}a cup b). Then beta_X^r(x,y)=beta_Y^r(i^*x,i^*y) for all x,y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
Apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor to the F_{q^m}-variety X, renaming q^m as the prime power in that lemma. The hypotheses match: X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d, Y is a smooth effective divisor of pure dimension d-1, and ell != p. Under the fixed identification of Q_ell(1) with Q_ell, the lemma provides the Gysin map i_!: H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^{n+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) characterized by tr_X(i_! a cup b) = tr_Y(a cup i^* b) for a in H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) and b in H^{2d-2-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell), and it satisfies i_!(i^* z) = z cup xi for every z in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell). The traces in the lemma are exactly the Poincare duality traces tr_X and tr_Y of the statement, and xi is the same cycle class of Y.

Fix r with 0 <= r <= d-2 and x,y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Put z := L_X^{d-1-r} x. Since L_X is cup product with xi, z = xi^{d-1-r} cup x, and deg(z) = r + 2(d-1-r) = 2d-2-r. Pullback along i is a graded ring homomorphism for the cup product, so i^* z = (i^* xi)^{d-1-r} cup i^* x = L_Y^{d-1-r} i^* x. Let a := L_Y^{d-1-r} i^* x = i^* z. Then a lies in H^{2d-2-r}_et(Y_k,Q_ell), and y lies in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell); hence the characterizing identity applies with n = 2d-2-r. We get beta_Y^r(i^* x, i^* y) = tr_Y(L_Y^{d-1-r} i^* x cup i^* y) = tr_Y(a cup i^* y) = tr_X(i_! a cup y). The degree of a cup i^* y is 2d-2, the top degree of Y, and the degree of i_! a cup y is 2d, the top degree of X, so both traces are defined.

By the second formula in the cited lemma, i_! a = i_!(i^* z) = z cup xi = (L_X^{d-1-r} x) cup xi = L_X^{d-r} x. Substituting this into the last expression gives beta_Y^r(i^* x, i^* y) = tr_X(L_X^{d-r} x cup y) = beta_X^r(x, y). This proves the desired equality for all x,y and all r.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d->H^{d+2}). Let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d. Then the restriction of beta to P^d x P^d is nondegenerate.
proof:
The target lemma is a direct special case of the proved lemma `Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103` with the parameter $j=0$. Let me verify the hypotheses match precisely, then write the proof.

**Verification of hypotheses:**
- Target has $d\geq 2$, which satisfies $d\geq 1$ in 9d4103. ✓
- All other hypotheses (smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension $d$, very ample divisor class $\xi$, Lefschetz operator $L$, hard Lefschetz isomorphisms $L^{d-n}$, Poincaré duality pairing $ eta$ on $H^d$) are identical. ✓
- In 9d4103, $P^r = \ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r	o H^{2d-r+2})$; for $r=d$ this gives $P^d = \ker(L:H^d	o H^{d+2})$, matching the target. ✓
- With $j=0$: $W_0 = L^0\, P^{d-2\cdot 0} = L^0\, P^d = P^d$. ✓
- The conclusion of 9d4103 for $j=0$ is exactly: the restriction of $ eta$ to $P^d	imes P^d$ is nondegenerate. ✓

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/ca5a01",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We show that the target statement is a direct special case of the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103 with the index j = 0.

Recall the statement of Miner/16d24b0281973336/9d4103: Let q = p^a, ell != p, m >= 1, k = overline(F_q), d >= 1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. With Tate twists identified with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-n}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0 <= n <= d. For 0 <= r <= d put P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)), and for 0 <= j <= floor(d/2) put W_j = L^j P^{d-2j}. Let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell). Then the restriction of beta to W_j x W_j is nondegenerate for every j.

We now verify that every hypothesis of 9d4103 is satisfied under the hypotheses of the target lemma:

(1) The target assumes q = p^a, ell != p, m >= 1, k = overline(F_q), and d >= 2. Since d >= 2 implies d >= 1, the dimension hypothesis of 9d4103 is met.

(2) The target assumes X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. This matches the hypothesis of 9d4103 exactly.

(3) The target assumes xi is the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor and L is cup product with xi. This matches 9d4103 exactly (the identification of Tate twists with Q_ell is implicit in both statements since the cohomology is taken with Q_ell coefficients).

(4) The target assumes L^{d-n}: H^n -> H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0 <= n <= d, where H^s = H^s_et(X_k, Q_ell). This is precisely the hard Lefschetz hypothesis of 9d4103.

(5) The target defines P^d = ker(L: H^d -> H^{d+2}). In 9d4103, P^r = ker(L^{d-r+1}: H^r -> H^{2d-r+2}) for 0 <= r <= d. Setting r = d gives P^d = ker(L^{d-d+1}: H^d -> H^{2d-d+2}) = ker(L^1: H^d -> H^{d+2}) = ker(L: H^d -> H^{d+2}), which is exactly the P^d of the target.

(6) The target takes beta to be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d = H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell). This is the same pairing as in 9d4103.

Now we specialize 9d4103 to j = 0. Since 0 <= floor(d/2) (as d >= 2), the index j = 0 is in the allowed range. The corresponding subspace is W_0 = L^0 P^{d-2\cdot 0} = L^0 P^d = P^d, where L^0 denotes the identity map on H^d. The conclusion of 9d4103 for j = 0 states that the restriction of beta to W_0 x W_0 = P^d x P^d is nondegenerate.

This is precisely the conclusion of the target lemma. Hence the restriction of the Poincare duality pairing beta to P^d x P^d is nondegenerate.

For completeness, we remark on the substance of the cited result. The proof of 9d4103 (which in turn invokes Miner/16d24b0281973336/4b7666) proceeds by the standard Lefschetz-decomposition dimension argument: hard Lefschetz (the hypothesis L^{d-n} is an isomorphism for 0 <= n <= d) implies in particular that L^2: H^{d-2} -> H^{d+2} is an isomorphism, so L: H^{d-2} -> H^d is injective and L: H^d -> H^{d+2} is surjective. Let U = L H^{d-2} (so dim U = dim H^{d-2}). The self-adjointness of L with respect to the Poincare duality pairing (beta(x, Lz) = beta(Lx, z) for x in H^d, z in H^{d-2}, which follows from the associativity and graded commutativity of the cup product together with the definition beta(x,y) = tr_X(x cup y)) implies that U is contained in the orthogonal complement (P^d)^perp of P^d with respect to beta, because for x in P^d and y = Lz in U one has beta(x, y) = beta(Lx, z) = beta(0, z) = 0. By nondegeneracy of beta on H^d, dim (P^d)^perp = dim H^d - dim P^d = dim image(L: H^d -> H^{d+2}) = dim H^{d+2} = dim H^{d-2} = dim U (the last equality using Poincare duality between H^{d-2} and H^{d+2}). Hence U = (P^d)^perp. The radical of beta restricted to P^d x P^d is P^d ∩ (P^d)^perp = P^d ∩ U. If x lies in this intersection, then x = Lz for some z in H^{d-2} and Lx = 0, so L^2 z = 0, whence z = 0 by the injectivity of L^2, and x = 0. Thus the radical is trivial and the restriction is nondegenerate."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y->X. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L_X be cup product with xi, let L_Y be cup product with i^*xi, let tr_X, tr_Y be the Poincare duality traces, and let F_X, F_Y be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. For N>=1 and 0<=r<=d-1, put beta_X^r(x,y)=tr_X(L_X^{d-r}x cup y), beta_Y^r(a,b)=tr_Y(L_Y^{d-1-r}a cup b), G_N^X(x,y)=beta_X^r(x,F_X^N y)+(-1)^r q^{mrN} beta_X^r(x,F_X^{-N} y), and G_N^Y(a,b)=beta_Y^r(a,F_Y^N b)+(-1)^r q^{mrN} beta_Y^r(a,F_Y^{-N} b). Then G_N^X(x,y)=G_N^Y(i^*x,i^*y) for all x,y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof: Proof. Let q0 = q^m = p^{am}. Since q0 is a prime power, we apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor to X over F_{q0} and to the divisor Y, using the fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) as the identification of Tate twists. Write xi for the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell). For n >= 0 the Gysin map i_!: H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^{n+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) satisfies tr_X(i_! a cup b) = tr_Y(a cup i^* b) for every a in H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) and b in H^{2d-2-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell), and it satisfies i_!(i^* z) = z cup xi for every z in H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since Y is geometrically connected, the trace on Y_k in the cited lemma is the usual Poincare duality trace tr_Y. Fix x,y in H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Put z = L_X^{d-1-r} x = xi^{d-1-r} cup x. Then z lies in H^{2d-2-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell). By functoriality of pullback and cup product, i^* z = (i^* xi)^{d-1-r} cup i^* x = L_Y^{d-1-r} i^* x. Set a = i^* z and b = y. Because 0 <= r <= d-1, we have n = 2d-2-r >= 0 and b lies in H^{2d-2-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) = H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). The Gysin trace identity gives tr_X(i_! a cup y) = tr_Y(a cup i^* y). By the projection formula, i_! a = i_!(i^* z) = z cup xi = L_X^{d-r} x, since xi has degree 2. Therefore beta_X^r(x,y) = tr_X(L_X^{d-r} x cup y) = tr_Y(L_Y^{d-1-r} i^* x cup i^* y) = beta_Y^r(i^* x,i^* y). It remains to compare the Frobenius terms. Let sigma_X and sigma_Y be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius morphisms of X_k and Y_k. By the standard definition of the arithmetic Frobenius action on etale cohomology, F_X = sigma_X^* and F_Y = sigma_Y^*. Since i:Y -> X is defined over F_{q^m}, the base changed inclusion i_k:Y_k -> X_k satisfies sigma_X o i_k = i_k o sigma_Y, where o denotes composition. Pulling back this equality of morphisms gives i^* sigma_X^* = sigma_Y^* i^*, i.e. i^* F_X = F_Y i^*. The q^m-power Frobenius of the algebraically closed field k is an automorphism, so sigma_X and sigma_Y are automorphisms; hence the same equality holds after inversion and therefore for every integer N, i^* F_X^N = F_Y^N i^*. Apply the already proved pairing identity with y replaced by F_X^N y. We get beta_X^r(x,F_X^N y) = beta_Y^r(i^* x, i^* F_X^N y) = beta_Y^r(i^* x, F_Y^N i^* y). Apply it again with y replaced by F_X^{-N} y. We get beta_X^r(x,F_X^{-N} y) = beta_Y^r(i^* x, i^* F_X^{-N} y) = beta_Y^r(i^* x, F_Y^{-N} i^* y). Multiplying the second displayed equality by (-1)^r q^{mrN} and adding the first displayed equality yields G_N^X(x,y) = G_N^Y(i^* x,i^* y). Since x and y were arbitrary, this proves the lemma.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, let i:Y->X be the inclusion, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Then i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules.
proof: Let Q = q^m. Since d >= 2, the integer n = d-2 satisfies 0 <= n <= d-1 and n < d-1. The divisor Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, hence it is a nonempty effective very ample Cartier divisor of pure dimension d-1 over F_Q. By the proved lemma Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/258fa8, applied with base field F_Q and with n = d-2, the pullback i^*: H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces. Next we show that this isomorphism is compatible with Frobenius. Apply the proved lemma Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_283 with its base prime power replaced by Q = q^m. Its hypotheses hold: X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d >= 1 over F_Q, and Y is an effective ample Cartier divisor defined over F_Q and smooth of pure dimension d-1, because very ample implies ample and a divisor on a variety of pure dimension d has pure dimension d-1. Let U be the open complement of Y in X. The lemma gives the Gysin long exact sequence for (X,Y,U) and states that every map in it commutes with the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms of the terms. In particular, for n = d-2, the middle map i^* satisfies i^* F_X = F_Y i^*, where F_X and F_Y are the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms on H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell). These are exactly the Frobenius endomorphisms denoted F in the target statement. Finally, an invertible Q_ell-linear map that intertwines two endomorphisms is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules: if g is the inverse of i^*, then from i^* F_X = F_Y i^* we obtain F_X g = g F_Y by composing with g on the left and on the right. Thus g is also Q_ell[F]-linear, and i^* is an isomorphism in the category of Q_ell[F]-modules. This proves the claim.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let V and W be finite-dimensional K-vector spaces, let T_V in GL_K(V), let T_W in GL_K(W), let c in K^*, and let <,>:V x W -> K be a nondegenerate bilinear pairing such that <T_V v, T_W w> = c <v,w> for all v in V and w in W. If T_W is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K, then T_V is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K.
proof:
Fix an algebraic closure Kbar of K. We prove that T_V \otimes 1 is diagonalizable over Kbar; this is exactly the statement that T_V is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K. (We work directly with explicit eigenvector bases over Kbar, so no minimal-polynomial criterion is invoked.)

Step 1 (the pairing identifies V with W^*). Define \varphi: V -> W^* by (\varphi(v))(w) = <v,w> for v in V, w in W. It is K-linear.
- \varphi is injective: if \varphi(v) = 0 then <v,w> = 0 for every w in W, so by nondegeneracy in the first variable v = 0.
- Define \psi: W -> V^* by (\psi(w))(v) = <v,w>. If \psi(w) = 0 then <v,w> = 0 for every v in V, so by nondegeneracy in the second variable w = 0; hence \psi is injective.
- From \varphi injective, dim V <= dim W^* = dim W. From \psi injective, dim W <= dim V^* = dim V. Hence dim V = dim W =: n.
- \varphi: V -> W^* is injective and dim V = dim W^* = n, so \varphi is an isomorphism of K-vector spaces.

Step 2 (the similitude is a conjugacy). For v in V, w in W:
(\varphi T_V v)(w) = <T_V v, w>.
Since T_W in GL_K(W), write w = T_W u with u = T_W^{-1} w. By the similitude hypothesis,
<T_V v, w> = <T_V v, T_W u> = c <v, u> = c <v, T_W^{-1} w>.
Now c <v, T_W^{-1} w> = c (\varphi v)(T_W^{-1} w), and by the definition of the dual map, ((T_W^{-1})^* (\varphi v))(w) = (\varphi v)(T_W^{-1} w). Hence
(\varphi T_V v)(w) = c ((T_W^{-1})^* (\varphi v))(w)
for every w in W, so \varphi T_V v = c (T_W^{-1})^* (\varphi v) for every v in V. Thus
\varphi T_V = c (T_W^{-1})^* \varphi   (*)
and, since \varphi is an isomorphism,
T_V = c \varphi^{-1} (T_W^{-1})^* \varphi   (**).
So T_V is K-conjugate to the endomorphism c (T_W^{-1})^* of W^*. (Note: we used only the definition of the dual map; we do not assert that A -> A^* is a homomorphism, and we do not need the identity (T_W^{-1})^* = (T_W^*)^{-1}.)

Step 3 (T_W^{-1} is diagonalizable over Kbar). By hypothesis T_W is diagonalizable over Kbar, so there is a Kbar-basis e_1,...,e_n of W_{Kbar} = W \otimes_K Kbar with T_W e_i = \lambda_i e_i (i = 1,...,n), \lambda_i in Kbar. Each \lambda_i != 0: if \lambda_i = 0 then T_W e_i = 0 with e_i != 0, contradicting invertibility of T_W. Then T_W^{-1} e_i = \lambda_i^{-1} e_i, so in the basis e_1,...,e_n the matrix of T_W^{-1} on W_{Kbar} is diag(\lambda_1^{-1},...,\lambda_n^{-1}), which is diagonal. Hence T_W^{-1} is diagonalizable over Kbar.

Step 4 ((T_W^{-1})^* is diagonalizable over Kbar). Let e^1,...,e^n be the dual basis of (W^*)_{Kbar} to e_1,...,e_n, i.e. e^i(e_j) = \delta_{ij}. For i, j in {1,...,n}, by the definition of the dual map,
((T_W^{-1})^* e^i)(e_j) = e^i(T_W^{-1} e_j) = e^i(\lambda_j^{-1} e_j) = \lambda_j^{-1} \delta_{ij}.
The right-hand side is the value on e_j of the functional \lambda_i^{-1} e^i, so (T_W^{-1})^* e^i = \lambda_i^{-1} e^i. Thus e^1,...,e^n is a Kbar-basis of eigenvectors of (T_W^{-1})^* on (W^*)_{Kbar} (eigenvalues \lambda_i^{-1}), so (T_W^{-1})^* is diagonalizable over Kbar.

Step 5 (c (T_W^{-1})^* is diagonalizable over Kbar). From Step 4, c (T_W^{-1})^* e^i = c \lambda_i^{-1} e^i (i = 1,...,n). Hence in the basis e^1,...,e^n the matrix of c (T_W^{-1})^* on (W^*)_{Kbar} is diag(c \lambda_1^{-1},...,c \lambda_n^{-1}), which is diagonal. So c (T_W^{-1})^* is diagonalizable over Kbar.

Step 6 (T_V is diagonalizable over Kbar). Base change (*) to Kbar: the isomorphism \varphi extends to an isomorphism \varphi_{Kbar}: V_{Kbar} -> (W^*)_{Kbar} (base change preserves isomorphisms), and (*) becomes
\varphi_{Kbar} (T_V \otimes 1) = c ((T_W^{-1})^* \otimes 1) \varphi_{Kbar}.
By Step 5, c ((T_W^{-1})^* \otimes 1) is diagonalizable over Kbar: its matrix in the basis e^1 \otimes 1,...,e^n \otimes 1 is the diagonal matrix diag(c \lambda_1^{-1},...,c \lambda_n^{-1}). Since \varphi_{Kbar} is an isomorphism, T_V \otimes 1 is Kbar-conjugate to c ((T_W^{-1})^* \otimes 1), namely
T_V \otimes 1 = c \varphi_{Kbar}^{-1} ((T_W^{-1})^* \otimes 1) \varphi_{Kbar},
so T_V \otimes 1 is diagonalizable over Kbar (conjugate operators over Kbar share diagonalizability: if S = P D P^{-1} with D diagonal, then c \varphi_{Kbar}^{-1} S \varphi_{Kbar} = (\varphi_{Kbar}^{-1} P) (cD) (P^{-1} \varphi_{Kbar}) is a conjugate of the diagonal matrix cD).

This proves T_V is diagonalizable over the algebraic closure Kbar of K. QED.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, 0<=r<d, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y->X. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L_X be cup product with xi, let L_Y be cup product with i^*xi, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Put P_X=ker(L_X^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)) and P_Y=ker(L_Y^{d-r}:H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)). Suppose i^*(P_X) is contained in P_Y and i^*|_{P_X}:P_X->P_Y is an injective homomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules. Let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If P_Y tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y) for all x,y, then P_X tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_X with h_X((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h_X(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
Proof. We show that the positive definite Hermitian form h on P_Y ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C pulls back along the injective Q_ell[F]-module map i^*|_{P_X}: P_X → P_Y to a positive definite Hermitian form h_X on P_X ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C with the same Frobenius scaling q^{mr}.

Step 0 (Finiteness). The etale cohomology groups H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) and H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces (finitude of etale cohomology of smooth projective varieties). Since P_X ⊆ H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) and P_Y ⊆ H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) are Q_ell-subspaces, P_X and P_Y are finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector spaces. Hence V := P_X ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C and W := P_Y ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C are finite-dimensional C-vector spaces.

Step 1 (The map f and the base-changed map φ). Let f = i^*|_{P_X}: P_X → P_Y be the restriction of the pullback i^*: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) → H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) to P_X. By hypothesis, i^*(P_X) ⊆ P_Y, so f is well-defined; f is Q_ell-linear (restriction of a Q_ell-linear map); f is injective (hypothesis); and f is a Q_ell[F]-module homomorphism, i.e. f(Fx) = Ff(x) for every x ∈ P_X, where F on P_X and P_Y denotes the restriction of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. (The statement that f is a Q_ell[F]-module homomorphism presupposes, and we use, that F(P_X) ⊆ P_X and F(P_Y) ⊆ P_Y so that F restricts to both spaces.)

Define φ: V → W by φ(x ⊗ c) = f(x) ⊗ c for x ∈ P_X, c ∈ C, extended C-linearly. Well-definedness: for λ ∈ Q_ell, φ((λx) ⊗ c) = f(λx) ⊗ c = (λ f(x)) ⊗ c = f(x) ⊗ σ(λ) c = φ(x ⊗ σ(λ) c) = φ((x ⊗ 1)(σ(λ) c)), where the third equality uses Q_ell-linearity of f and the fourth uses the defining relation of the tensor product P_X ⊗_{Q_ell} C (with C as a Q_ell-algebra via σ). Thus φ is well-defined and C-linear by construction.

Step 2 (φ is injective). Let {e_i}_{i=1}^n be a Q_ell-basis of P_X (finite since P_X is finite-dimensional). Then {e_i ⊗ 1}_{i=1}^n is a C-basis of V. Since f is injective, {f(e_i)}_{i=1}^n is Q_ell-linearly independent in P_Y. Extend {f(e_i)}_{i=1}^n to a Q_ell-basis {f(e_i)}_{i=1}^n ∪ {w_j}_{j=1}^m of P_Y (possible since P_Y is finite-dimensional and any linearly independent set extends to a basis). Then {f(e_i) ⊗ 1}_{i=1}^n ∪ {w_j ⊗ 1}_{j=1}^m is a C-basis of W. Now let v ∈ V with φ(v) = 0. Write v = Σ_{i=1}^n (e_i ⊗ 1) c_i for unique c_i ∈ C (finite sum, since {e_i ⊗ 1} is a C-basis of V). Then 0 = φ(v) = Σ_{i=1}^n (f(e_i) ⊗ 1) c_i. By linear independence of the C-basis {f(e_i) ⊗ 1}_{i=1}^n ∪ {w_j ⊗ 1}_{j=1}^m of W, we obtain c_i = 0 for every i. Hence v = 0, proving φ is injective.

Step 3 (Definition of h_X). Define h_X: V × V → C by h_X(v, w) = h(φ(v), φ(w)) for all v, w ∈ V, where h: W × W → C is the given positive definite Hermitian form on W.

Step 4 (h_X is a Hermitian form). We verify the three defining properties of a Hermitian form.

Step 4(a) (C-linearity in the first argument). Let a, b ∈ C and let x, z, z' ∈ V (all three are vectors in V). Since φ is C-linear, φ(ax + bz) = aφ(x) + bφ(z). Therefore
h_X(ax + bz, z') = h(φ(ax + bz), φ(z')) = h(aφ(x) + bφ(z), φ(z')) = a h(φ(x), φ(z')) + b h(φ(z), φ(z')) = a h_X(x, z') + b h_X(z, z'),
where the third equality uses C-linearity of h in its first argument. This shows h_X(ax + bz, z') = a h_X(x, z') + b h_X(z, z') for all a, b ∈ C and x, z, z' ∈ V, i.e. h_X is C-linear in its first argument.

Step 4(b) (Conjugate-linearity in the second argument). Let a, b ∈ C and let x, y, z' ∈ V (all three are vectors in V). Since φ is C-linear, φ(ay + bz') = aφ(y) + bφ(z'). Therefore
h_X(x, ay + bz') = h(φ(x), φ(ay + bz')) = h(φ(x), aφ(y) + bφ(z')) = ā h(φ(x), φ(y)) + b̄ h(φ(x), φ(z')) = ā h_X(x, y) + b̄ h_X(x, z'),
where the third equality uses conjugate-linearity of h in its second argument. This shows h_X(x, ay + bz') = ā h_X(x, y) + b̄ h_X(x, z') for all a, b ∈ C and x, y, z' ∈ V, i.e. h_X is conjugate-linear in its second argument.

Step 4(c) (Conjugate symmetry). For any x, y ∈ V,
h_X(x, y) = h(φ(x), φ(y)) = overline{h(φ(y), φ(x))} = overline{h_X(y, x)},
where the middle equality uses conjugate symmetry of h. Thus h_X is conjugate symmetric.

Combining Steps 4(a)–4(c), h_X is a Hermitian form on V.

Step 5 (Positive definiteness). For any v ∈ V, h_X(v, v) = h(φ(v), φ(v)) ≥ 0, since h is positive definite on W. If h_X(v, v) = 0, then h(φ(v), φ(v)) = 0, hence φ(v) = 0 by positive definiteness of h, hence v = 0 by injectivity of φ (Step 2). Conversely, h_X(0, 0) = h(0, 0) = 0. Therefore h_X(v, v) > 0 for every nonzero v ∈ V, and h_X is positive definite.

Step 6 (Frobenius compatibility). Let F_V = F ⊗ id: V → V and F_W = F ⊗ id: W → W denote the base-changed Frobenius actions. We first verify that φ intertwines F_V and F_W. For a simple tensor v = x ⊗ c ∈ V (x ∈ P_X, c ∈ C),
φ(F_V v) = φ((Fx) ⊗ c) = f(Fx) ⊗ c = Ff(x) ⊗ c = F_W(f(x) ⊗ c) = F_W(φ(v)),
where the third equality uses F-linearity of f, namely f(Fx) = Ff(x). Since both sides are C-linear in v, this identity extends to all v ∈ V: φ(F_V v) = F_W φ(v) for every v ∈ V.

Now for any x, y ∈ V,
h_X(F_V x, F_V y) = h(φ(F_V x), φ(F_V y)) = h(F_W φ(x), F_W φ(y)) = q^{mr} h(φ(x), φ(y)) = q^{mr} h_X(x, y),
where the third equality uses the Frobenius compatibility of h, namely h((F_W)u, (F_W)v) = q^{mr} h(u, v) for all u, v ∈ W, applied with u = φ(x) and v = φ(y).

Conclusion. We have constructed a positive definite Hermitian form h_X on V = P_X ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C satisfying h_X((F ⊗ id)x, (F ⊗ id)y) = q^{mr} h_X(x, y) for all x, y ∈ V. This completes the proof. ∎

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Then H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the direct sum of L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) and P^d.
proof: Let U=H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell), V=H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), and T=H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell). Write A:U->V and B:V->T for the two maps both given by cup product with xi, i.e. A=L on H^{d-2} and B=L on H^d. Then B composed with A is cup product with xi^2, i.e. L^2. Since d>=2, the integer n=d-2 lies in the range 0<=n<=d, and the hypothesis gives that C:=B composed with A:U->T is an isomorphism. Set W=L H^{d-2}=im(A) and P=P^d=ker(B). First we show W intersect P is {0}. If z is in W intersect P, then z=A(u) for some u in U. Because z is in P, B(z)=0. Hence C(u)=B(A(u))=0. Since C is injective, u=0, and therefore z=0. Next we show V=W+P. Take any v in V. Put y=B(v) in T. Since C is surjective, choose u in U with C(u)=y. Let w=A(u) in W. Then B(w)=C(u)=y=B(v), so B(v-w)=0. Thus v-w is in P, and v=w+(v-w) lies in W+P. We have shown W intersect P is {0} and V=W+P. Hence V is the direct sum W direct sum P. In the notation of the lemma, H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)=L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) direct sum P^d. The previously rejected step is avoided: this proof does not use orthogonal complements, perfectness of a pairing, or any double-orthogonal identity. In particular, no inference of the form (A^perp)^perp=A is made. For completeness, if one does use the Poincare duality pairing beta(x,y)=tr(x cup y) on H^d, graded commutativity of the etale cohomology ring gives beta(x,y)=(-1)^{d^2} beta(y,x), so the double-orthogonal identity would be valid; but it is not needed here.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, let i:Y->X be the inclusion, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Then for every integer r with 0<=r<=d-2, the homomorphism i^*:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules.
proof:
Fix an integer r with 0 <= r <= d-2. We prove that the restriction map i^*: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules, where F denotes the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius.

Step 1 (i^* is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces). We invoke the Lefschetz hyperplane theorem, lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/0d5e83, which states: for q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, a smooth projective geometrically connected variety X of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and a smooth ample divisor Y on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, the restriction map i^*: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer n with 0 <= n < d-1. We check the hypotheses: X is smooth, projective, geometrically connected, of pure dimension d >= 2 over F_{q^m} (given); Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} (given), and a very ample divisor is in particular an ample divisor, so Y satisfies the 'smooth ample divisor ... geometrically connected' hypothesis of the lemma. Hence, for every n with 0 <= n < d-1, i^*: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces. Because d >= 2 we have d-1 >= 1, so the inequality 0 <= n < d-1 is equivalent to 0 <= n <= d-2. In particular, for our fixed r with 0 <= r <= d-2, the map i^*: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces.

Step 2 (i^* is F-linear). We show i^* F_X = F_Y i^*, where F_X and F_Y are the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenii on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) and H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) respectively. Recall that the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is the action of the element Frob_ar of the Galois group Gal(overline(F_q) / F_{q^m}) on the cohomology, where Frob_ar is the automorphism of overline(F_q) given by t -> t^{q^m} (the geometric Frobenius is its inverse t -> t^{-q^m}).

The Galois group Gal(overline(F_q) / F_{q^m}) acts on X_k = X x_{F_{q^m}} overline(F_q) by acting on the overline(F_q) factor: for sigma in the Galois group, the morphism sigma: X_k -> X_k is (x, t) -> (x, sigma(t)). This induces the Galois action on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) (pullback along sigma), and in particular Frob_ar induces F_X. Similarly the Galois group acts on Y_k, and Frob_ar induces F_Y.

The closed immersion i_k: Y_k -> X_k, the base change of i: Y -> X to overline(F_q), is Gal(overline(F_q) / F_{q^m})-equivariant: for every sigma in the Galois group, i_k o sigma_Y = sigma_X o i_k. Indeed, writing sigma_X and sigma_Y for the Galois actions on X_k and Y_k, we have i_k(y, t) = (i(y), t), so (sigma_X o i_k)(y, t) = sigma_X(i(y), t) = (i(y), sigma(t)) = i_k(y, sigma(t)) = (i_k o sigma_Y)(y, t), as required.

By the functoriality of etale cohomology, which is contravariant in the scheme (a morphism f: A -> B induces f^*: H^r(B) -> H^r(A), and (f o g)^* = g^* o f^*), the equality of morphisms i_k o sigma_Y = sigma_X o i_k implies the equality of the induced maps on cohomology, sigma_Y^* o i^* = i^* o sigma_X^*, for every sigma in the Galois group. Taking sigma = Frob_ar, we obtain F_Y o i^* = i^* o F_X, i.e. i^* F_X = F_Y i^*. Thus i^* is a homomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules.

Step 3 (Conclusion). From Step 1, i^* is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces; from Step 2, i^* is F-linear, i^* F_X = F_Y i^*. We claim i^* is therefore an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules. It is a bijection of underlying Q_ell-vector spaces and is F-linear by construction. It remains to note that its inverse (i^*)^{-1}: H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) -> H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) is also F-linear: starting from i^* F_X = F_Y i^*, compose on the left with (i^*)^{-1} and on the right with (i^*)^{-1} to obtain (i^*)^{-1} F_Y = F_X (i^*)^{-1}. Hence i^* is an isomorphism in the category of Q_ell[F]-modules.

Since r with 0 <= r <= d-2 was arbitrary, the map i^*: H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules for every such r. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), n>=1, and let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension n over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mn}h(x,y) for all x,y, then H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h' with h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(n-2)}h'(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Let V = H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ell) and put V_sigma = V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C; write V(-1)_sigma for V(-1) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. Let F_V be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on V, and let T = F_V tensor id_C. The hypothesis is h(Tx,Ty)=q^{mn}h(x,y) for all x,y in V_sigma. We first determine the scalar by which the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acts on Q_ell(-1). Let G = Gal(k/F_{q^m}); it is procyclic and is generated by the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F_{q^m}, defined on k by x -> x^{q^m}. For each r>=1, since ell != p, mu_{ell^r}(k) is cyclic of order ell^r and F_{q^m} sends zeta to zeta^{q^m}, an automorphism because q^m is invertible modulo ell^r. The ell-adic cyclotomic character chi_ell: G -> Z_ell^* is defined by F_{q^m}(zeta_{ell^r}) = zeta_{ell^r}^{chi_ell(F_{q^m}) mod ell^r} for a compatible system of primitive roots. Since chi_ell(F_{q^m}) is congruent to q^m modulo ell^r for every r, it equals q^m in Z_ell. With the standard normalization of the Tate twist, Q_ell(1) is the one-dimensional Q_ell-representation on which G acts through chi_ell, and Q_ell(-1) is its dual. Hence F_{q^m} acts on Q_ell(1) by multiplication by q^m, and on Q_ell(-1) by multiplication by q^{-m}. Because q^m lies in Q, the embedding sigma fixes it, so after base change to C the scalar is still q^{-m}. Choose a Q_ell-basis e of Q_ell(-1) and let theta: V(-1) -> V be the Q_ell-linear isomorphism theta(v tensor a e)=a v. Its base change theta_sigma: V(-1)_sigma -> V_sigma is a C-linear isomorphism. If T' denotes the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on V(-1)_sigma, then T' is the base change of F_V tensor F_{Q_ell(-1)}, and the preceding paragraph gives F_{Q_ell(-1)}=q^{-m}; therefore theta_sigma o T' = q^{-m} o T o theta_sigma. Now define h' on V(-1)_sigma by h'(x,y)=h(theta_sigma(x),theta_sigma(y)). Since theta_sigma is an isomorphism and h is Hermitian, h' is Hermitian; since h is positive definite, h' is positive definite, because if x != 0 then theta_sigma(x) != 0 and h'(x,x)=h(theta_sigma(x),theta_sigma(x))>0.
