Finally, for all x,y in V(-1)_sigma, h'(T'x,T'y)=h(theta_sigma(T'x),theta_sigma(T'y))=h(q^{-m}Ttheta_sigma(x),q^{-m}Ttheta_sigma(y))=q^{-2m}h(Ttheta_sigma(x),Ttheta_sigma(y))=q^{-2m}q^{mn}h(theta_sigma(x),theta_sigma(y))=q^{m(n-2)}h'(x,y). The factor q^{-2m} appears because q^{-m} is a positive real scalar, so a Hermitian form sees it as |q^{-m}|^2=q^{-2m}. The last equality uses -2m+mn=m(n-2). This proves the required identity. If V is the zero space, the same construction gives the unique Hermitian form on the zero space and the identity is vacuous.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let beta be a nondegenerate bilinear form on V, let c in K^*, and let T in GL_K(V) satisfy beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y) for all x,y in V. Then, for every eigenvalue alpha of T over an algebraic closure of K, c/alpha is also an eigenvalue of T over that algebraic closure with the same algebraic multiplicity.
proof: Let n=dim_K V. If n=0, T has no eigenvalues, so the assertion is vacuous; hence assume n>=1. Let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K. Choose a K-basis of V and identify V with K^n. There is a unique n x n matrix S such that beta(x,y)=x^T S y for all column vectors x,y. The matrix S is invertible: if S were singular, there would be a nonzero column vector v with S v=0. Then beta(x,v)=x^T S v=0 for every x, contradicting nondegeneracy of beta (for v nonzero there must exist x with beta(x,v) != 0). Let A be the matrix of T; since T is in GL(V), A is invertible. The condition beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y) says (A x)^T S (A y)=c x^T S y for all x,y, so A^T S A=c S. Left-multiply this identity by S^{-1} and right-multiply by A^{-1}; this gives S^{-1} A^T S=c A^{-1}. Put A^*=S^{-1} A^T S. Then A^*=c A^{-1}. Also A^* is similar to A^T because A^*=S^{-1} A^T S. Since det(zI-A^T)=det((zI-A)^T)=det(zI-A), A^T and A have the same characteristic polynomial. Therefore chi_{cA^{-1}}(z)=chi_A(z). Let f(z)=chi_A(z). For z != 0 we compute f(z)=det(zI-cA^{-1})=det(A^{-1}) det(zA-cI)=det(A)^{-1} det(zA-cI). Now zA-cI=z(A-c z^{-1} I), so det(zA-cI)=z^n det(A-c z^{-1} I). Since A-c z^{-1} I=-(c z^{-1} I-A), det(A-c z^{-1} I)=(-1)^n det(c z^{-1} I-A)=(-1)^n f(c/z). Hence, with C=(-1)^n det(A)^{-1} (a nonzero scalar), f(z)=C z^n f(c/z) for all z != 0. Let alpha_1,...,alpha_n be the eigenvalues of A in Kbar, counted with algebraic multiplicity. Then f(z)=prod_{i=1}^n (z-alpha_i), and each alpha_i is nonzero because A is invertible. For z != 0, f(z)=C z^n prod_{i=1}^n (c/z-alpha_i)=C prod_{i=1}^n (c-alpha_i z)=C (-1)^n (prod_{i=1}^n alpha_i) prod_{i=1}^n (z-c/alpha_i). The product of the alpha_i equals det(A): indeed f(0)=prod_{i=1}^n (-alpha_i)=(-1)^n prod_{i=1}^n alpha_i, while f(0)=det(-A)=(-1)^n det(A). Since C=(-1)^n det(A)^{-1}, the scalar factor C (-1)^n prod_{i=1}^n alpha_i is 1. Thus for all z != 0, f(z)=prod_{i=1}^n (z-c/alpha_i). The right-hand side is a polynomial in z, and it agrees with the polynomial f(z) on the infinite set of nonzero elements of Kbar; hence the equality holds as a polynomial identity. Therefore prod_{i=1}^n (z-alpha_i)=prod_{i=1}^n (z-c/alpha_i) in Kbar[z]. Consequently the multiset of roots {alpha_1,...,alpha_n} equals the multiset {c/alpha_1,...,c/alpha_n}. Hence, if alpha is any eigenvalue of A, its algebraic multiplicity (the number of i with alpha_i=alpha) equals the number of i with c/alpha_i=alpha, i.e. with alpha_i=c/alpha; this is exactly the algebraic multiplicity of c/alpha. This proves the claim.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y->X. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L_X be cup product with xi, let L_Y be cup product with i^*xi, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on both cohomologies. Suppose i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective. Put P_X=ker(L_X:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)) and P_Y=ker(L_Y:H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)). Then i^* induces an injective homomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules P_X->P_Y.
proof:
We write H^r(X) = H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell) and H^r(Y) = H^r_et(Y_k, Q_ell), and let F_X and F_Y denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms on H^{d-1}(X) and H^{d-1}(Y) respectively (the target lemma's notation uses F for both).

**Step 1. F_X and F_Y are Q_ell-linear automorphisms.**
By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, applied to the scheme X over the finite field F_{q^m} (instantiating the lemma's prime power q with q^m, so that sigma is the (q^m)-power automorphism of k = overline(F_q)), the pullback F_X = (id_X x sigma)^* is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^{d-1}(X). Similarly, applying the same lemma to the scheme Y over F_{q^m}, F_Y = (id_Y x sigma)^* is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^{d-1}(Y).

**Step 2. Frobenius-Lefschetz commutation on X: F_X L_X = q^m L_X F_X on H^{d-1}(X).**
Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable to the smooth projective variety X over F_{q^m} of pure dimension d (instantiating the lemma's q with q^m), with the very ample divisor H = Y defined over F_{q^m}. The divisor Y is very ample by hypothesis, so the lemma applies with xi = cl(Y), L = L_X (cup product with xi). The lemma's first conclusion gives F_X o L_X = q^m L_X o F_X on every H^m(X), in particular on H^{d-1}(X).

**Step 3. F_X(P_X) is contained in P_X.**
Let x in P_X, so L_X x = 0. From Step 2, F_X L_X = q^m L_X F_X, equivalently L_X F_X = (1/q^m) F_X L_X. Since ell != p, the integer q^m is a unit in Q_ell, so 1/q^m is well-defined. Then
  L_X(F_X x) = (1/q^m) F_X(L_X x) = (1/q^m) F_X(0) = 0.
Hence F_X x in P_X, i.e. F_X(P_X) subset P_X.

**Step 4. O_Y(Y) is very ample on Y.**
Since O_X(Y) is very ample on X, there exists a closed immersion j: X -> P^n_{F_{q^m}} such that O_X(Y) = j^* O_{P^n}(1) = O_{P^n}(1)|_X (this is the standard characterization of very ample line bundles). Since X has pure dimension d >= 2, the image j(X) has dimension d, so n >= d >= 2. The composition (j|_Y): Y -> P^n_{F_{q^m}} is a closed immersion (composition of the closed immersion i: Y -> X with the closed immersion j). Under this immersion,
  (j|_Y)^* O_{P^n}(1) = j^* O_{P^n}(1)|_Y = O_X(Y)|_Y = i^* O_X(Y) = O_Y(Y).
Therefore O_Y(Y) = O_{P^n}(1)|_Y, which is very ample on Y.

**Step 5. Existence of an effective F_{q^m}-rational divisor H_Y on Y in |O_Y(Y)| with cl(H_Y) = i^*xi.**
From Step 4, we have a closed immersion Y -> P^n_{F_{q^m}} with O_Y(Y) = O_{P^n}(1)|_Y. Let S = F_{q^m}[x_0, ..., x_n] be the homogeneous coordinate ring of P^n, and let S_1 = (x_0, ..., x_n) be its degree-1 part, identified with the dual of F_{q^m}^{n+1}. Let I(Y) be the homogeneous ideal of Y in S. Since Y is a nonempty closed subvariety of P^n (it has pure dimension d-1 >= 1), I(Y) is a proper ideal, i.e. I(Y) != S.

Suppose for contradiction that every linear form in S_1 vanishes on Y, i.e. S_1 subset I(Y). Since I(Y) is an ideal, it then contains every polynomial in the x_i, i.e. I(Y) contains S_{>=1} = the irrelevant ideal m. Since I(Y) is a proper ideal and S = F_{q^m} ⊕ S_{>=1}, the only proper ideal containing S_{>=1} is S_{>=1} itself (any larger ideal would be S). So I(Y) = S_{>=1} = m. But V(m) = empty in P^n (no point of P^n is annihilated by all coordinates), contradicting that Y = V(I(Y)) is nonempty. Hence S_1 is not contained in I(Y), so there exists a linear form l in S_1 \ I(Y), defined over F_{q^m}, that does not vanish identically on Y.

The hyperplane H' = V(l) = {P in P^n : l(P) = 0} is defined over F_{q^m} and does not contain Y (since l not in I(Y)). Set H_Y = H' ∩ Y. Then H_Y is the zero locus of the nonzero section l|_Y of O_{P^n}(1)|_Y = O_Y(Y). Since Y is smooth (hence regular, so every local ring is a domain), the nonzero section l|_Y is a non-zero-divisor at every point of Y, and H_Y is an effective Cartier divisor on Y defined over F_{q^m} with O_Y(H_Y) = O_Y(1) = O_Y(Y).

Moreover, H_Y is nonempty: if H_Y were empty, then l|_Y would be a nowhere-vanishing section of O_Y(1), making O_Y(1) trivial. But O_Y(1) is very ample on Y of dimension d-1 >= 1, so h^0(Y, O_Y(1)) >= dim(Y) + 1 >= 2, whereas a trivial line bundle on the connected variety Y has h^0 = 1, a contradiction.

The cycle class of H_Y satisfies cl(H_Y) = c_1(O_Y(H_Y)) = c_1(O_Y(1)) = c_1(O_Y(Y)) = c_1(i^* O_X(Y)) = i^* c_1(O_X(Y)) = i^* xi in H^2_et(Y_k, Q_ell) (using the identification of Tate twists with Q_ell). Thus the divisor H_Y is a very ample F_{q^m}-rational divisor on Y whose cycle class is i^*xi.

**Step 6. Frobenius-Lefschetz commutation on Y: F_Y L_Y = q^m L_Y F_Y on H^{d-1}(Y).**
Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable to the smooth projective variety Y over F_{q^m} of pure dimension d-1 (instantiating the lemma's q with q^m), with the very ample divisor H = H_Y defined over F_{q^m} (constructed in Step 5). The cycle class of H_Y is i^*xi, so the lemma's L is cup product with i^*xi, which is exactly L_Y. The lemma gives F_Y o L_Y = q^m L_Y o F_Y on every H^m(Y), in particular on H^{d-1}(Y).

**Step 7. F_Y(P_Y) is contained in P_Y.**
Let y in P_Y, so L_Y y = 0. From Step 6, F_Y L_Y = q^m L_Y F_Y, equivalently L_Y F_Y = (1/q^m) F_Y L_Y. Since ell != p, q^m is a unit in Q_ell. Then
  L_Y(F_Y y) = (1/q^m) F_Y(L_Y y) = (1/q^m) F_Y(0) = 0.
Hence F_Y y in P_Y, i.e. F_Y(P_Y) subset P_Y.

(Equivalently, by the "consequently" clause of eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable applied to Y of dimension d-1 with divisor H_Y: P^{d-1} = ker(L_Y^{(d-1)-(d-1)+1} : H^{d-1}(Y) -> H^{2(d-1)-(d-1)+2}(Y)) = ker(L_Y : H^{d-1}(Y) -> H^{d+1}(Y)) = P_Y, and the lemma states P^{d-1} is stable under F_Y, giving F_Y(P_Y) subset P_Y directly.)

**Step 8. i^*(P_X) is contained in P_Y and i^*|_{P_X} is injective.**
By Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_511: X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d >= 2 over F_{q^m}, and Y is a nonempty effective very ample Cartier divisor defined over F_{q^m}, smooth and geometrically connected of pure dimension d-1, with closed immersion i: Y -> X. All hypotheses are satisfied (Y is very ample by hypothesis, hence ample; it is effective as a divisor defined by a section; it is smooth and geometrically connected by hypothesis; it has pure dimension d-1; and it is nonempty since d-1 >= 1). The lemma concludes that i^* restricts to an injective Q_ell-linear homomorphism
  ker(L_X : H^{d-1}(X) -> H^{d+1}(X)) -> ker(L_Y : H^{d-1}(Y) -> H^{d+1}(Y)),
i.e. i^*(P_X) subset P_Y and i^*|_{P_X} : P_X -> P_Y is injective. (The target lemma's hypothesis that i^* : H^{d-1}(X) -> H^{d-1}(Y) is injective is not needed for this step, as lemma_511 provides the required injectivity directly.)

**Step 9. Frobenius commutation: i^* F_X = F_Y i^* on H^{d-1}(X).**
By Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_283, applied to X over F_{q^m} (instantiating the lemma's q with q^m): X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d >= 1 over F_{q^m}, and Y is an effective ample divisor defined over F_{q^m} and smooth of pure dimension d-1 (Y is very ample, hence ample). The lemma provides a long exact sequence ... -> H^n_c(U_k, Q_ell) -> H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) --i^*--> H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ell) -> H^{n+1}_c(U_k, Q_ell) -> ... in which every map commutes with the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms. In particular, the map i^* : H^{d-1}(X) -> H^{d-1}(Y) commutes with Frobenius:
  i^* o F_X = F_Y o i^*.

**Step 10. Conclusion: i^*|_{P_X} is an injective homomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules.**
We have established:
- i^*|_{P_X} : P_X -> P_Y is a Q_ell-linear map (Step 8), with i^*(P_X) subset P_Y.
- i^*|_{P_X} is injective (Step 8).
- For x in P_X: F_X x in P_X (Step 3), so F_X|_{P_X}(x) is defined; i^* x in P_Y (Step 8); and F_Y(i^* x) in P_Y (Step 7).
- i^*(F_X x) = F_Y(i^* x) by Step 9.

Therefore, for every x in P_X,
  i^*|_{P_X}(F_X|_{P_X}(x)) = i^*(F_X x) = F_Y(i^* x) = F_Y|_{P_Y}(i^*|_{P_X}(x)),
showing that i^*|_{P_X} commutes with the Frobenius action. Since i^*|_{P_X} is Q_ell-linear and commutes with F_X|_{P_X} and F_Y|_{P_Y}, it is a homomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules. Combined with injectivity (Step 8), i^* induces an injective homomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules P_X -> P_Y. ∎

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), n>=1, and let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension n over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If every eigenvalue of F on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mn/2}, then every eigenvalue of F on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(n-2)/2}.
proof: Let V=H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) and let F_V be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on V. Write W=H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)=V tensor Q_ell(-1). We first determine the scalar by which F acts on Q_ell(-1). In the convention used in the statement, Q_ell(1) is the ell-adic cyclotomic character, so the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acts on Q_ell(1) by q^m and on Q_ell(-1) by q^{-m}. For completeness, here is the computation. Let sigma:k->k be x->x^{q^m}. For r>=1 let mu_{ell^r} be the group of ell^r-th roots of unity in k. Because ell!=p and k is algebraically closed, mu_{ell^r} is cyclic of order ell^r, and sigma acts on it by zeta->zeta^{q^m}. Choose compatible primitive roots zeta_r in mu_{ell^r}. The isomorphism mu_{ell^r} -> Z/ell^rZ sending zeta_r to 1 is compatible with the transition maps mu_{ell^{r+1}} -> mu_{ell^r}, zeta -> zeta^ell. Under this identification, sigma sends 1 to q^m mod ell^r. Passing to the inverse limit Z_ell(1) of the system mu_{ell^r}, the induced action of sigma is multiplication by q^m in Z_ell; since ell!=p, q^m is a unit in Z_ell. Hence on Q_ell(1)=Q_ell tensor Z_ell(1) it is multiplication by q^m, and on the inverse twist Q_ell(-1) it is multiplication by q^{-m}. Let e be the chosen nonzero element of Q_ell(1), and let e^{-1} in Q_ell(-1) be its inverse under the canonical pairing Q_ell(1) tensor Q_ell(-1) -> Q_ell. By functoriality of Frobenius on tensor products, F_W = F_V tensor F_{Q_ell(-1)}. Identify W with V by v -> v tensor e^{-1}. Then for v in V, F_W(v tensor e^{-1}) = F_V(v) tensor F_{Q_ell(-1)}(e^{-1}) = F_V(v) tensor q^{-m} e^{-1} = q^{-m}(F_V(v) tensor e^{-1}). Thus under the identification, F_W is q^{-m} F_V. Consequently, if A is a matrix of F_V in a Q_ell-basis of V, a matrix of F_W in the corresponding basis is q^{-m}A. If alpha is an eigenvalue of F_V over overline(Q_ell), then q^{-m}alpha is an eigenvalue of F_W, and every eigenvalue of F_W arises in this way: indeed, if A v = alpha v for a nonzero vector v, then (q^{-m}A)v = q^{-m}alpha v; conversely, if (q^{-m}A)v = lambda v for a nonzero v, then A v = q^m lambda v, so alpha = q^m lambda is an eigenvalue of A. Let lambda be an eigenvalue of F_W. Then lambda=q^{-m}alpha for some eigenvalue alpha of F_V. By the hypothesis, |alpha|_Weil = q^{mn/2}. To compute the Weil absolute value of lambda, let L be the number field generated by alpha over the field Q of rational numbers (the hypothesis that alpha has a Weil absolute value means alpha is algebraic). The embeddings tau of L into C fix the rational number q^{-m}. Therefore |lambda|_Weil = (product over all embeddings tau of L into C of |tau(lambda)|)^{1/[L:Q]} = (product |q^{-m} tau(alpha)|)^{1/[L:Q]} = q^{-m} (product |tau(alpha)|)^{1/[L:Q]} = q^{-m} |alpha|_Weil = q^{-m} q^{mn/2} = q^{mn/2-m} = q^{m(n-2)/2}. This holds for every eigenvalue lambda of F_W. If V=0 there are no eigenvalues and the assertion is vacuous; otherwise the argument applies to each eigenvalue. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), n>=1, and let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension n over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Suppose F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) and every eigenvalue of F on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mn/2}. Then H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(n-2)}h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Let V = H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). This is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space by the standard finiteness of etale cohomology for smooth projective varieties over finite fields. The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F on V is invertible: since q^m is a prime power, apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a to Y over F_{q^m} (replacing q in that lemma by q^m); it says that pullback by the field automorphism x -> x^{q^m} of k = overline(F_q) is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Set c = q^{mn} in Q_ell^*. Since q^{mn} is a positive rational number, sigma(c) = q^{mn} > 0 and sqrt(sigma(c)) = q^{mn/2}. By hypothesis F is diagonalizable over the algebraic closure of Q_ell on V. Also every eigenvalue alpha of F has Weil absolute value q^{mn/2}; in the terminology used by the cited lemmas this means that for the chosen embedding sigma we have |sigma(alpha)| = q^{mn/2} = sqrt(sigma(c)) for every eigenvalue alpha. If V = 0 the desired conclusion is vacuous, and the following application of the cited lemmas is also valid in that zero-dimensional case. Apply Miner/16d24b0281973336/ccebfa with K = Q_ell, the vector space V, the automorphism F, and c = q^{mn}. It gives a positive definite Hermitian form h on V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C such that h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h(x,y) = q^{mn} h(x,y) for all x,y in V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. Now apply Miner/16d24b0281973336/f3da8d to Y, n, F, and sigma. Its hypothesis is exactly the existence of the positive definite Hermitian form h on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C with the scaling q^{mn} constructed above. It therefore yields a positive definite Hermitian form h' on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C such that h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = q^{m(n-2)} h'(x,y) for all x,y. The action of F on the twisted cohomology is the natural one compatible with the chosen identification of Q_ell(1) with Q_ell. Renaming h' as h gives the required form.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y->X. Let F_X and F_Y be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) and H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell), respectively. Suppose i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective and satisfies i^* F_X = F_Y i^*. Let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F_Y tensor id)x,(F_Y tensor id)y)=q^{m(d-1)}h(x,y), then H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_X with h_X((F_X tensor id)x,(F_X tensor id)y)=q^{m(d-1)}h_X(x,y).
proof:
Let V = H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k, Q_ell) and W = H^{d-1}_{et}(Y_k, Q_ell), and write V_C = V ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C and W_C = W ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C. By hypothesis i^*: V → W is an injective Q_ell-linear map satisfying i^* F_X = F_Y i^*, and W_C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F_Y⊗id)x, (F_Y⊗id)y) = q^{m(d-1)} h(x,y) for all x,y ∈ W_C. We construct the desired h_X on V_C by pullback.

Step 1 (i^* remains injective over C). The Q_ell-linear map i^* induces the C-linear map ι := i^* ⊗ id_C: V_C → W_C. We claim ι is injective. Let (e_1,...,e_n) be a Q_ell-basis of V, n = dim_{Q_ell} V. Since i^* is injective, the tuple (i^* e_1,...,i^* e_n) is linearly independent over Q_ell in W, so it extends to a Q_ell-basis (i^* e_1,...,i^* e_n, f_{n+1},...,f_N) of W. Under this choice, V_C = ⊕_{j=1}^n C·(e_j⊗1) and W_C = (⊕_{j=1}^n C·(i^* e_j⊗1)) ⊕ (⊕_{j=n+1}^N C·(f_j⊗1)) are direct sum decompositions, and ι(e_j⊗1) = i^* e_j⊗1 for j ≤ n. If x = Σ_{j=1}^n c_j (e_j⊗1) ∈ V_C satisfies ι x = 0, then Σ_{j=1}^n c_j (i^* e_j⊗1) = 0 in the direct sum W_C, which forces c_j = 0 for every j, hence x = 0. Thus ker ι = 0.

Step 2 (definition of h_X). Define h_X: V_C × V_C → C by h_X(x,y) := h(ι x, ι y) for all x,y ∈ V_C.

Step 3 (h_X is a Hermitian form). Let x, x', y, y' ∈ V_C and α, β ∈ C. Since ι is C-linear and h is sesquilinear (conjugate-linear in the first variable, linear in the second):
h_X(αx + βx', y) = h(α ι x + β ι x', ι y) = ᾱ h(ι x, ι y) + β̄ h(ι x', ι y) = ᾱ h_X(x,y) + β̄ h_X(x',y),
h_X(x, αy + βy') = h(ι x, α ι y + β ι y') = α h_X(x,y) + β h_X(x,y').
Moreover, using the Hermitian symmetry h(u,v) = overline{h(v,u)} of h:
h_X(x,y) = h(ι x, ι y) = overline{h(ι y, ι x)} = overline{h_X(y,x)}.
Thus h_X is a Hermitian form on V_C.

Step 4 (positive definiteness). Let x ∈ V_C be nonzero. By Step 1, ι x ≠ 0 in W_C. By the positive definiteness of h, h(ι x, ι x) ∈ R_{>0}. Hence h_X(x,x) = h(ι x, ι x) > 0. Therefore h_X is positive definite on V_C.

Step 5 (Frobenius relation). The hypothesis i^* F_X = F_Y i^* implies ι ∘ (F_X⊗id) = (F_Y⊗id) ∘ ι as C-linear maps V_C → W_C: indeed both sides are C-linear and agree on pure tensors v⊗c, where (ι∘(F_X⊗id))(v⊗c) = i^*F_X(v)⊗c = F_Y(i^*v)⊗c = ((F_Y⊗id)∘ι)(v⊗c), and pure tensors span V_C. Consequently, for all x,y ∈ V_C:
h_X((F_X⊗id)x, (F_X⊗id)y) = h(ι(F_X⊗id)x, ι(F_X⊗id)y) = h((F_Y⊗id)(ι x), (F_Y⊗id)(ι y)) = q^{m(d-1)} h(ι x, ι y) = q^{m(d-1)} h_X(x,y),
where the third equality is the hypothesis on h.

Conclusion. The form h_X defined in Step 2 is a positive definite Hermitian form on H^{d-1}_{et}(X_k, Q_ell) ⊗_{Q_ell,σ} C = V_C satisfying h_X((F_X⊗id)x, (F_X⊗id)y) = q^{m(d-1)} h_X(x,y) for all x,y, as required.

Remark. The argument uses only the two stated hypotheses on i^* (injectivity and the intertwining relation i^* F_X = F_Y i^*) together with the existence of h on W_C; the geometric hypotheses (smoothness, projectivity, very ampleness, geometric connectedness, d ≥ 3) are part of the context in which i^* arises and play no further role in this step. (The construction was additionally checked on a random finite-dimensional example with an injective intertwining map and a positive definite Hermitian form satisfying the Frobenius relation, confirming that the pullback is positive definite and inherits the relation.)

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Put P=ker(L^2:H^{d-1}->H^{d+3}). Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}, suppose F(P) is contained in P, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If H^{d-1} tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(d-1)}h(x,y), then P tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_P with h_P((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(d-1)}h_P(x,y).
proof:
Let $V = H^{d-1} \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$ and let $W = P \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$. Since $P$ is a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear subspace of $H^{d-1}$ (namely $P = \ker(L^2: H^{d-1} \to H^{d+3})$), the natural map $P \hookrightarrow H^{d-1}$ induces an injection $W \hookrightarrow V$, so we identify $W$ with the $\mathbb{C}$-subspace of $V$ spanned by elements $p \otimes 1$ for $p \in P$. In particular $W$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb{C}$-vector space.

Let $T = F \otimes \mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{C}} \in \mathrm{GL}_{\mathbb{C}}(V)$ be the induced action on $V$. We claim $T(W) \subseteq W$. Indeed, take any $w \in W$. Since $W$ is the $\mathbb{C}$-span of elements $p \otimes 1$ with $p \in P$, it suffices to check $T(p \otimes 1) \in W$ for $p \in P$. But $T(p \otimes 1) = F(p) \otimes 1$, and by the hypothesis $F(P) \subseteq P$, we have $F(p) \in P$, so $F(p) \otimes 1 \in W$. By $\mathbb{C}$-linearity, $T(W) \subseteq W$.

Now define $h_P = h|_{W \times W}$, the restriction of $h$ to $W$. We verify that $h_P$ satisfies all required properties.

**Step 1: $h_P$ is a Hermitian form on $W$.**

For $x, y \in W$ and $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{C}$:
- Sesquilinearity in the first variable: $h_P((\alpha x + \beta y), z) = h(\alpha x + \beta y, z) = \alpha\, h(x,z) + \beta\, h(y,z) = \alpha\, h_P(x,z) + \beta\, h_P(y,z)$, since $x, y, z \in W \subseteq V$ and $h$ is sesquilinear on $V$.
- Sesquilinearity in the second variable: $h_P(x, \alpha y + \beta z) = h(x, \alpha y + \beta z) = \overline{\alpha}\, h(x,y) + \overline{\beta}\, h(x,z) = \overline{\alpha}\, h_P(x,y) + \overline{\beta}\, h_P(x,z)$.
- Hermitian symmetry: $h_P(y,x) = h(y,x) = \overline{h(x,y)} = \overline{h_P(x,y)}$.

Thus $h_P$ is a Hermitian form on $W$.

**Step 2: $h_P$ is positive definite.**

Let $x \in W$ with $x \neq 0$. Since $W \subseteq V$ and $h$ is positive definite on $V$, we have $h(x,x) > 0$. But $h(x,x) = h_P(x,x)$ because $x \in W$. Hence $h_P(x,x) > 0$ for every nonzero $x \in W$, so $h_P$ is positive definite.

**Step 3: The scaling relation holds on $W$.**

Let $x, y \in W$. Since $T(W) \subseteq W$ (established above), $T(x) \in W$ and $T(y) \in W$. The hypothesis on $h$ states that for all $u, v \in V$,
$$h(Tu, Tv) = q^{m(d-1)}\, h(u,v).$$
Applying this to $u = x$ and $v = y$ (both in $W \subseteq V$), we get
$$h(Tx, Ty) = q^{m(d-1)}\, h(x,y).$$
Since $x, y, Tx, Ty \in W$, the left-hand side is $h_P(Tx, Ty)$ and the right-hand side is $q^{m(d-1)}\, h_P(x,y)$. Therefore
$$h_P((F \otimes \mathrm{id})\, x,\, (F \otimes \mathrm{id})\, y) = q^{m(d-1)}\, h_P(x,y)$$
for all $x, y \in W = P \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$.

**Conclusion.** The form $h_P = h|_{W \times W}$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $P \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma} \mathbb{C}$ satisfying $h_P((F \otimes \mathrm{id})\, x,\, (F \otimes \mathrm{id})\, y) = q^{m(d-1)}\, h_P(x,y)$ for all $x, y$. This completes the proof. $\blacksquare$

Remark on the role of the hypotheses: The assumption that $L^{d-n}: H^n \to H^{2d-n}$ is an isomorphism for $0 \leq n \leq d$ (a form of the Hodge conjecture) and the specific definition $P = \ker(L^2: H^{d-1} \to H^{d+3})$ are part of the geometric setup that motivates the lemma and ensures $P$ is a meaningful cohomological subspace. However, the logical implication stated — that a positive definite Hermitian form with the Frobenius-scaling relation on $H^{d-1} \otimes \mathbb{C}$ restricts to the $F$-stable subspace $P \otimes \mathbb{C}$ with the same relation — depends only on: (i) $P$ being a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-subspace of $H^{d-1}$, (ii) $F(P) \subseteq P$, and (iii) the stated properties of $h$. These are exactly the facts used in Steps 1–3 above.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Let 0<=r<=d and 0<=j<=d-r, put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}), let L^j P^r be the image of P^r under L^j, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose F(P^r) is contained in P^r, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mr}h(x,y), then L^j P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_j with h_j((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(r+2j)}h_j(x,y).
proof: Let V = P^r and W = L^j V. If W = 0, the zero Hermitian form on the zero vector space satisfies the required identity vacuously, so assume W != 0. Put c = q^(mr) and let V_C = V tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. Write T for the operator F|_V tensor id on V_C. The given form h is positive definite Hermitian on V_C and satisfies h(Tx,Ty)=c h(x,y). First we show T is diagonalizable over C and every eigenvalue of T has complex absolute value q^(mr/2). If Tx=0, then 0=h(Tx,Tx)=c h(x,x), so x=0; hence T is invertible. Let T^* be the adjoint of T with respect to h, i.e. h(Tx,y)=h(x,T^* y). Then h(Tx,Ty)=h(x,T^* T y)=c h(x,y), so T^* T = c I. Since T is invertible, T^* = c T^(-1), and therefore T T^* = c I. Thus T is normal, and by the spectral theorem for normal operators over C it is diagonalizable over C. If lambda is an eigenvalue and 0 != x is a corresponding eigenvector, then |lambda|^2 h(x,x)=h(Tx,Tx)=c h(x,x), so |lambda|=q^(mr/2). We now use the standard action of Frobenius on the divisor class. The cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational divisor is fixed by arithmetic Frobenius in H^2(X_k,Q_ell(1)) because the cycle class map is defined over F_{q^m}; under the fixed identification Q_ell(1)=Q_ell the Frobenius action on the Tate twist is multiplication by q^(-m), so in untwisted cohomology F(xi)=q^m xi. Since F is a ring automorphism of the cohomology ring, F(Lz)=F(xi cup z)=F(xi) cup F(z)=q^m L(Fz) for all z, and by induction F(L^j u)=q^(mj) L^j(Fu). Because F(P^r) is contained in P^r, W is F-stable: for w=L^j u, Fw=q^(mj)L^j(Fu) lies in W. Let S = L^j|_V : V -> H^(r+2j); then W = im(S). Let K = ker(S). From F S = q^(mj) S F, K is F-stable: if u in K, then S(Fu)=q^(-mj)F(Su)=0. Thus F induces T_bar on V/K by T_bar([u])=[Fu]. Pass to C. Since S is defined over Q_ell, K_C = K tensor C = ker(S_C) and W_C = im(S_C), and the map V_C/K_C -> W_C, [u] -> S_C(u), is an isomorphism. The operator T on V_C is diagonalizable, so V_C is the direct sum of its eigenspaces E_lambda. Because K_C is T-stable and the eigenspace projections are polynomials in T, K_C is the direct sum of K_C cap E_lambda over lambda. Hence V_C/K_C is the direct sum of E_lambda/(K_C cap E_lambda), and T_bar acts on the summand corresponding to lambda as multiplication by lambda. Therefore T_bar is diagonalizable over C, and its eigenvalues are a subset of the eigenvalues of T, each of modulus q^(mr/2). Under the isomorphism V_C/K_C -> W_C, the operator F|_W corresponds to q^(mj) T_bar, because F(S_C(u))=q^(mj)S_C(Fu). Hence F|_W is diagonalizable over C, and its eigenvalues are q^(mj) lambda for lambda an eigenvalue of T_bar. Each such eigenvalue has modulus q^(mj) q^(mr/2)=q^(m(r+2j)/2). Choose a C-basis e_1,...,e_N of W_C consisting of eigenvectors of F|_W, with eigenvalues mu_1,...,mu_N. By the preceding paragraph, |mu_i|=q^(m(r+2j)/2) for every i. Define a Hermitian form h_j on W_C by h_j(sum a_i e_i, sum b_i e_i)=sum a_i conj(b_i). This form is positive definite: if x=sum a_i e_i is nonzero, then some a_i is nonzero and h_j(x,x)=sum |a_i|^2 > 0. It is Hermitian because its matrix in the basis e_i is the identity. Finally, for x=sum a_i e_i and y=sum b_i e_i, h_j(Fx,Fy)=sum mu_i conj(mu_i) a_i conj(b_i)=q^(m(r+2j)) sum a_i conj(b_i)=q^(m(r+2j)) h_j(x,y). This is the desired positive definite Hermitian form on L^j P^r tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), n>=1, and let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension n over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(n-2)}h(x,y), then H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h' with h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{mn}h'(x,y).
proof: Let U = H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1). The usual definition of Tate twists gives a canonical isomorphism U tensor_{Q_ell} Q_ell(1) -> H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell). Let e be the fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1), and use it to identify H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) with U by sending u tensor e to u. Write F_U for the Frobenius on U. By the standard Tate-twist convention used in the statement, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acts on Q_ell(1) by multiplication by q^m; explicitly, it raises the compatible system of ell-power roots of unity to the q^m-th power, which is multiplication by q^m on that one-dimensional Q_ell-representation. Hence F_{Q_ell(1)}(e) = q^m e. Therefore, under the identification above, the Frobenius F on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is q^m times F_U: for u in U, F(u tensor e) = F_U(u) tensor q^m e = q^m (F_U(u) tensor e). Let U_C = U tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C and V_C = H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. The hypothesis gives a positive definite Hermitian form h on U_C with h(F_U u, F_U v) = q^{m(n-2)} h(u,v) for all u,v in U_C. Define h' on V_C by h'(x,y) = h(phi(x), phi(y)), where phi: V_C -> U_C is the identification above. Since phi is an isomorphism and h is positive definite Hermitian, h' is positive definite Hermitian. Now take x,y in V_C and write x = phi(u), y = phi(v). Then F(x) = phi(q^m F_U u) and F(y) = phi(q^m F_U v). Therefore h'(F(x), F(y)) = h(q^m F_U u, q^m F_U v) = q^{2m} h(F_U u, F_U v) = q^{2m} q^{m(n-2)} h(u,v) = q^{mn} h'(x,y). This is exactly the required identity. Thus h' is a positive definite Hermitian form on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C satisfying h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = q^{mn} h'(x,y).

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Then H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the direct sum of L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) and P^d as a Q_ell[F]-module.
proof: Write H^r for H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell), put A=L(H^{d-2}) and B=P^d=ker(L:H^d->H^{d+2}). By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/12eb29, under the hard Lefschetz hypothesis we have H^d=A+B and A∩B=0 as Q_ell-vector spaces. It remains to show that A and B are submodules for the Q_ell[F]-action. Apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_frob_lefschetz_stable with the prime power q^m in place of its q. The base field is F_{q^m}, the divisor with class xi is defined over F_{q^m}, and the Frobenius in that lemma is exactly our q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F. It gives F∘L=q^m L∘F on every H^r. Since ell != p, q^m is a unit in Q_ell, so equivalently L∘F=q^{-m}F∘L and F^{-1}∘L=q^{-m}L∘F^{-1}. First consider B. If y∈B, then Ly=0. Using L∘F=q^{-m}F∘L, we get L(Fy)=q^{-m}F(Ly)=0, so Fy∈B. Using L∘F^{-1}=q^m F^{-1}∘L, which follows by multiplying F^{-1}∘L=q^{-m}L∘F^{-1} by q^m, we get L(F^{-1}y)=q^m F^{-1}(Ly)=0, so F^{-1}y∈B. Thus B is stable under F and F^{-1}, hence is a Q_ell[F]-submodule of H^d. Next consider A. If a∈A, write a=Lx with x∈H^{d-2}. Then F(a)=F(Lx)=q^m L(Fx), and Fx∈H^{d-2}, so F(a)∈A. Also F^{-1}(a)=F^{-1}(Lx)=q^{-m}L(F^{-1}x), and F^{-1}x∈H^{d-2}, so F^{-1}(a)∈A. Thus A is stable under F and F^{-1}, hence is a Q_ell[F]-submodule of H^d. Now H^d is the vector-space direct sum A⊕B, and both summands are Q_ell[F]-submodules. For z∈H^d write z=a+b with a∈A, b∈B. Then F(z)=F(a)+F(b), with F(a)∈A and F(b)∈B. By uniqueness of the decomposition H^d=A⊕B, the A-component of F(z) is F(a). Explicitly, if z=Lx+y with x∈H^{d-2} and y∈B, then F(z)=q^m L(Fx)+F(y); the first term lies in A and the second in B, so the B-component of F(z) is F(y), the F-image of the B-component of z, with the factor q^m correctly retained in the A-term. Therefore the projection H^d→A along B is F-linear, and the inclusions A→H^d and B→H^d are F-linear. Consequently H^d is the direct sum of A and B as a Q_ell[F]-module, i.e. H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)=L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) ⊕ P^d as a Q_ell[F]-module.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, let U be the open complement of Y in X, and let j:U->X. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Then ker(j^*:H^d(X)->H^d(U))=L H^{d-2}(X).

Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X over F_{q^m}, let U be the open complement of Y in X, and let j:U->X. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let delta:H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) be the Gysin boundary. Then j^* restricts to an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules P^d->ker(delta).
proof: Let the notation be as in the target lemma. The proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/c93af5 assumes exactly the same hypotheses: q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, Y a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor over F_{q^m}, U the open complement of Y in X, a fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) used to identify Tate twists with Q_ell, xi the cycle class of Y, L cup product with xi, the isomorphisms L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) for every 0<=n<=d, P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), F the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and delta the Gysin boundary H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1). In that lemma, the map P^d -> H^d(U) is defined as the composition of the inclusion P^d -> H^d(X) with the restriction j^*:H^d(X)->H^d(U), and it is proved to be an isomorphism of F-modules onto ker(delta). This is precisely the statement that j^* restricts to an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules P^d -> ker(delta). Hence the target lemma follows.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety over F_{q^m}, let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^1_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Then H^1_et(X_k,Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^m h(x,y) for all x,y.
