statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X smooth projective geometrically connected of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)=L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) ⊕ P^d as a direct sum of Q_ell[F]-submodules. If F on L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell) and F on P^d are each diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) and every eigenvalue of either, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}, then F on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) and every eigenvalue has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}.
proof:
Let K=Q_ell and Kbar=overline(Q_ell). Put V=H^d_et(X_k,K), A=L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,K), and B=P^d. The hypothesis says V=A direct sum B and that F(A) is contained in A and F(B) is contained in B. Write F_A=F|_A and F_B=F|_B. If A=0 or B=0, the conclusion is immediate from the corresponding hypothesis, so assume A and B are nonzero. Extend scalars to Kbar and write Vbar=V tensor_K Kbar, Abar=A tensor_K Kbar, Bbar=B tensor_K Kbar, and S=F tensor_K id_Kbar. Because the direct sum is F-stable, Vbar=Abar direct sum Bbar and S is the direct sum S_A direct sum S_B, where S_A=F_A tensor_K id_Kbar and S_B=F_B tensor_K id_Kbar.

First we show S is diagonalizable over Kbar. Since S_A is diagonalizable over Kbar, let lambda_1,...,lambda_r be its distinct eigenvalues in Kbar. For each i choose an eigenvector v_i with S_A v_i=lambda_i v_i. The polynomial m_A(t)=prod_{i=1}^r (t-lambda_i) annihilates S_A: on the eigenspace for lambda_i the factor t-lambda_i is zero. It is the minimal polynomial: if P in Kbar[t] annihilates S_A, then for each i, 0=P(S_A)v_i=P(lambda_i)v_i, and v_i is nonzero, so P(lambda_i)=0; hence every t-lambda_i divides P, and because the factors are distinct, m_A divides P. Thus m_A is squarefree. The same argument gives a squarefree minimal polynomial m_B for S_B, a product of distinct linear factors.

For the direct sum S, a polynomial P in Kbar[t] annihilates S if and only if it annihilates both S_A and S_B. Indeed, if P(S)=0, then for v in Abar, P(S)v=P(S_A v)=0, so P(S_A)=0, and similarly for Bbar; conversely, if P(S_A)=P(S_B)=0, then for v=a+b with a in Abar and b in Bbar, P(S)v=P(S_A a)+P(S_B b)=0. Therefore the annihilator ideal of S is the intersection of the principal ideals generated by m_A and m_B, so the minimal polynomial m_S of S is the least common multiple lcm(m_A,m_B). The least common multiple of two squarefree polynomials is squarefree: for each irreducible factor f, its exponent in the least common multiple is the maximum of its exponents in m_A and m_B, and each of those exponents is 0 or 1. Since Kbar is algebraically closed, every irreducible factor is linear, so m_S is a product of distinct linear factors.

It remains to note that a linear operator over an algebraically closed field is diagonalizable over that field when its minimal polynomial is a product of distinct linear factors. Write m_S(t)=prod_{i=1}^s (t-mu_i) with distinct mu_i. For each i let W_i=ker(S-mu_i id). Because the factors t-mu_i are pairwise coprime, the primary decomposition theorem gives Vbar=direct sum_i W_i; equivalently, for each i the Bezout identity between t-mu_i and the product of the other factors produces a projection of Vbar onto W_i along the sum of the other W_j. Each W_i is exactly the mu_i-eigenspace of S, so Vbar is a direct sum of eigenspaces. Hence S is diagonalizable over Kbar. Translating back, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).

Now consider eigenvalues. Choose bases of Abar and Bbar in which S_A and S_B are diagonal. In the direct sum basis of Vbar, S has a block diagonal matrix. Therefore its characteristic polynomial satisfies chi_S(t)=chi_{S_A}(t) chi_{S_B}(t). Consequently the multiset of eigenvalues of S over Kbar is the union of the multisets of eigenvalues of S_A and S_B. By hypothesis, every eigenvalue of F_A and every eigenvalue of F_B, viewed in Kbar, has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}. Thus every eigenvalue of S, and hence every eigenvalue of F, viewed in Kbar, has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}. This completes the proof.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K, let sigma:Kbar->C, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let T in GL_K(V), let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let h be a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((T tensor id)x,(T tensor id)y)=c h(x,y) for all x,y, and let W be a T-stable K-subspace of V. Then T|_W is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue of T|_W has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c)).
proof:
Let A := T|_W, the restriction of T to W. We prove that A is diagonalizable over Kbar and that every eigenvalue of A has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c)).

Step 0 (A is an automorphism of W). Since T in GL_K(V) and W is T-stable (T(W) subset W), the map T|_W : W -> W is an automorphism. Indeed, T is injective on V, hence on W, so dim T(W) = dim W; since T(W) is a subspace of W with dim T(W) = dim W, we have T(W) = W. Thus T|_W is surjective (and injective) on W, i.e. A in GL_K(W). Also W is finite-dimensional (a K-subspace of the finite-dimensional V).

Step 1 (restrict h to W). The inclusion W subset V of K-subspaces induces, after tensoring over K with C (where C is regarded as a K-algebra via K -> Kbar -> C, i.e. via the restriction of sigma to K), an inclusion of C-vector spaces W tensor_{K,sigma} C subset V tensor_{K,sigma} C. Let h_W := h|_{W tensor C} : (W tensor C) x (W tensor C) -> C be the restriction of h. Then h_W is a positive definite Hermitian form on W tensor C: it is Hermitian because it is the restriction of the Hermitian form h, and for 0 != x in W tensor C we have x != 0 in V tensor C, hence h_W(x,x) = h(x,x) > 0. Moreover, for x,y in W tensor C, since T(W) subset W we have (A tensor id)(x) = (T tensor id)(x) in W tensor C, and
  h_W((A tensor id)x, (A tensor id)y) = h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = c h(x,y) = c h_W(x,y),
where the middle equality is the hypothesis on h applied to x,y (which lie in V tensor C). Thus h_W((A tensor id)x,(A tensor id)y) = c h_W(x,y) for all x,y in W tensor C.

Step 2 (apply the proved lemma over C). We now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/45d6ea with the following data: the field K (of characteristic 0); the field embedding sigma|_K : K -> C (the restriction of sigma to K, which is a field embedding because sigma is injective on Kbar and K subset Kbar); the finite-dimensional K-vector space W; the automorphism A = T|_W in GL_K(W); and the scalar c in K^* with sigma(c) > 0. The hypothesis is satisfied by the positive definite Hermitian form h_W on W tensor_{K,sigma|_K} C = W tensor_{K,sigma} C (the two tensor products coincide since sigma|_K and sigma agree on K) together with the scaling identity h_W((A tensor id)x,(A tensor id)y) = c h_W(x,y). By the lemma, A tensor id is diagonalizable over C, and every eigenvalue of A tensor id (as a C-linear operator on W tensor C) has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c)).

Step 3 (descent: A is diagonalizable over Kbar). We prove A is diagonalizable over Kbar.
Let m(t) in Kbar[t] be the minimal polynomial of A over Kbar. Since Kbar is algebraically closed, A admits a Jordan canonical form over Kbar, and
  m(t) = prod_{lambda in Lambda} (t - lambda)^{e_lambda},
where Lambda is the set of distinct eigenvalues of A in Kbar and, for each lambda in Lambda, e_lambda >= 1 is the size of the largest Jordan block of A corresponding to lambda. (Standard linear algebra: over an algebraically closed field, the minimal polynomial of a linear operator is the product, over its distinct eigenvalues lambda, of (t - lambda) raised to the size of the largest Jordan block for lambda.)
Now consider the C-linear operator A tensor id on W tensor_{K,sigma} C. There is a canonical isomorphism W tensor_{K,sigma} C = W tensor_K C (C as a K-algebra via K -> Kbar -> C) and (W tensor_K Kbar) tensor_{Kbar,sigma} C, so A tensor id on W tensor C is the base change, via sigma : Kbar -> C, of the Kbar-linear operator B := A tensor id on W tensor_K Kbar. We claim the minimal polynomial of B tensor id over C is m_C(t) := prod_{lambda in Lambda} (t - sigma(lambda))^{e_lambda}.
Proof of claim: Since m(B) = 0, applying the field homomorphism sigma coefficientwise gives sigma(m)(B tensor id) = 0, so the minimal polynomial m_C of B tensor id over C divides sigma(m) = prod_{lambda in Lambda} (t - sigma(lambda))^{e_lambda} in C[t]. For the reverse bound on the exponents, fix lambda in Lambda and let U_lambda subset W tensor_K Kbar be the generalized eigenspace of B for lambda. By the definition of e_lambda, (B - lambda I)^{e_lambda}|_{U_lambda} = 0 but (B - lambda I)^{e_lambda - 1}|_{U_lambda} != 0. Tensoring with C over Kbar (an exact functor, since C is a flat Kbar-module) and using that base change preserves whether a linear map is zero (if f != 0 then there is u with f(u) != 0, and (f tensor id)(u tensor 1) = f(u) tensor 1 != 0 because u -> u tensor 1 is injective), we get (B tensor id - sigma(lambda) I)^{e_lambda}|_{U_lambda tensor C} = 0 but (B tensor id - sigma(lambda) I)^{e_lambda - 1}|_{U_lambda tensor C} != 0. Hence (B tensor id - sigma(lambda) I)^{e_lambda - 1} != 0 on all of W tensor C, so the exponent of (t - sigma(lambda)) in m_C is at least e_lambda. Combined with m_C | sigma(m) (exponent at most e_lambda), the exponent is exactly e_lambda for each lambda. Thus m_C = prod_{lambda in Lambda} (t - sigma(lambda))^{e_lambda}. Claim proved.
Since A tensor id is diagonalizable over C (Step 2) and A tensor id corresponds to B tensor id under the isomorphism above, B tensor id is diagonalizable over C, so its minimal polynomial m_C is a product of distinct linear factors over C. Hence every exponent e_lambda in m_C equals 1, i.e. e_lambda = 1 for all lambda in Lambda.
Therefore m(t) = prod_{lambda in Lambda} (t - lambda) is a product of distinct linear factors over Kbar. Over an algebraically closed field, a linear operator is diagonalizable if and only if its minimal polynomial is a product of distinct linear factors. Hence A is diagonalizable over Kbar.

Step 4 (eigenvalue absolute values). Let lambda be an eigenvalue of A = T|_W in Kbar. The eigenvalues of A tensor id on W tensor C are exactly {sigma(mu) : mu an eigenvalue of A in Kbar}, because the characteristic polynomial of A tensor id over C is the image under sigma of the characteristic polynomial of A over Kbar, and both are monic polynomials whose roots are the respective eigenvalues. In particular sigma(lambda) is an eigenvalue of A tensor id. By Step 2, every eigenvalue of A tensor id has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c)), so |sigma(lambda)| = sqrt(sigma(c)). Thus every eigenvalue of T|_W has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c)).

Combining Step 3 (A = T|_W is diagonalizable over Kbar) and Step 4 (every eigenvalue of T|_W has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c))), the lemma is proved.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, let U be the open complement of Y in X, and let j:U->X. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y, and let L denote cup product with xi. Suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Then ker(j^*:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell)) equals the image of L: H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof: Write H^n(Z) for H^n_et(Z_k,Q_l), and note that k=overline(F_q)=overline(F_{q^m}). A very ample divisor is the zero locus of a nonzero section of a very ample line bundle; hence Y is a nonempty smooth effective Cartier divisor on X, defined over F_{q^m}, and O_X(Y) is very ample, in particular ample. Thus Y is a smooth ample Cartier divisor, and it is geometrically connected by hypothesis. Since d>=3, d>=2. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/9e70fa applied to the pair (X,Y), the segment H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) -> H^d(X) -> H^d(U) with maps i_! and j^* is exact. Hence ker(j^*) = im(i_!) as subspaces of H^d(X). Next, by eoinm/ebe471c6ef5b2d01/f527bc, because Y is a nonempty smooth ample Cartier divisor on X, the restriction map i^*: H^{d-2}(X) -> H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism. Under the fixed identification Q_l(1)=Q_l, identify H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) with H^{d-2}(Y) and denote the corresponding Gysin map again by i_!. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/1f2e4b, for every x in H^{d-2}(X) one has i_!(i^*x) = x cup xi = Lx. This shows im(L) is contained in im(i_!). Conversely, let a be an element of H^{d-2}(Y)(-1), identified with H^{d-2}(Y). Since i^* is surjective, choose x in H^{d-2}(X) with i^*x = a. Then i_!(a) = i_!(i^*x) = Lx, so im(i_!) is contained in im(L). Therefore im(i_!) = im(L). Combining this with the exactness identity gives ker(j^*) = im(L), which is the desired statement. The hard Lefschetz assumptions on X are not needed for this particular identification, but the proof is valid under the stated hypotheses.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, and let i:Y->X. Then for every integer r with 0<=r<=d-2, i^*:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism.
proof:
We prove the statement by applying the proved Lefschetz hyperplane theorem, lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/309c9b, which states: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ell != p be prime, let m>=1, let k be an algebraic closure of F_q, let d>=2, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth geometrically connected very ample Cartier divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, and let i:Y->X be the closed immersion. Then i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer n with 0<=n<=d-2.

Step 1 (check the hypotheses of 309c9b against the present situation).
(a) The parameters q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2 and the variety X (smooth, projective, geometrically connected, of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}) are exactly as assumed in the target statement, hence exactly as required by 309c9b.
(b) The divisor Y. The target assumes Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X. We verify that this makes Y a 'smooth geometrically connected very ample Cartier divisor on X' in the sense of 309c9b. (i) Cartier: very ampleness of a divisor is defined via invertible sheaves: a divisor D on X is called very ample if the invertible sheaf O_X(D) is very ample, i.e. if the complete linear system |D| gives a closed immersion of X into some projective space over the base; this definition presupposes (and is standardly understood to mean) that D is an effective Cartier divisor, since a divisor represents an invertible sheaf if and only if it is Cartier. Thus Y is an effective Cartier divisor. In any case the distinction is immaterial here, because X is smooth, hence locally factorial, so every Weil divisor on X is Cartier; under either interpretation of the word 'divisor' in the hypothesis, Y is a Cartier divisor. (ii) Smoothness, geometric connectedness, and very ampleness of Y are assumed verbatim in the target statement. (iii) Defined over F_{q^m}: Y is a closed subscheme of X, and X is a scheme over F_{q^m}; composing the structure morphism Y->X with X->Spec F_{q^m} gives a structure morphism Y->Spec F_{q^m}, so Y is automatically a scheme (a divisor) defined over F_{q^m}. No extra choice is involved.
(c) The map i:Y->X is the inclusion of the effective Cartier divisor Y into X, hence a closed immersion, as required.

Step 2 (apply the lemma). All hypotheses of Miner/16d24b0281973336/309c9b are satisfied by the present data (X, Y, i, q, ell, m, k, d). Therefore, by that lemma, for every integer n with 0<=n<=d-2 the restriction map i^*:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces.

Step 3 (conclusion). The target asks for this to hold for every integer r with 0<=r<=d-2. Taking n=r in the conclusion of Step 2 gives, for each such r, that i^*:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^r_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. This is exactly the desired statement. QED.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, and let i:Y->X. Then i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is injective.
proof:
We verify that the stated hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses of the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/58bcf9, and then apply it.

Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, and k=overline(F_q). Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d>=2 over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, and let i:Y->X be the closed immersion. Since Y is a divisor on the smooth F_{q^m}-scheme X and is very ample, it is an effective Cartier divisor defined over F_{q^m}; its base change Y_k is smooth and geometrically connected, and i remains the closed immersion Y->X_k after base change.

Thus all assumptions of Miner/16d24b0281973336/58bcf9 are satisfied: q is a prime power, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and Y is a smooth geometrically connected very ample Cartier divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}.

By Miner/16d24b0281973336/58bcf9, the restriction map
i^*:H^{d-1}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)
is injective. This is precisely the desired conclusion.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then F L = q^m L F on every H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
I have read the three lemmas I need. Now let me verify the key instantiation carefully and write the proof.

The target lemma asks to show that for $X$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$, the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius $F$ satisfies $F \circ L = q^m \, L \circ F$ on every cohomology group, where $L$ is cup product with the cycle class $\xi$ of an $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-rational very ample divisor.

The fix from the feedback is clear: apply lemma_291 directly with base prime power $Q = q^m$ (not re-basing to $\mathbb{F}_q$), with $j=1$ and extension degree $1$, to get $F(\xi) = q^m\,\xi$. Then use the ring property (lemma_220) and $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linearity (lemma_6a) to conclude.

Let me verify the key details are consistent:
- $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} = \overline{\mathbb{F}_q}$: yes, since $\mathbb{F}_q \subseteq \mathbb{F}_{q^m} \subseteq \overline{\mathbb{F}_q}$ and $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q}$ is algebraically closed.
- The $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-rational divisor is a codimension-1 cycle on $X_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}}$ itself, so the extension degree in lemma_291 is $1$.
- The $Q$-power arithmetic Frobenius with $Q = q^m$ is exactly the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius $F$ of the target.

All checks pass. No computation is needed; the proof is a direct application of the three lemmas.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/5153a9",
  "cited_lemmas": ["eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_291", "eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_220", "eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that $F \circ L = q^m\, L \circ F$ on every $H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$.

**Setup.** Write $Q = q^m = p^{am}$, which is a prime power. Since $\mathbb{F}_q \subseteq \mathbb{F}_{q^m} \subseteq \overline{\mathbb{F}_q}$ and $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q}$ is algebraically closed, we have $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} = \overline{\mathbb{F}_q} = k$. Thus the base change $X_k = X \times_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} k$ is the same as the base change to $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}}$.

**Step 1: $F(\xi) = q^m\, \xi$.**

We apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_291 with the following choices:
- Base prime power: $Q = q^m$.
- $X$: the given smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension $d$ over $\mathbb{F}_Q = \mathbb{F}_{q^m}$. This is exactly the hypothesis of the target lemma, so all hypotheses of lemma_291 are satisfied.
- $k = \overline{\mathbb{F}_Q} = \overline{\mathbb{F}_q}$ (as noted above).
- $\ell \neq p$ (as in the target).
- $j = 1$ (the divisor has codimension $1$).
- Extension degree $m' = 1$: the divisor $z$ is $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-rational, hence is a codimension-$1$ cycle on $X_{\mathbb{F}_Q} = X_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}}$ itself, i.e. on $X$ over its own base field $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$.
- $z$: the given $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-rational very ample divisor.
- $\mathrm{cl}(z)$: the cycle class of $z$, defined in lemma_291 as the image of the class of $z$ in $H^{2}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell(1))$ under a fixed identification $\mathbb{Q}_\ell(1) \cong \mathbb{Q}_\ell$. The target fixes such an identification (a nonzero element of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell(1)$) and calls the resulting class $\xi$. Hence $\mathrm{cl}(z) = \xi$.
- $F$: the $Q$-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism of $H^{2}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$. Since $Q = q^m$, this is the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius, which is exactly the $F$ of the target lemma.

The conclusion of lemma_291 states $F^{m'}(\mathrm{cl}(z)) = Q^{m' j}\, \mathrm{cl}(z)$. Substituting $m' = 1$, $j = 1$, $Q = q^m$, and $\mathrm{cl}(z) = \xi$, we obtain
$$F(\xi) = q^m\, \xi. \tag{1}$$

**Step 2: $F$ is a ring automorphism and $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear.**

By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_220, instantiated with the prime power $Q = q^m$ (so that $X$ is a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{F}_Q$, $k = \overline{\mathbb{F}_Q}$, $\ell \neq p$), the $Q$-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism $F$ of the graded ring $H^*_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ satisfies
$$F(x \cup y) = F(x) \cup F(y) \tag{2}$$
for all homogeneous classes $x, y \in H^*_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$.

By the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, instantiated with the prime power $Q = q^m$, the $Q$-power arithmetic Frobenius $F_{\mathrm{ar}} = (\mathrm{id}_X \times \sigma)^*$, where $\sigma: k \to k$ is the $Q$-power field automorphism $\sigma(a) = a^Q = a^{q^m}$, is a $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear automorphism of $H^i_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ for every $i \geq 0$. Hence $F$ is $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear on each $H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$. In particular, for any $\alpha \in H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$, $F(\alpha) \in H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{\ell})$ and $F$ respects $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-scalar multiplication.

**Step 3: Compute $F(L(\alpha))$ for arbitrary $\alpha$.**

Let $n \geq 0$ be an arbitrary integer and let $\alpha \in H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$. By the definition of $L$ (cup product with $\xi$), $L(\alpha) = \xi \cup \alpha$. We compute:
$$F(L(\alpha)) = F(\xi \cup \alpha) \qquad \text{(definition of $L$)}$$
$$= F(\xi) \cup F(\alpha) \qquad \text{(by (2), the ring property of $F$)}$$
$$= (q^m\, \xi) \cup F(\alpha) \qquad \text{(by (1), $F(\xi) = q^m\, \xi$)}$$
$$= q^m\, (\xi \cup F(\alpha)) \qquad \text{(by $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-bilinearity of the cup product)}$$
$$= q^m\, L(F(\alpha)) \qquad \text{(definition of $L$).}$$

In the fourth equality we use that the cup product $\cup: H^2_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \times H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) \to H^{n+2}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ is $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-bilinear, so for the scalar $q^m \in \mathbb{Q}_\ell$ we have $(q^m\, \xi) \cup F(\alpha) = q^m\, (\xi \cup F(\alpha))$. No sign correction is needed: we are pulling out a scalar from the first factor, not interchanging the order of two classes of different degrees.

**Conclusion.** Since $n \geq 0$ was arbitrary and $\alpha \in H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ was arbitrary, we have shown that $F(L(\alpha)) = q^m\, L(F(\alpha))$ for all $\alpha$ in every cohomology group. Equivalently, $F \circ L = q^m\, L \circ F$ on every $H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$. This completes the proof. $\blacksquare$"
}

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let T be a K-linear automorphism of V, let c in K^*, and let beta:V x V -> K be a nondegenerate skew-symmetric bilinear form such that beta(Tx,Ty)=c beta(x,y) for all x,y in V. If T is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K, then for every eigenvalue lambda of T in that algebraic closure, c/lambda is an eigenvalue of T with the same algebraic multiplicity.
proof:
Let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K and set Vbar = V tensor_K Kbar. Let Tbar = T tensor id be the induced Kbar-linear automorphism of Vbar.

Step 0 (diagonalization and eigenspaces). Since T is diagonalizable over Kbar, Tbar is diagonalizable over Kbar: there is a Kbar-basis of Vbar consisting of eigenvectors of Tbar with eigenvalues in Kbar. Let Lambda subset Kbar be the finite set of eigenvalues of Tbar (finite because the minimal polynomial of Tbar splits into linear factors over Kbar), and for lambda in Lambda let E_lambda = {v in Vbar : Tbar v = lambda v} be the lambda-eigenspace. Then Vbar = direct sum over lambda in Lambda of E_lambda, a direct sum of nonzero Kbar-subspaces. Each lambda in Lambda is nonzero: Tbar is an automorphism, so Tbar v = 0 forces v = 0, i.e. 0 is not an eigenvalue. Hence for each lambda in Lambda the element c/lambda in Kbar is well defined and nonzero.

Step 1 (extension of the form). Extend beta to a Kbar-bilinear form betabar: Vbar x Vbar -> Kbar by betabar(v tensor a, w tensor b) = a b beta(v,w); this is well defined and Kbar-bilinear by the universal property of the tensor product. We record two facts.

Fact 1.1 (betabar is nondegenerate). Nondegeneracy of beta means the K-linear map phi: V -> V^*, phi(v) = (w -> beta(v,w)), is an isomorphism: it is injective (if v != 0 then nondegeneracy gives w with beta(v,w) != 0, so phi(v) != 0), and it is surjective because dim V = dim V^* < infinity. Tensoring with Kbar gives a Kbar-linear isomorphism phi tensor id: Vbar = V tensor_K Kbar -> V^* tensor_K Kbar. Under the standard identification V^* tensor_K Kbar ~= (V tensor_K Kbar)^* = Vbar^* (given by (f tensor a) -> (v tensor b -> a b f(v))), this isomorphism is the map Vbar -> Vbar^*, v -> (w -> betabar(v,w)). An isomorphism of this form is exactly the statement that betabar is nondegenerate. Done.

Fact 1.2 (scaling is preserved). The map (u,v) -> betabar(Tbar u, Tbar v) - c betabar(u,v) is Kbar-bilinear in (u,v) and vanishes on the spanning set V x V, where it equals beta(Tu,Tv) - c beta(u,v) = 0. Hence it vanishes identically: betabar(Tbar u, Tbar v) = c betabar(u,v) for all u,v in Vbar.

Step 2 (orthogonality of eigenspaces). Let lambda, mu in Lambda, x in E_lambda, y in E_mu. Then Tbar x = lambda x and Tbar y = mu y, so by bilinearity betabar(Tbar x, Tbar y) = lambda mu betabar(x,y). By Fact 1.2, betabar(Tbar x, Tbar y) = c betabar(x,y). Subtracting gives (lambda mu - c) betabar(x,y) = 0. Since Kbar is a field, if lambda mu != c then betabar(x,y) = 0. Thus:
(∗) For x in E_lambda and y in E_mu, if mu != c/lambda then betabar(x,y) = 0.

Step 3 (the pairing of reciprocal eigenspaces is perfect). Fix lambda in Lambda and consider the restriction b_lambda: E_lambda x E_{c/lambda} -> Kbar of betabar, and the induced map Phi_lambda: E_lambda -> (E_{c/lambda})^*, Phi_lambda(x) = (y -> b_lambda(x,y)).

Claim 3.1 (Phi_lambda is injective). Let x in E_lambda with b_lambda(x,y) = 0 for every y in E_{c/lambda}. Take any v in Vbar and write v = sum over mu in Lambda of v_mu with v_mu in E_mu (a finite sum). By (∗), betabar(x, v_mu) = 0 for every mu != c/lambda, so betabar(x,v) = sum_mu betabar(x, v_mu) = b_lambda(x, v_{c/lambda}) = 0. Thus x lies in the radical of betabar on Vbar, and Fact 1.1 (nondegeneracy) forces x = 0. Hence Phi_lambda is injective.

Claim 3.2 (the opposite map is injective). The same argument with the two factors interchanged shows that the map E_{c/lambda} -> (E_lambda)^*, y -> (x -> b_lambda(x,y)), is injective: condition (∗) is symmetric, since it kills beta on a pair of eigenspaces exactly when the product of the two eigenvalues differs from c, and (c/lambda) * lambda = c.

From Claim 3.1, dim E_lambda <= dim (E_{c/lambda})^* = dim E_{c/lambda}. From Claim 3.2, dim E_{c/lambda} <= dim (E_lambda)^* = dim E_lambda. Hence dim E_lambda = dim E_{c/lambda}. Since Phi_lambda is injective (Claim 3.1) and its source and target have equal finite dimension, Phi_lambda is an isomorphism. (In the special case lambda = c/lambda, i.e. lambda^2 = c, this says the skew-symmetric form betabar|_{E_lambda x E_lambda} is nondegenerate, which is consistent and causes no difficulty.)

Step 4 (conclusion). Since lambda in Lambda, E_lambda != 0, so dim E_{c/lambda} = dim E_lambda >= 1, hence E_{c/lambda} != 0. Thus c/lambda in Lambda is an eigenvalue of Tbar, and therefore an eigenvalue of T: the characteristic polynomial is unchanged under base change, because if e_1,...,e_n is a K-basis of V in which T has matrix A, then e_1 tensor 1,...,e_n tensor 1 is a Kbar-basis of Vbar in which Tbar has the same matrix A (Tbar(e_i tensor 1) = (T e_i) tensor 1 = sum_j a_{ij} (e_j tensor 1)), so chi_{Tbar}(X) = det(X I - A) = chi_T(X) viewed in Kbar[X].

It remains to compare algebraic multiplicities. Since Tbar is diagonalizable, choosing a Kbar-basis of Vbar by concatenating bases of the eigenspaces E_lambda, the matrix of Tbar is diagonal with the entry lambda appearing exactly dim E_lambda times. Hence chi_T(X) = chi_{Tbar}(X) = product over lambda in Lambda of (X - lambda)^{dim E_lambda}. The algebraic multiplicity of lambda is therefore dim E_lambda, and the algebraic multiplicity of c/lambda is dim E_{c/lambda} = dim E_lambda. Thus c/lambda is an eigenvalue of T with the same algebraic multiplicity as lambda. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth divisor on X, let U be the open complement of Y in X, let j:U->X and i:Y->X. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell), with Tate twists identified by a fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d and F L=q^m L F. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X)), let delta:H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) be the Gysin boundary, and let phi:P^d->ker(delta) be the restriction of j^*. If the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)(-1)->H^d(X) has image L H^{d-2}(X), then phi is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules.
proof: Set H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_l) and write F_X, F_U for the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*(X) and H^*(U). Put L_1=L:H^{d-2}(X)->H^d(X) and L_2=L:H^d(X)->H^{d+2}(X). Then L^2=L_2 L_1. By the hard Lefschetz hypothesis with n=d-2, L^2 is an isomorphism. Hence L_1 is injective and L_2 is surjective. For any y in H^d(X), choose a in H^{d-2}(X) with L^2 a=L_2 y; this is possible because L^2 is surjective. Then p=y-L_1 a satisfies L_2 p=L_2 y-L_2 L_1 a=0, so p in P^d. Thus H^d(X)=L H^{d-2}(X)+P^d. If z lies in the intersection, then z=L_1 a and 0=L_2 z=L_2 L_1 a=L^2 a, so a=0 and z=0. Therefore H^d(X)=L H^{d-2}(X) direct sum P^d as Q_l-vector spaces. From F_X L=q^m L F_X we get F_X L_1 a=q^m L_1 F_X a, so F_X preserves L H^{d-2}(X). If p in P^d, then 0=F_X L_2 p=q^m L_2 F_X p, so F_X p in P^d. Hence both summands are F_X-stable, and the direct sum is a direct sum of Q_l[F_X]-submodules. By the cited Gysin sequence lemma, applied to the pair (X,Y) over the finite field F_{q^m}, the segment H^{d-2}(Y)(-1) -> H^d(X) -> H^d(U) -> H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) is exact, with the first map i_! and the second j^*. Hence ker(j^*)=im(i_!) and im(j^*)=ker(delta). By the hypothesis im(i_!)=L H^{d-2}(X), so ker(j^*)=L H^{d-2}(X). Now take y in H^d(X). Write y=L_1 a+p with p in P^d. Since L_1 a is in ker(j^*), j^* y=j^* p. Therefore im(j^*)=j^*(P^d). Since im(j^*)=ker(delta), the restriction phi=j^*|_{P^d} maps P^d onto ker(delta). If p in P^d and phi(p)=0, then p in ker(j^*)=L H^{d-2}(X), so p lies in the intersection P^d intersect L H^{d-2}(X), which is zero. Thus phi is a Q_l-linear isomorphism. Finally, arithmetic Frobenius is natural with respect to pullback by the open immersion j, so F_U j^*=j^* F_X. Because ker(delta)=im(j^*) and F_X is an automorphism of H^d(X), F_U(ker(delta))=F_U(im(j^*))=im(j^* F_X)=im(j^*)=ker(delta). Thus F_U preserves ker(delta). For p in P^d, F_X p in P^d, and phi(F_X p)=j^* F_X p=F_U j^* p=F_U phi(p). Hence phi intertwines the Frobenius actions. Since phi is bijective, its inverse also intertwines the Frobenius actions, and phi is an isomorphism of Q_l[F]-modules.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, suppose F L=q^m L F, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Suppose that for every smooth projective geometrically connected variety Z of dimension less than d over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r(Z) for every r>=0 and every eigenvalue, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Then, where L H^{d-2} denotes the image of L in H^d and carries the Frobenius induced from H^d, L H^{d-2} tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h' with h'((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{md}h'(x,y) for all x,y.
proof: Let D be the given F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor and let xi be its cycle class. The operator L depends only on xi, so we may replace D by a smooth geometrically connected member of the same linear system; such a member exists by Bertini and the connectedness theorem, and the replacement does not change xi. Denote this divisor by Y and let i:Y -> X. Then Y is smooth projective geometrically connected of dimension d-1 over F_{q^m}, and d-1 < d. Since d>=2, the integer d-2 is nonnegative. By the Lefschetz hyperplane lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/fadc41, i^*:H^{d-2}(X) -> H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism. Because i is defined over F_{q^m}, the pullback commutes with the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius: i^* F_X = F_Y i^*. The induction hypothesis applies to Y. Hence F_Y on H^{d-2}(Y) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue alpha of F_Y has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-2)/2}; for the fixed embedding sigma this means |sigma(alpha)| = q^{m(d-2)/2}. Conjugating by i^*, F_X on H^{d-2}(X) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue beta of F_X satisfies |sigma(beta)| = q^{m(d-2)/2}. Next, L: H^{d-2}(X) -> H^d(X) is injective. Indeed, taking n=d-2 in the hypothesis that L^{d-n}:H^n -> H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism gives L^2: H^{d-2}(X) -> H^{d+2}(X) an isomorphism; if Lx=0 then L^2x=0, so x=0. Put W = L H^{d-2}(X) in H^d(X). The assumed identity F L = q^m L F implies F(W) subset W, since for x in H^{d-2}(X), F(Lx)=q^m L(Fx) lies in W. Since F is an automorphism of H^d(X), its restriction F_W to W is an automorphism of W; this is precisely the Frobenius induced from H^d on W. The subspace W is finite-dimensional over Q_ell. Because L is injective, it identifies H^{d-2}(X) with W as Q_ell-vector spaces. Choose a basis v_j of H^{d-2}(X) over overline(Q_ell) such that F_X v_j = beta_j v_j. Then L v_j is a basis of W over overline(Q_ell), and F_W(L v_j) = F(L v_j) = q^m L(F_X v_j) = q^m beta_j L v_j. Thus F_W is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue gamma of F_W is of the form q^m beta_j. Therefore |sigma(gamma)| = sigma(q^m) |sigma(beta_j)| = q^m q^{m(d-2)/2} = q^{md/2}. Finally apply the general Hermitian-form lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ccebfa with K=Q_ell, the given sigma, c=q^{md}, V=W, and T=F_W. We have c in Q_ell^* and sigma(c)=q^{md}>0, T in GL_{Q_ell}(W), T diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue gamma of T satisfies |sigma(gamma)| = q^{md/2} = sqrt(sigma(c)). Hence W tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h' with h'((F_W tensor id)x,(F_W tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h'(x,y) = q^{md} h'(x,y). This is the required form on L H^{d-2} tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, let i:Y->X. Suppose that for every smooth projective geometrically connected variety Z of dimension less than d over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r(Z) for every r>=0 and every eigenvalue, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Suppose i^*:H^r(X)->H^r(Y) is an isomorphism for 0<=r<=d-2 and is injective for r=d-1. Then for every 0<=r<d, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r(X) and every eigenvalue, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.
proof: Let Kbar = overline(Q_ell). Let F_X and F_Y denote the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*(X_k,Q_ell) and H^*(Y_k,Q_ell). Since Y is a very ample divisor, it is an effective ample divisor defined over F_{q^m} and is smooth of pure dimension d-1. Apply Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_283 with the prime power Q = q^m to the pair Y subset X. The lemma gives the long exact sequence whose middle map is the pullback i^*, and it says that every map in that sequence commutes with the Q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms of the four terms. In particular, for every n>=0, i^* F_X = F_Y i^* on H^n(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^n(Y_k,Q_ell), and F_Y on H^n(Y_k,Q_ell) is a Q_ell-linear automorphism. The induction hypothesis applies to Z=Y because dim Y = d-1 < d. Hence for every r>=0, F_Y on H^r(Y) is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue, viewed in Kbar, has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Now fix r with 0<=r<d. If 0<=r<=d-2, the map i^*:H^r(X)->H^r(Y) is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism by hypothesis. It commutes with Frobenius, so after scalar extension to Kbar we have F_X tensor id = (i^* tensor id)^{-1} (F_Y tensor id) (i^* tensor id). Conjugate linear operators have the same characteristic polynomial, hence the same eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity. Since F_Y tensor id is diagonalizable over Kbar, so is F_X tensor id. Since every eigenvalue of F_Y tensor id has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}, every eigenvalue of F_X tensor id has the same Weil absolute value. If r=d-1 and H^{d-1}(X)=0, the desired statement is vacuous, so assume H^{d-1}(X) is nonzero. Put V=H^{d-1}(X), W=H^{d-1}(Y), and phi=i^*:V->W. By hypothesis phi is injective. Let U=phi(V) subset W. The commutation relation gives F_Y(U) subset U, because for u=phi(v) in U, F_Y(u)=phi(F_X(v)) lies in U. Let Wbar=W tensor_{Q_ell} Kbar, Ubar=U tensor_{Q_ell} Kbar, and F_Ybar=F_Y tensor id. By induction F_Ybar is diagonalizable over Kbar, and since F_Y is an automorphism, F_Ybar is a semisimple Kbar-linear automorphism of Wbar. The subspace Ubar is F_Ybar-stable. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_515, the restriction F_Ybar|_{Ubar} is semisimple over Kbar. Since Kbar is algebraically closed, semisimple is the same as diagonalizable over Kbar; thus F_Y|_U tensor id is diagonalizable over Kbar. The map phi is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces from V onto U. After scalar extension to Kbar, phi_bar:V tensor Kbar -> Ubar is an isomorphism and satisfies phi_bar (F_X tensor id) = (F_Y|_U tensor id) phi_bar. Therefore F_X tensor id is conjugate over Kbar to F_Y|_U tensor id, and so F_X tensor id is diagonalizable over Kbar. Finally, let lambda be an eigenvalue of F_X tensor id. By the conjugacy just described, lambda is an eigenvalue of F_Y|_U tensor id, so there is a nonzero u in Ubar with F_Ybar u = lambda u. Since Ubar is a subspace of Wbar, lambda is also an eigenvalue of F_Ybar on Wbar. By the induction hypothesis its Weil absolute value is q^{m(d-1)/2}. Hence every eigenvalue of F_X tensor id has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2}. This completes the proof for all 0<=r<d.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let r be an integer with 0<=r<=2d, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), then F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
Now I have all the pieces I need. Let me verify the two key lemmas:

1. **`eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77`** (part (b)): For every $n$ with $0 \le n \le 2d$, the Poincaré duality pairing $H^n_{	ext{ét}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) 	imes H^{2d-n}_{	ext{ét}}(Y_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell) 	o \mathbb{Q}_\ell(-d)$ is **perfect**, and satisfies $\langle Fx, Fyangle = q^{md}\langle x, yangle$.

2. **`Miner/16d24b0281973336/dadf7b`**: If $V, W$ are finite-dimensional $K$-spaces with a nondegenerate pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdotangle: V	imes W	o K$ and $T_V, T_W$ satisfy $\langle T_V v, T_W wangle = c\langle v,wangle$, then $T_W$ diagonalizable $\Rightarrow$ $T_V$ diagonalizable.

These two lemmas together give the result directly.

  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/cfb6af",
  "cited_lemmas": ["eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77", "Miner/16d24b0281973336/dadf7b"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "Let q=p^a, ℓ≠p, m≥1, k=overline(ℱ_q), d≥1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over ℱ_{q^m}. Let 0≤r≤2d and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. Assume F is diagonalizable over overline(ℚ_ℓ) on H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ). We prove F is diagonalizable over overline(ℚ_ℓ) on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ).

Step 1: The Poincaré duality pairing and its Frobenius compatibility.
By part (b) of eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, applied to Y=X (which is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over ℱ_{q^m}), with n=2d−r (which satisfies 0≤2d−r≤2d since 0≤r≤2d), the pairing
  β : H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) × H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) → ℚ_ℓ(−d),  (x,y) ↦ tr_X(x∪y)
is a perfect pairing of ℚ_ℓ-vector spaces, and it satisfies
  β(Fx, Fy) = q^{md} β(x, y)  for all x ∈ H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ), y ∈ H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ).

Step 2: Convert to a pairing valued in ℚ_ℓ.
Since ℚ_ℓ(−d) is a one-dimensional ℚ_ℓ-vector space, fix a nonzero element ω ∈ ℚ_ℓ(−d). The ℚ_ℓ-linear map φ : ℚ_ℓ(−d) → ℚ_ℓ given by φ(a) = λ where a = λω is an isomorphism. Define
  β' : H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) × H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) → ℚ_ℓ,  β'(x,y) = φ(β(x,y)).
Since β is perfect (the induced maps H^{2d-r} → (H^r)^* and H^r → (H^{2d-r})^* are isomorphisms), and φ is an isomorphism, β' is also a perfect (hence nondegenerate) bilinear pairing. Moreover,
  β'(Fx, Fy) = φ(β(Fx, Fy)) = φ(q^{md} β(x,y)) = q^{md} φ(β(x,y)) = q^{md} β'(x, y)
for all x, y, using the ℚ_ℓ-linearity of φ.

Step 3: Apply the linear algebra lemma.
We now invoke Miner/16d24b0281973336/dadf7b with the following choices:
  • K = ℚ_ℓ (a field of characteristic 0);
  • V = H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) (a finite-dimensional ℚ_ℓ-vector space, since X is smooth projective of finite dimension over a finite field);
  • W = H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) (likewise finite-dimensional);
  • T_V = F|_V, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ); this is a ℚ_ℓ-linear automorphism of V (Frobenius is an automorphism of each cohomology group);
  • T_W = F|_W, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ); likewise a ℚ_ℓ-linear automorphism of W;
  • c = q^{md} ∈ ℚ_ℓ^*;
  • ⟨v, w⟩ = β'(v, w), the nondegenerate bilinear pairing V × W → ℚ_ℓ constructed in Step 2.
The compatibility condition is verified in Step 2: ⟨T_V v, T_W w⟩ = β'(Fv, Fw) = q^{md} β'(v,w) = c ⟨v,w⟩ for all v ∈ V, w ∈ W.
The hypothesis of Miner/16d24b0281973336/dadf7b requires that T_W be diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of K = ℚ_ℓ. By assumption, F is diagonalizable over overline(ℚ_ℓ) on H^r_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ) = W, i.e., T_W is diagonalizable over overline(ℚ_ℓ), which is an algebraic closure of ℚ_ℓ.

Step 4: Conclusion.
By Miner/16d24b0281973336/dadf7b, T_V is diagonalizable over an algebraic closure of ℚ_ℓ, i.e., over overline(ℚ_ℓ). Since T_V = F|_{H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ)}, this means F is diagonalizable over overline(ℚ_ℓ) on H^{2d-r}_et(X_k, ℚ_ℓ), as required.

Remark on edge cases. The argument covers all 0≤r≤2d uniformly. For r=0: H^0_et(X_k,ℚ_ℓ)≅ℚ_ℓ (X geometrically connected) and H^{2d}_et(X_k,ℚ_ℓ) is one-dimensional; the pairing is perfect and the conclusion is that F on H^{2d} is diagonalizable. For r=2d: symmetric. For r=d: the pairing is the usual self-pairing on H^d, and the argument recovers the familiar statement that diagonalizability of Frobenius on H^d is self-dual under Poincaré duality. No separate treatment is needed since the perfect-pairing hypothesis of lemma_77(b) holds for every n with 0≤n≤2d."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every integer r with 0<=r<=d, then F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) for every integer r>=0.
proof: Let H^r denote H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). We split into three ranges. If r>2d, then the base change X_k is a projective k-scheme of pure dimension d. By Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing, H^r=0. The Frobenius action on the zero vector space is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), because after tensoring with overline(Q_ell) the space is still zero and the zero space is the direct sum of the eigenspaces for the empty set of eigenvalues. If 0<=r<=d, the conclusion is exactly the hypothesis. If d<r<=2d, put s=2d-r. Then s is an integer with 0<=s<d, hence 0<=s<=2d. By hypothesis, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^s. The lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/cfb6af applies to X and to this degree s, and it says that diagonalizability of F on H^s implies diagonalizability of F on H^{2d-s}. Since 2d-s=r, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r. These cases exhaust all integers r>=0.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X smooth projective geometrically connected of dimension d over F_{q^m}, Y a smooth divisor, i:Y->X. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, let i_{1,!}:H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) be the Gysin map, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism and L:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is injective, then i_{1,!} is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules from H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) onto L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
Based on my analysis, the proof is self-contained: it uses the Poincaré duality characterization of the Gysin map to prove the projection formula, then uses the corrected scalar convention (arithmetic Frobenius acts on $\mathbb{Q}_\ell(1)$ by $q^m$, hence $F_X(\xi) = q^{-m}\xi$) to verify Frobenius equivariance. No listed lemmas are needed since the projection formula here is for a general smooth divisor (not necessarily very ample), so I prove it directly.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/944096",
  "cited_lemmas": [],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that i_{1,!} is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules from H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) onto L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell).

**Step 1: The projection formula i_{1,!} ∘ i^* = L.**

We use the Poincaré duality characterization of the Gysin map. The (untwisted) Gysin map i_!: H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) → H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) is the unique Q_ell-linear map satisfying, for all a ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) and all b ∈ H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell):
  tr_X(i_!(a) · b) = tr_Y(a · i^*b)  … (*)
where tr_X: H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell) → Q_ell and tr_Y: H^{2(d-1)}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) → Q_ell are the Poincaré duality trace maps. The map i_{1,!} is obtained from i_! by the chosen identification of Q_ell(-1) with Q_ell: under the isomorphism H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) ≅ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) sending y ⊗ e^{-1} to y (where e^{-1} is the chosen nonzero element of Q_ell(-1)), the map i_{1,!} corresponds to i_!. Equivalently, for a ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) written as a = a_0 · e^{-1} with a_0 ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell), we have i_{1,!}(a) = i_!(a_0).

We claim: for every x ∈ H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell), i_!(i^*x) = x · [Y], where [Y] ∈ H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell(1)) is the cycle class of Y.

Proof of claim. Fix b ∈ H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell). By (*):
  tr_X(i_!(i^*x) · b) = tr_Y(i^*x · i^*b) = tr_Y(i^*(x · b)).

The cycle class [Y] ∈ H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell(1)) is defined by the property that for every c ∈ H^{2d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell(-1)):
  tr_X(c · [Y]) = tr_Y(i^*c).

Under the chosen identification Q_ell(1) ≅ Q_ell (sending the chosen element e to 1), this reads: for every c ∈ H^{2d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell),
  tr_X(c · ξ) = tr_Y(i^*c),
where ξ is the image of [Y] under the identification, i.e., [Y] = ξ · e.

Take c = x · b ∈ H^{2d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) (since deg(x) = d-2 and deg(b) = d, deg(c) = 2d-2). Then:
  tr_Y(i^*(x · b)) = tr_X((x · b) · ξ) = tr_X(x · ξ · b) = tr_X(L(x) · b).

Combining with the earlier equation:
  tr_X(i_!(i^*x) · b) = tr_X(L(x) · b)
for all b ∈ H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell). Since the Poincaré duality pairing (a, b) ↦ tr_X(a · b) on H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) × H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) is nondegenerate (X is smooth projective of dimension d, so 2d - d = d), we conclude i_!(i^*x) = L(x) = x · ξ.

Under the twist identification, this gives the projection formula:
  i_{1,!}(i^*x) = L(x)  for all x ∈ H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell).  … (PF)

**Step 2: i_{1,!} is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism onto L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell).**

Since i^*: H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) → H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism (hypothesis), under the twist identification every element a ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) can be written uniquely as a = i^*x for a unique x ∈ H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell).

(Containment of image.) For any a ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1), write a = i^*x. By (PF): i_{1,!}(a) = i_{1,!}(i^*x) = L(x) ∈ L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell). Hence im(i_{1,!}) ⊆ L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell).

(Surjectivity onto L·H^{d-2}.) For any y ∈ L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell), write y = L(x) for some x. Then y = i_{1,!}(i^*x) = i_{1,!}(a) where a = i^*x. Hence y ∈ im(i_{1,!}).

(Injectivity.) Suppose i_{1,!}(a) = 0. Write a = i^*x. Then 0 = i_{1,!}(i^*x) = L(x). Since L is injective (hypothesis), x = 0, hence a = 0.

Therefore i_{1,!} is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism from H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) onto L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell).

**Step 3: Frobenius equivariance i_{1,!} ∘ F = F_X ∘ i_{1,!}.**

We use the standard ℓ-adic convention Q_ell(1) = colim_n μ_{ℓ^n}. Under this convention, the arithmetic Frobenius (the automorphism x ↦ x^{q^m} of k) acts on Q_ell(1) by the scalar q^m (it acts on each μ_{ℓ^n} by the q^m-th power map, which on the ℓ-adic Tate module T_ℓ is multiplication by q^m). Consequently, F acts on Q_ell(-1) = Q_ell(1)^* by the inverse scalar q^{-m}.

(3a) Frobenius invariance of the cycle class. Since Y is a smooth divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, its cycle class [Y] ∈ H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell(1)) is fixed by arithmetic Frobenius: F([Y]) = [Y].

Write [Y] = ξ · e where e is the chosen nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and ξ ∈ H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell). The action of F on H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell(1)) satisfies (for x ∈ H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell)):
  F(x · e) = F_X(x) · F(e) = F_X(x) · (q^m · e) = q^m · (F_X(x) · e).

Applying to x = ξ and using F([Y]) = [Y]:
  [Y] = F(ξ · e) = q^m · (F_X(ξ) · e).

Since [Y] = ξ · e and the map x ↦ x · e is an isomorphism H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell) → H^2_et(X_k, Q_ell(1)), we get:
  ξ · e = q^m · (F_X(ξ) · e)  ⟹  F_X(ξ) = q^{-m} · ξ.  … (3a)

(3b) Action of F on the domain. Let a ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) and write a = i^*x for the unique x ∈ H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) (under the twist identification, a = i^*x ⊗ e^{-1} where e^{-1} is the chosen element of Q_ell(-1)).

The action of F on H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) = H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) ⊗ Q_ell(-1) is:
  F(a) = F(i^*x ⊗ e^{-1}) = F_Y(i^*x) ⊗ F(e^{-1}).

By naturality of the pullback map with respect to Frobenius (the square formed by i^*, F_X, F_Y, and the identity on the base commutes, since i is defined over F_{q^m}):
  F_Y(i^*x) = i^*(F_X(x)).

And F acts on Q_ell(-1) by q^{-m}, so F(e^{-1}) = q^{-m} · e^{-1}. Therefore:
  F(a) = i^*(F_X(x)) ⊗ (q^{-m} · e^{-1}) = q^{-m} · (i^*(F_X(x)) ⊗ e^{-1}) = q^{-m} · (i^*(F_X(x)))
where the last expression is in H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) under the twist identification.

(3c) Compute the left side i_{1,!}(F(a)). By Q_ell-linearity of i_{1,!} and the projection formula (PF):
  i_{1,!}(F(a)) = i_{1,!}(q^{-m} · i^*(F_X(x))) = q^{-m} · i_{1,!}(i^*(F_X(x))) = q^{-m} · L(F_X(x)).  … (LHS)

(3d) Compute the right side F_X(i_{1,!}(a)). First, i_{1,!}(a) = i_{1,!}(i^*x) = L(x) = x · ξ by (PF). Then, using that F_X is a ring homomorphism on the cohomology ring and (3a):
  F_X(i_{1,!}(a)) = F_X(x · ξ) = F_X(x) · F_X(ξ) = F_X(x) · (q^{-m} · ξ) = q^{-m} · (F_X(x) · ξ) = q^{-m} · L(F_X(x)).  … (RHS)

(3e) Conclusion. From (LHS) = (RHS), we have i_{1,!}(F(a)) = F_X(i_{1,!}(a)) for every a ∈ H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1). Hence i_{1,!} ∘ F_Y = F_X ∘ i_{1,!}, i.e., i_{1,!} is F-linear.

**Step 4: F-stability of the image and final conclusion.**

From Step 3d, for any x ∈ H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell):
  F_X(L(x)) = q^{-m} · L(F_X(x)) ∈ L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell),
since F_X(x) ∈ H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell). Thus L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is F_X-stable, hence a Q_ell[F]-submodule of H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell).

From Step 2, i_{1,!} is a Q_ell-linear isomorphism from H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) onto L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell). From Step 3, it commutes with F. Since the target L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is an F-stable Q_ell-subspace (a Q_ell[F]-submodule), i_{1,!} is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules from H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) onto L·H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell). ∎"
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell, and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1). Let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. Suppose that for every smooth projective geometrically connected variety Z of dimension less than d over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(Z_k,Q_ell) for every r>=0 and every eigenvalue, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Then H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) tensor_{Q_ell,sigma}C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{m(d-3)}h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
Both key lemmas are confirmed. Now I can write the proof. The strategy is:

1. Apply the induction hypothesis to $Z = Y$ (dimension $d-1 < d$) and $r = d-1$ to get that $F$ is diagonalizable on $H^{d-1}(Y)$ with eigenvalues of Weil absolute value $q^{m(d-1)/2}$.
2. Apply lemma `5d27b2` to get a positive definite Hermitian form on $H^{d-1}(Y)$ with multiplier $q^{m(d-1)}$.
3. Apply lemma `f3da8d` (with $n = d-1$) to get a positive definite Hermitian form on $H^{d-1}(Y)(-1)$ with multiplier $q^{m(d-3)}$.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/fdd0f7",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Miner/16d24b0281973336/5d27b2", "Miner/16d24b0281973336/f3da8d"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F⊗id)x, (F⊗id)y) = q^{m(d-3)} h(x,y) for all x,y.\n\nStep 1: Apply the induction hypothesis to Y. Since Y is a smooth divisor on the smooth projective geometrically connected variety X of dimension d, Y is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d-1 over F_{q^m}. Since d ≥ 2, we have d-1 ≥ 1, so dim Y = d-1 < d. The induction hypothesis states that for every smooth projective geometrically connected variety Z of dimension less than d over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ℓ) on H^r_et(Z_k, Q_ℓ) for every r ≥ 0, and every eigenvalue, viewed in overline(Q_ℓ), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Taking Z = Y and r = d-1, we conclude that the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ℓ) on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ), and every eigenvalue of F on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in overline(Q_ℓ), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2}.\n\nStep 2: Translate to the embedding σ. The condition that every eigenvalue has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2} means that for every embedding τ: overline(Q_ℓ) → C, every eigenvalue λ of F on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) satisfies |τ(λ)| = q^{m(d-1)/2}. In particular, for the specific embedding σ: overline(Q_ℓ) → C given in the statement, every eigenvalue of F ⊗ id on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C has complex absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2}. Moreover, since F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ℓ), the operator F ⊗ id on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C is diagonalizable over C.\n\nStep 3: Apply the linear algebra lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/5d27b2. Set K = Q_ℓ, V = H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ), T = F (the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, which is an automorphism of V), and c = q^{m(d-1)} > 0. The conditions of the lemma are satisfied: T ⊗ id is diagonalizable over C (Step 2), and every eigenvalue of T ⊗ id has complex absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2} = sqrt(q^{m(d-1)}) = sqrt(c) (Step 2). Therefore, by Miner/16d24b0281973336/5d27b2, V ⊗_{K,σ} C = H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F⊗id)x, (F⊗id)y) = q^{m(d-1)} h(x,y) for all x,y.\n\nStep 4: Apply the Tate twist lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/f3da8d. Set n = d-1. The variety Y is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension n = d-1 over F_{q^m}. We have shown in Step 3 that H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C = H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F⊗id)x, (F⊗id)y) = q^{mn} h(x,y) = q^{m(d-1)} h(x,y) for all x,y. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/f3da8d, it follows that H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C = H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1) ⊗_{Q_ℓ,σ} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h' with h'((F⊗id)x, (F⊗id)y) = q^{m(n-2)} h'(x,y) = q^{m(d-3)} h'(x,y) for all x,y.\n\nThis is exactly the desired conclusion. The Frobenius F in the conclusion is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1), which is the same operator that appears in the statement of the target lemma. This completes the proof."
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, let i:Y->X, fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell, let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L:H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is injective. Then the image of i_!:H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is L H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell).
proof:
We prove the claim by applying the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/b8e973 in the case d=2.

Recall the statement of b8e973: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and let i:Y->X be the inclusion. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Let xi be the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), let L be cup product with xi, and suppose i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Then the image of the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) equals L H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell).

We verify that all hypotheses of b8e973 hold with d=2 in the present situation.

(1) Dimension and smoothness. X is a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}, hence a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d=2 over F_{q^m}.

(2) The divisor Y. By hypothesis Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}. A very ample divisor is in particular ample, so Y is a smooth ample divisor on X defined over F_{q^m} that is geometrically connected, and i:Y->X is the inclusion. This matches the hypothesis on Y in b8e973.

(3) Tate twists, cycle class, and L. We use the fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell (the same identification as in the target statement). xi is the cycle class of Y in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), and L is cup product with xi, exactly as in b8e973.

(4) The remaining hypothesis of b8e973: i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism. With d=2 this is the map i^*:H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell). We prove it is an isomorphism.

We use the following standard fact.
Fact. If Z is a connected scheme, then H^0_et(Z,Q_ell)=Q_ell, identified with the constant functions.
Proof of the fact. H^0_et(Z,Q_ell) is the group of sections of the constant sheaf Q_ell on the etale site of Z, i.e. the set of functions f:Z->Q_ell (with Q_ell regarded as a discrete set) that are etale-locally constant: for every z in Z there exists an etale morphism V->Z and a point v in V with (V->Z)(v)=z such that f o (V->Z) is constant on an open neighborhood of v in V; replacing V by that open neighborhood (still etale over Z), we may assume f o (V->Z) is constant on all of V. Fix such an f. For s in Q_ell set Z_s={z in Z : f(z)=s}. First, Z_s is open in the usual topology: take z in Z_s; by the etale-locally-constant property there is an etale V->Z with (V->Z)(V) contained in Z_s (since f o (V->Z)=s on V and f(z)=s). Etale morphisms are open, so (V->Z)(V) is an open subset of Z, and z lies in the open set (V->Z)(V) contained in Z_s; hence Z_s is open. Second, Z_s is closed, since Z_s = Z \ union_{t != s} Z_t and each Z_t is open by the same argument. Thus each Z_s is clopen, and the family {Z_s}_{s in Q_ell} is a disjoint clopen decomposition of Z (every point of Z lies in exactly one Z_s, since f is a function). Because Z is connected, a disjoint clopen decomposition of Z has a unique nonempty member, so exactly one Z_s equals Z and f is constant. Hence H^0_et(Z,Q_ell) consists of the constant functions, i.e. H^0_et(Z,Q_ell)=Q_ell. This proves the fact.

Now apply the fact. Since X is geometrically connected over F_{q^m}, its base change X_k = X x_{F_{q^m}} k is connected (geometric connectedness of a variety over a field means precisely that the base change to an algebraic closure is connected). Similarly, since Y is geometrically connected, Y_k is connected. Therefore, by the fact, H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)=Q_ell (the constant functions on the connected scheme X_k) and H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)=Q_ell (the constant functions on the connected scheme Y_k). The pullback i^*:H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell) sends the constant function 1 to the constant function 1, because the pullback of a constant function along any morphism is the same constant function. Under the identifications of both groups with Q_ell via the constant functions, i^* is the identity map Q_ell->Q_ell, which is an isomorphism. This verifies the remaining hypothesis of b8e973.

(5) Conclusion. All hypotheses of b8e973 with d=2 are satisfied (steps (1)-(4)), so by b8e973 the image of the Gysin map i_!:H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) equals L H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell).

It remains to reconcile the Tate-twist convention. The Gysin map for the codimension-1 divisor i:Y->X is canonically the map i_!:H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell). Writing it instead as i_!:H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) (as in b8e973) amounts to precomposing the source with the canonical isomorphism H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell) -> H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) induced by the fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Q_ell(1) with Q_ell. Since this is an isomorphism of the source, the two maps have the same image in H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell). Hence the image of i_!:H^0_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) equals L H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell), which is precisely the desired conclusion. (Note that the additional hypothesis in the target statement, that L:H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is injective, is not needed for this argument; the conclusion holds a fortiori under the target's hypotheses.)

This completes the proof.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let sigma:K->C be an embedding, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let T in GL_K(V), and let h be a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((T tensor id)x,(T tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h(x,y) for all x,y in V tensor_{K,sigma} C. Let W be a T-stable K-subspace of V. Then (V/W) tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_W with h_W((T tensor id)x,(T tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h_W(x,y) for all x,y in (V/W) tensor_{K,sigma} C.
proof:
Proof. Fix the convention that a Hermitian form is C-linear in its first variable and C-conjugate-linear in its second, so h(y,x)=overline{h(x,y)} and h(x,x) is real with h(x,x)>0 for x≠0. Put V_C:=V⊗_{K,σ} C and W_C:=W⊗_{K,σ} C; both are C-vector spaces, dim_C W_C=dim_K W≤dim_K V, and W_C⊂V_C.

Step 1 (identifying the quotient). The quotient map π:V→V/W is surjective. Because K is a field, C is a flat K-module, so -⊗_{K,σ} C is exact; applying it to 0→W→V→V/W→0 gives 0→W_C→V_C→(V/W)_C→0, where (V/W)_C=(V/W)⊗_{K,σ}C and V_C→(V/W)_C sends v⊗z to (v+W)⊗z. Hence (V/W)_C≅V_C/W_C via (v+W)⊗z↦(v⊗z)+W_C. We identify the two and prove the claim for V_C/W_C.

Step 2 (T preserves W_C). If {f_1,...,f_r} is a K-basis of W then {f_j⊗1} is a C-basis of W_C, so W_C is a C-subspace of V_C. T is K-linear and T(W)⊂W, so (T⊗id)(W_C)⊂W_C. Since T is invertible, T|_W:W→W is a K-linear injection of the finite-dimensional space W, hence an isomorphism; thus T(W)=W and (T⊗id)(W_C)=W_C. So T descends to an automorphism of V_C/W_C.

Step 3 (orthonormal basis of W_C and the orthogonal projection). Let r=dim_C W_C. (If r=0 then W_C={0}, W_C^⊥=V_C, and all sums below are empty; assume r≥1.) Choose a C-basis e_1,...,e_r of W_C and build an orthonormal basis g_1,...,g_r by Gram-Schmidt: set s_1:=sqrt(h(e_1,e_1))>0, g_1:=e_1/s_1; for i=2,...,r set r_i:=e_i-Σ_{k=1}^{i-1} h(e_i,g_k)g_k, s_i:=sqrt(h(r_i,r_i)), g_i:=r_i/s_i.

We prove by induction on i that {g_1,...,g_i} is orthonormal (h(g_i,g_j)=δ_{ij}) and span{g_1,...,g_i}=span{e_1,...,e_i}. For i=1: h(g_1,g_1)=h(e_1,e_1)/s_1^2=1 and span{g_1}=span{e_1}.

Inductive step, i≥2. First r_i≠0: if r_i=0 then e_i=Σ_{k<i}h(e_i,g_k)g_k∈span{g_1,...,g_{i-1}}=span{e_1,...,e_{i-1}} (induction), contradicting the independence of e_1,...,e_r; hence h(r_i,r_i)>0 and s_i>0, and span{g_1,...,g_i}=span{e_1,...,e_i} since g_i=r_i/s_i with r_i=e_i-(element of span{g_1,...,g_{i-1}}). Now for j<i:
h(r_i,g_j)=h(e_i-Σ_{k<i}h(e_i,g_k)g_k,g_j)=h(e_i,g_j)-Σ_{k<i}h(e_i,g_k)h(g_k,g_j).
By the induction hypothesis {g_1,...,g_{i-1}} is orthonormal, so h(g_k,g_j)=δ_{kj} for k,j<i; as j<i the sum Σ_{k<i}h(e_i,g_k)δ_{kj} is the single term h(e_i,g_j) (at k=j). Thus h(r_i,g_j)=h(e_i,g_j)-h(e_i,g_j)=0, so h(g_i,g_j)=h(r_i/s_i,g_j)=0. Also h(g_i,g_i)=h(r_i,r_i)/s_i^2=1. Hence {g_1,...,g_i} is orthonormal, completing the induction.

Define p:V_C→W_C by p(x):=Σ_{j=1}^{r}h(x,g_j)g_j. Then p(x)∈W_C for all x; for every x, x-p(x)∈W_C^⊥ (where W_C^⊥:={x∈V_C: h(x,w)=0 for all w∈W_C}) because for each j, h(x-p(x),g_j)=h(x,g_j)-Σ_k h(x,g_k)h(g_k,g_j)=h(x,g_j)-h(x,g_j)=0; the decomposition V_C=W_C⊕W_C^⊥ is direct (W_C∩W_C^⊥={0} since h(x,x)=0 forces x=0, and x=p(x)+(x-p(x))); and p is the orthogonal projection onto W_C (p|_{W_C}=id because if x=Σ_j a_j g_j then p(x)=Σ_j h(x,g_j)g_j=Σ_j a_j g_j=x, and p^2=p).

Step 4 (defining h_W). Define h_W:(V_C/W_C)×(V_C/W_C)→C by h_W(x+W_C,y+W_C):=h(x,(I-p)(y)).

Well-defined: in the second slot, y→y+w (w∈W_C) sends (I-p)(y) to (I-p)(y)+(I-p)(w)=(I-p)(y) since p(w)=w; in the first slot, x→x+w' (w'∈W_C) adds h(w',(I-p)(y))=0 since (I-p)(y)∈W_C^⊥ and w'∈W_C.

Sesquilinearity: (I-p) is C-linear, so h_W(αx+W_C,y+W_C)=h(αx,(I-p)(y))=αh_W(x+W_C,y+W_C) and h_W(x+W_C,αy+W_C)=h(x,(I-p)(αy))=h(x,α(I-p)(y))=overline{α}h_W(x+W_C,y+W_C).

Hermitian: h_W(y+W_C,x+W_C)=h(y,(I-p)(x)), whose conjugate is h((I-p)(x),y). Now h(x,(I-p)(y))=h((I-p)(x),(I-p)(y)) (as h(p(x),(I-p)(y))=0) and h((I-p)(x),(I-p)(y))=h((I-p)(x),y) (as h((I-p)(x),p(y))=0), so h_W(x+W_C,y+W_C)=h((I-p)(x),y)=overline{h_W(y+W_C,x+W_C)}.

Positive definite: h_W(x+W_C,x+W_C)=h(x,(I-p)(x))=h((I-p)(x),(I-p)(x)) (as h(p(x),(I-p)(x))=0)≥0, with equality iff (I-p)(x)=0 iff x∈W_C iff x+W_C=0. So h_W is a positive definite Hermitian form on V_C/W_C.

Step 5 (T preserves W_C^⊥ and commutes with p). Let u∈W_C^⊥ and w∈W_C. As T(W_C)=W_C, pick w'∈W_C with w=T(w'); then h(Tu,w)=h(Tu,T(w'))=σ(c)h(u,w')=0 (since u∈W_C^⊥), so Tu∈W_C^⊥, i.e. T(W_C^⊥)⊂W_C^⊥. For any x, T(x)=T(p(x))+T((I-p)(x)) with T(p(x))∈W_C and T((I-p)(x))∈W_C^⊥; by uniqueness of the decomposition, p(T(x))=T(p(x)), so pT=Tp and (I-p)T=T(I-p).

Step 6 (similitude). For x,y∈V_C:
h_W(Tx+W_C,Ty+W_C)=h(Tx,(I-p)(Ty))=h(Tx,T(I-p)(y))  [by (I-p)T=T(I-p)]
=σ(c)h(x,(I-p)(y))  [by h(Ta,Tb)=σ(c)h(a,b) with a=x, b=(I-p)(y)]
=σ(c)h_W(x+W_C,y+W_C).

This is the required identity. Since V_C/W_C is canonically (V/W)⊗_{K,σ} C, the lemma follows. QED.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L:H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) and L:H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^4_et(X_k,Q_ell) are isomorphisms, put P^2=ker(L:H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^4_et(X_k,Q_ell)), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If every smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over F_{q^m} has q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^1_et(C_k,Q_ell) and every eigenvalue, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m/2}, then P^2 tensor_{Q_ell,sigma}C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{2m}h(x,y) for all x,y.
proof:
I have completed thorough verification. No proved lemma or reference is required — the result is a self-contained degenerate case. The hypothesis that $L: H^2 	o H^4$ is an isomorphism forces $P^2 = \ker(L) = 0$, so $P^2 \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_\ell,\sigma}\mathbb{C} = 0$, and the zero Hermitian form on the zero space is positive definite (vacuously) and satisfies the functional equation (vacuously). The curve hypothesis is not used.

Here is my final answer:

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/2a3bc8",
  "cited_lemmas": [],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that P^2 tensor_{Q_l, sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id) x, (F tensor id) y) = q^{2m} h(x, y) for all x, y. The argument is self-contained and uses only the hypothesis that L: H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^4_et(X_k, Q_l) is an isomorphism together with the definition P^2 = ker(L: H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^4_et(X_k, Q_l)).

Step 1 (L: H^2 -> H^4 is injective). By hypothesis the map L: H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^4_et(X_k, Q_l) is an isomorphism of Q_l-vector spaces, so it has a two-sided inverse L^{-1}: H^4_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^2_et(X_k, Q_l). Hence L is injective: if v in H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) satisfies L(v) = 0, then v = L^{-1}(L(v)) = L^{-1}(0) = 0, since L^{-1} is Q_l-linear and sends 0 to 0. Thus ker(L: H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^4_et(X_k, Q_l)) = {0}.

Step 2 (P^2 = 0). By definition P^2 = ker(L: H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^4_et(X_k, Q_l)). By Step 1 this kernel is {0}, so P^2 = 0, the zero Q_l-vector space.

Step 3 (P^2 tensor C = 0). The tensor product of the zero vector space with any vector space is the zero vector space: every element of (P^2 tensor_{Q_l, sigma} C) = (0 tensor_{Q_l, sigma} C) is a finite sum of pure tensors v tensor w with v in P^2 = {0}, hence v = 0, so each pure tensor is 0 tensor w = 0 and the sum is 0. Therefore P^2 tensor_{Q_l, sigma} C = 0, the zero C-vector space. Write V = P^2 tensor_{Q_l, sigma} C = {0}.

Step 4 (define h). Define h: V x V -> C by h(0, 0) = 0. This is the unique map from the one-point set V x V to C sending (0,0) to 0.

Step 5 (h is a Hermitian form). A Hermitian form on a C-vector space V is a map h: V x V -> C that is (i) C-linear in the first variable, h(a u + b v, w) = a h(u, w) + b h(v, w) for all a, b in C and u, v, w in V; (ii) conjugate-linear in the second variable, h(u, a v + b w) = conj(a) h(u, v) + conj(b) h(u, w); and (iii) satisfies h(u, v) = conj(h(v, u)) for all u, v in V. Since V = {0} has the single element 0, condition (i) reads h(0, 0) = a h(0, 0) + b h(0, 0), i.e. 0 = a*0 + b*0 = 0; condition (ii) reads h(0, 0) = conj(a) h(0, 0) + conj(b) h(0, 0), i.e. 0 = 0; and condition (iii) reads h(0, 0) = conj(h(0, 0)), i.e. 0 = conj(0) = 0. All three identities hold, so h is a Hermitian form on V.

Step 6 (h is positive definite). A Hermitian form h on V is positive definite if h(v, v) > 0 for every v in V with v != 0. Since V = {0} contains no element v != 0, the condition 'for every v != 0, h(v, v) > 0' holds vacuously. Hence h is positive definite.

Step 7 (functional equation). Let x, y be arbitrary elements of V = {0}; necessarily x = y = 0. The map F tensor id: V -> V is C-linear (it is the scalar extension via sigma of the Q_l-linear automorphism F of P^2 = {0}), so (F tensor id)(0) = 0. Therefore h((F tensor id) x, (F tensor id) y) = h(0, 0) = 0, while q^{2m} h(x, y) = q^{2m} * h(0, 0) = q^{2m} * 0 = 0. Hence h((F tensor id) x, (F tensor id) y) = q^{2m} h(x, y) for all x, y in V.

Step 8 (conclusion). Combining Steps 3, 5, 6, and 7, the space P^2 tensor_{Q_l, sigma} C = V carries the positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id) x, (F tensor id) y) = q^{2m} h(x, y) for all x, y, which is exactly the desired conclusion.

Remark on the curve hypothesis: the assumption that for every smooth projective geometrically connected curve C over F_{q^m} the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is diagonalizable over Q_l-bar on H^1_et(C_k, Q_l) with every eigenvalue of Weil absolute value q^{m/2} is not used anywhere in the argument. The conclusion follows purely from the fact that the hypothesis 'L: H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) -> H^4_et(X_k, Q_l) is an isomorphism' forces P^2 = ker(L) = 0 (Steps 1-2), a degenerate case in which the required positive definite Hermitian form is the zero form on the zero space. (Equivalently, the hypotheses force dim_{Q_l} H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) = dim_{Q_l} H^4_et(X_k, Q_l) = 1 and H^2_et(X_k, Q_l) = Q_l * xi, so the 'primitive' middle cohomology P^2 vanishes identically.)"
}

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. If for every integer r with 0<=r<=d, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) and every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}, then for every integer r>=0, F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell) and every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.
proof:
We must prove that for every integer r ≥ 0, two properties hold: (i) F is diagonalizable over Q̄_ℓ on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), and (ii) every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in Q̄_ℓ, has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.

**Part (i): Diagonalizability in all degrees.**
By the hypothesis, F is diagonalizable over Q̄_ℓ on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) for every integer r with 0 ≤ r ≤ d. We now invoke the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/79ad28, which states: for a smooth projective geometrically connected variety X of pure dimension d ≥ 1 over F_{q^m}, if F is diagonalizable over Q̄_ℓ on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) for every integer r with 0 ≤ r ≤ d, then F is diagonalizable over Q̄_ℓ on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) for every integer r ≥ 0. All hypotheses of 79ad28 are satisfied: q = p^a with ℓ ≠ p, m ≥ 1, k = F̄_q, d ≥ 1, and X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Therefore, F is diagonalizable over Q̄_ℓ on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) for every integer r ≥ 0. This establishes property (i).

**Part (ii): Weil absolute value bound in all degrees.**
We split into three cases according to the size of r.

*Case 1: 0 ≤ r ≤ d.*
The Weil bound is given directly by the hypothesis: every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in Q̄_ℓ, has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}.

*Case 2: d ≤ r ≤ 2d.*
Set s = 2d − r. Then 0 ≤ s ≤ d, so s satisfies the hypothesis range. By the hypothesis, every eigenvalue of F on H^s_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in Q̄_ℓ, has Weil absolute value q^{ms/2}. We now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/df3b9b, which states: for a smooth projective geometrically connected variety X of pure dimension d ≥ 1 over F_{q^m}, and an integer s with 0 ≤ s ≤ 2d, if every eigenvalue of F on H^s_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) has Weil absolute value q^{ms/2}, then every eigenvalue of F on H^{2d−s}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) has Weil absolute value q^{m(2d−s)/2}. All hypotheses of df3b9b are met: d ≥ 1, 0 ≤ s = 2d − r ≤ d ≤ 2d, and the Weil bound in degree s follows from the hypothesis (since s ∈ [0, d]). The conclusion of df3b9b gives: every eigenvalue of F on H^{2d−s}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) = H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in Q̄_ℓ, has Weil absolute value q^{m(2d−s)/2} = q^{mr/2}. This is exactly property (ii) in degree r.

*Case 3: r > 2d.*
We invoke the proved lemma Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_projective_top_degree_vanishing, which states: if k is an algebraically closed field, ℓ is a prime different from the characteristic of k, and X is a projective scheme over k of pure dimension d ≥ 0, then H^n_et(X, Q_ℓ) = 0 for every integer n > 2d. In our setting, k = F̄_q is algebraically closed, ℓ ≠ p = char(k), and X_k is a projective scheme over k of pure dimension d ≥ 1 (hence d ≥ 0). Since r > 2d, the lemma gives H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) = 0. On the zero vector space, F is trivially diagonalizable (property (i)), and the statement "every eigenvalue has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}" (property (ii)) is vacuously true, since there are no eigenvalues.

**Conclusion.**
For every integer r ≥ 0, both properties (i) and (ii) hold: F is diagonalizable over Q̄_ℓ on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), and every eigenvalue of F on H^r_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), viewed in Q̄_ℓ, has Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. This completes the proof.
