statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, X smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and Y a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor. Let i:Y->X, let U be the open complement of Y in X, and write H^s(Z)=H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell, and let beta_Y: H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) x H^{d-1}(Y) -> Q_ell be the Poincare duality pairing. If delta:H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) is the Gysin boundary, then im(delta)={a in H^{d-1}(Y)(-1): beta_Y(a,i^*b)=0 for every b in H^{d-1}(X)}.
proof:
Let q^m be the prime power defining the base field. Since Y is very ample, it is in particular an effective ample divisor. Let xi be the cycle class of Y under the fixed identification Q_ell(1) = Q_ell, and let L be cup product with xi.

Step 1. We show im(delta) = ker(i_!). By the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/fadc41, for r = d-2 the restriction i^*: H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d-2}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism. Apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439 to X over the finite field F_{q^m} (replacing q in that lemma by q^m). It gives the exact sequence 0 -> H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) / L H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^d_et(U_k, Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) -> H^{d+1}_et(X_k, Q_ell), where the second arrow is the Gysin boundary delta and the third arrow is the Gysin map i_!: H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) -> H^{d+1}_et(X_k, Q_ell). Exactness at H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) gives im(delta) = ker(i_!).

Step 2. We identify ker(i_!) with the stated orthogonal complement. Let tr_X and tr_Y be the Poincare duality traces normalized as in eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77 and composed with the fixed identification of Tate twists with Q_ell. By part (b) of that lemma, the pairing (u, v) -> tr_X(u cup v) on H^{d+1}_et(X_k, Q_ell) x H^{d-1}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is perfect. Now let a be in H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1). Under the fixed identification of the twist, write a = c(-1) for a unique c in H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell). The pairing beta_Y in the statement is the Poincare duality pairing with the first factor twisted; therefore there is a fixed nonzero scalar mu in Q_ell^* such that beta_Y(a, v) = mu tr_Y(c cup v) for every v in H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell). This scalar is independent of a and v and is nonzero because all identifications involved are isomorphisms. Hence beta_Y(a, i^*b) = 0 for all b in H^{d-1}_et(X_k, Q_ell) if and only if tr_Y(c cup i^*b) = 0 for all such b.

Apply eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor with n = d-1. It gives, for c in H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell) and b in H^{d-1}_et(X_k, Q_ell), the identity tr_X(i_! c cup b) = tr_Y(c cup i^* b), where i_! c is the usual untwisted Gysin image of c. The Gysin map appearing in the exact sequence is the twisted Gysin map, and under the fixed identification of Tate twists it sends a = c(-1) to i_! c. Thus tr_X(i_! a cup b) = tr_Y(c cup i^* b) for every b. By perfectness of the X pairing, a lies in ker(i_!) if and only if tr_X(i_! a cup b) = 0 for every b in H^{d-1}_et(X_k, Q_ell). By the displayed identity this is equivalent to tr_Y(c cup i^*b) = 0 for every b, and by the previous paragraph it is equivalent to beta_Y(a, i^*b) = 0 for every b. Therefore ker(i_!) = { a in H^{d-1}_et(Y_k, Q_ell)(-1) : beta_Y(a, i^*b) = 0 for every b in H^{d-1}_et(X_k, Q_ell) }. Combining this with im(delta) = ker(i_!) proves the lemma.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected surface over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, let P^2 = ker(L:H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^4_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell) is the direct sum of the Q_ell[F]-submodule L H^0_et(X_k,Q_ell), on which F acts by multiplication by q^m, and the Q_ell[F]-submodule P^2.
proof: Fix the usual nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and use it to identify Tate twists with Q_ell; this is the convention under which xi is written in H^2 and L has target H^4. Let H^r denote H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell). Since X_k is connected, a section of the constant sheaf Q_ell is locally constant, hence constant, so H^0 = Q_ell, generated by 1. Thus L H^0 is the line Q_ell xi because L(1)=xi. By Poincare duality, eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, the pairing beta(x,y)=tr(x cup y) on H^2 is nondegenerate. Let D be the very ample divisor whose cycle class is xi. Applying eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_272 with q^m in place of q gives that the Poincare trace of xi^2 is the image in Q_ell of a positive rational number; hence beta(xi,xi) != 0. In particular xi != 0. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/3f2004, x is in P^2 if and only if beta(xi,x)=0. Thus P^2 is the kernel of the nonzero linear functional x -> beta(xi,x). We now decompose. For x in H^2, set a = beta(x,xi)/beta(xi,xi) and y = x - a xi. Then beta(xi,y)=beta(xi,x)-a beta(xi,xi)=0, so y in P^2 by Miner/16d24b0281973336/3f2004. Hence x = a xi + y is in L H^0 + P^2. If a xi + y = 0 with y in P^2, then 0 = beta(xi,a xi) + beta(xi,y) = a beta(xi,xi), so a=0 and then y=0. Therefore H^2 = L H^0 direct sum P^2 as Q_ell-vector spaces. For Frobenius, Miner/16d24b0281973336/5153a9 gives F L = q^m L F on every cohomology group. If x in P^2, then Lx=0, so 0 = F(Lx) = q^m L(Fx). Since ell != p, q^m is invertible in Q_ell, hence L(Fx)=0, and Fx in P^2. Thus P^2 is F-stable. Applying eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_265 with q^m in place of q, F acts as the identity on H^0, so F(1)=1. Hence F(xi)=F(L(1))=q^m L(F(1))=q^m L(1)=q^m xi. Therefore F(a xi)=a q^m xi for every a in Q_ell, so F acts on L H^0 by multiplication by q^m and L H^0 is F-stable. Since both summands are F-stable, the vector-space direct sum is a direct sum of Q_ell[F]-submodules, with the stated scalar action on L H^0.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, assume L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let beta be the Poincare duality pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then the restriction of beta to P^d is nondegenerate.
proof: Write H^s = H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Let tr_X: H^{2d} -> Q_ell(-d) be the Poincare duality trace and set beta(x,y)=tr_X(x cup y) for x,y in H^d. Nondegeneracy is independent of whether the target is viewed as Q_ell(-d) or, after choosing a nonzero element of Q_ell(-d), as Q_ell. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77, part (b), for every r with 0<=r<=2d the pairing H^r x H^{2d-r} -> Q_ell(-d), (u,v) -> tr_X(u cup v), is perfect. Hence beta is nondegenerate on H^d, and the pairing H^{d-2} x H^{d+2} is perfect. Let A = L(H^{d-2}) subset H^d and P = P^d = ker(L:H^d -> H^{d+2}). First, L:H^{d-2} -> H^d is injective: if y in H^{d-2} and L y = 0, then L^2 y = 0; by the hypothesis with n=d-2, L^2: H^{d-2} -> H^{d+2} is an isomorphism, so y=0. Next, the restriction L_A: A -> H^{d+2}, L_A(L y)=L^2 y, is an isomorphism. For surjectivity, given w in H^{d+2}, choose y in H^{d-2} with L^2 y=w; then w=L_A(L y). For injectivity, if L y in A and L_A(L y)=0, then L^2 y=0, so y=0 and L y=0. Since L:H^d -> H^{d+2} has kernel P and L_A is an isomorphism from A onto H^{d+2}, we get H^d = A direct sum P. Indeed, for any v in H^d let w=L(v); choose a in A with L_A(a)=w; then v-a lies in ker L=P. If a+p=0 with a in A and p in P, then 0=L(a+p)=L_A(a), so a=0 and then p=0. Now we show A and P are orthogonal for beta. Take y in H^{d-2} and z in P. Then beta(L y,z) = tr_X((xi cup y) cup z). The cup product is associative and graded-commutative. Since xi has degree 2, moving xi past y of degree d-2 introduces the sign (-1)^{2(d-2)}=1. Thus (xi cup y) cup z = y cup (xi cup z) = y cup L z. Because z in P, L z=0, so beta(L y,z)=0. Hence beta(A,P)=0. Also, for u,v in H^d, beta(v,u)=(-1)^d beta(u,v), again by graded commutativity because u and v have degree d; hence beta(P,A)=0 as well. Finally, let z in P and suppose beta(z,z')=0 for every z' in P. For any a in A, beta(z,a)=0 by beta(P,A)=0. Since H^d=A direct sum P, every v in H^d can be written v=a+z' with a in A and z' in P. Then beta(z,v)=beta(z,a)+beta(z,z')=0. Thus z is in the radical of beta on H^d. By Poincare duality, i.e. the perfectness of beta from eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77 with r=d, the radical is zero, so z=0. This shows the first radical of beta|_P is zero; since beta on H^d satisfies beta(u,v)=(-1)^d beta(v,u), the second radical is also zero, so the restriction is nondegenerate. For completeness, the same argument also shows A is nondegenerate: identify A with H^{d-2} via the injective map y -> L y. For y,y' in H^{d-2}, beta(L y,L y') = tr_X((xi cup y) cup (xi cup y')) = tr_X(y cup L^2 y'), using associativity and graded commutativity and the even degree of xi. If this vanishes for all y', then for every w in H^{d+2}, choosing y' with L^2 y'=w gives tr_X(y cup w)=0. By the perfect pairing H^{d-2} x H^{d+2}, y=0. Hence beta|_A is nondegenerate.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, let U be the open complement of Y in X, fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifying Tate twists with Q_ell, and let delta:H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) be the Gysin boundary. Let F_U and F_Y be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell) and H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1), respectively. Then F_Y delta = delta F_U.
proof:
Let f_X: X_k -> X_k be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism, i.e. the map induced by id_X x Spec(sigma_m), where sigma_m(c)=c^{q^m}. Since Y is defined over F_{q^m}, f_X preserves Y_k and U_k; write f_Y and f_U for the restrictions. Let F_X, F_U, F_Y^0 denote the induced q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius endomorphisms on H^*(X_k,Q_ell), H^*(U_k,Q_ell), H^*(Y_k,Q_ell), respectively. The F_Y in the statement is the induced Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1). In all applications of the cited lemmas below, the base prime power is q^m.

By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement, the pair (X_k,Y_k,U_k) has the long exact sequence ... -> H^{d-2}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) -> H^d(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^d(U_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d-1}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) -> ... with the last displayed arrow the Gysin boundary delta. This long exact sequence is the hypercohomology long exact sequence of the Gysin triangle R i_! Q_ell(-1)[-2] -> Q_ell -> R j_* Q_ell. Standard homological algebra gives a representative of this triangle as a short exact sequence of cochain complexes of Q_ell-vector spaces 0 -> A^* -> V^* -> B^* -> 0 such that H^n(A^*) can be identified with H^{n-2}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1), H^n(V^*) can be identified with H^n(X_k,Q_ell), H^n(B^*) can be identified with H^n(U_k,Q_ell), and the connecting homomorphism H^d(B^*) -> H^{d+1}(A^*) is the Gysin boundary delta.

The functoriality of the Gysin triangle for morphisms of smooth closed-open pairs applies to the automorphism f_X of the pair (X_k,Y_k,U_k). Thus, choosing a representative of this endomorphism of the triangle, we obtain a commutative diagram of short exact sequences of cochain complexes of Q_ell-vector spaces with vertical chain maps a:A^*->A^*, v:V^*->V^*, b:B^*->B^*. On cohomology, H^*(v) is F_X and H^*(b) is F_U. In degree d+1, H^{d+1}(a) is the Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1).

We justify the Tate-twist identification. By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77(a) applied to P^1 over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acts on Q_ell(-1) as multiplication by q^m. Hence, under the fixed identification of Q_ell(1) with Q_ell, H^{d+1}(a) is F_Y^0 tensor q^m, which is exactly the F_Y in the statement. If the Gysin map in the triangle is written as lambda i_!^0 for a normalized un-twisted Gysin map i_!^0, then the exact value of lambda is irrelevant: applying eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_207 to the closed immersion i:Y_k->X_k over F_{q^m} gives i_!^0 F_Y^0 = q^{-m} F_X i_!^0, because dim Y=d-1 and dim X=d. Therefore F_X(lambda i_!^0) = lambda i_!^0 (q^m F_Y^0), so the first square is Frobenius-compatible with the chosen Tate-twist identification. The second square is the usual pullback equivariance F_U j^* = j^* F_X, which follows from functoriality of pullback because f_X restricts to f_U. These checks do not by themselves imply the third square; the third square is supplied by the commutativity of the whole short exact sequence, not by the two squares alone.

Apply Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/3c0537 to the commutative diagram of short exact sequences with A'=A, V'=V, B'=B and vertical maps a,v,b. Let delta' be the connecting homomorphism of the second row; since the second row is the same short exact sequence, delta'=delta. For k=d, the lemma gives delta' H^d(b) = H^{d+1}(a) delta. Under the identifications above, H^d(b)=F_U and H^{d+1}(a)=F_Y. Hence F_Y delta = delta F_U. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and assume L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer n with 0<=n<=d. Put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Then the restriction of the Poincare duality pairing H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) x H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell(d) to P^d x P^d is nondegenerate.
proof: Let H^s denote H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). The cohomology ring H^*_et(X_k,Q_ell) is graded-commutative. With the implicit identification of Q_ell(1) with Q_ell used in the definition of L, let tr_X:H^{2d}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->Q_ell(d) be the Poincare duality trace. For homogeneous classes u,v with deg u+deg v=2d, put B(u,v)=tr_X(u cup v). In particular beta(u,v)=B(u,v) for u,v in H^d is the Poincare duality pairing on H^d. By Poincare duality for smooth projective geometrically connected varieties, beta is a nondegenerate bilinear form on H^d x H^d; equivalently the map H^d -> Hom_Q_ell(H^d,Q_ell(d)), u |-> (v |-> B(u,v)), is an isomorphism. The groups are finite-dimensional over Q_ell. First note that L is self-adjoint with respect to B. The class xi has degree 2, hence it commutes with every cohomology class under cup product. Therefore, for a in H^{d-2} and c in H^d, B(L a,c)=tr_X((a cup xi) cup c)=tr_X(a cup (xi cup c))=B(a,L c). If c is in P^d, then L c=0, so B(L a,c)=0. Thus L H^{d-2} is contained in P^{d,perp}:= {u in H^d : B(u,c)=0 for every c in P^d}. Now use the hard Lefschetz hypothesis. Taking n=d-2 gives that L^2:H^{d-2}->H^{d+2} is an isomorphism. Hence L:H^{d-2}->H^d is injective: if L a=0, then L^2 a=0, so a=0. Its image therefore has dimension dim H^{d-2}. For any x in H^d, surjectivity of L^2 gives a in H^{d-2} with L^2 a = L x. Then L(x-L a)=0, so x-L a lies in P^d. Thus H^d = L H^{d-2} + P^d. If L a lies in P^d, then L^2 a=0, and injectivity of L^2 gives a=0, hence L a=0. Therefore the sum is direct, and dim P^d = dim H^d - dim H^{d-2}. Because beta is nondegenerate on H^d, the map H^d -> Hom_Q_ell(P^d,Q_ell(d)) given by u |-> (c |-> B(u,c)) is surjective: compose the isomorphism H^d -> Hom_Q_ell(H^d,Q_ell(d)) with the restriction map Hom_Q_ell(H^d,Q_ell(d)) -> Hom_Q_ell(P^d,Q_ell(d)). Its kernel is exactly P^{d,perp}. Hence dim P^{d,perp} = dim H^d - dim P^d = dim H^{d-2}. Since L H^{d-2} is a subspace of P^{d,perp} and both have dimension dim H^{d-2}, we have P^{d,perp}=L H^{d-2}. Finally, let c in P^d and suppose B(c,c')=0 for every c' in P^d. Then c lies in P^{d,perp}=L H^{d-2}. But c also lies in P^d, and H^d is the direct sum L H^{d-2} directsum P^d. Hence c=0. This says that the restriction of beta to P^d x P^d has zero left radical; since P^d is finite-dimensional, this is exactly nondegeneracy of the restricted pairing. This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let beta be the Poincare pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then the restriction of beta to P^d is nondegenerate.
proof:
The target lemma is a restatement of the already-proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/32c5ae. We verify that the hypotheses and conclusion coincide exactly.

Hypotheses comparison:
1. Both assume q=p^a, ℓ≠p, m≥1, k=overline(𝔽_q), d≥2, and X a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over 𝔽_{q^m}. ✓
2. Both take ξ to be the cycle class of an 𝔽_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor and L to be cup product with ξ. The target's additional phrase "Fix a nonzero element of Q_ℓ(1)" is the standard convention for identifying the cycle class of a divisor, which naturally lives in H²_et(X_k, Q_ℓ(1)), with an element of H²_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) so that L = cup product with ξ is a map H^n_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{n+2}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ). This identification is implicit in the statement of 32c5ae, where L is likewise cup product with ξ acting on untwisted cohomology. The choice of the nonzero element of Q_ℓ(1) does not affect the nondegeneracy of the Poincaré pairing on P^d: it merely rescales ξ by a fixed nonzero scalar, and L^{d-n} being an isomorphism for all 0≤n≤d is invariant under such a rescaling (since rescaling L by a nonzero scalar preserves the property that its powers are isomorphisms). ✓
3. Both assume L^{d-n}: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{2d-n}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) is an isomorphism for 0≤n≤d. ✓
4. Both define P^d = ker(L: H^d_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{d+2}_et(X_k, Q_ℓ)). ✓
5. Both take β to be the Poincaré (duality) pairing on H^d_et(X_k, Q_ℓ). The terms "Poincare pairing" and "Poincare duality pairing" denote the same bilinear form β: H^d_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) × H^d_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) → Q_ℓ given by cup product followed by the trace map (integration over X). ✓

Conclusion comparison:
Both conclude that the restriction of β to P^d × P^d is nondegenerate, i.e., that the only element a ∈ P^d satisfying β(a, b) = 0 for every b ∈ P^d is a = 0 (equivalently, the radical of β|_{P^d} is {0}). ✓

Since every hypothesis of the target lemma is satisfied under the hypotheses of 32c5ae (with the observation about the fixed element of Q_ℓ(1) being a harmless notational convention), and the conclusion is identical, the target lemma follows immediately from Miner/16d24b0281973336/32c5ae.

More explicitly: given the data of the target lemma, the fixed nonzero element of Q_ℓ(1) identifies Q_ℓ(1) with Q_ℓ, so the cycle class ξ of the very ample divisor is an element of H²_et(X_k, Q_ℓ), and L = cup product with ξ satisfies all the stated isomorphism conditions. This is precisely the setup of 32c5ae, whose conclusion — that the restriction of the Poincaré pairing β to P^d is nondegenerate — is exactly the desired result.

statement: Let ell be a prime, let V be a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, let T be a Q_ell-linear automorphism of V, and suppose that the characteristic polynomial of T has coefficients in Q. Let q>0 be a real number and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C be an embedding. If every eigenvalue of T has complex absolute value q under sigma, then for every embedding tau:overline(Q_ell)->C and every eigenvalue lambda of T, |tau(lambda)|=q.
proof: Let L be the algebraic closure of Q_ell and let n=dim_{Q_ell} V. Put P(t)=det(tI-T) in Q_ell[t]. By hypothesis P(t) lies in Q[t]. If n=0, then P(t)=1, T has no eigenvalues, and the assertion is vacuous. Assume n>0. We use the standard fact that the eigenvalues of T in L are exactly the roots of P in L, counted with multiplicity; indeed P(lambda)=0 iff det(lambda I-T)=0 iff lambda I-T is not invertible, and the multiplicity of a root is the algebraic multiplicity of the corresponding eigenvalue. Since L is algebraically closed, P(t)=prod_{j=1}^n (t-lambda_j) in L[t], where the lambda_j are the eigenvalues of T, counted with multiplicity. Let sigma:L->C be the given embedding. Every field embedding of L into C fixes the prime field Q, hence it fixes the rational coefficients of P; thus sigma(P)=P. Applying sigma to the displayed factorization gives P(t)=prod_{j=1}^n (t-sigma(lambda_j)) in C[t]. This is a factorization of the degree n polynomial P into n linear factors over C, so the multiset {sigma(lambda_j)} is exactly the multiset of all roots of P in C, counted with multiplicity. By the hypothesis, |sigma(lambda_j)|=q for every j. Therefore every root of P in C has complex absolute value q. Now let tau:L->C be any embedding and let lambda be any eigenvalue of T, i.e. a root of P in L. Since P(lambda)=0 and tau fixes Q, we have 0=tau(P(lambda))=tau(P)(tau(lambda))=P(tau(lambda)). Hence tau(lambda) is a root of P in C. By the preceding paragraph, |tau(lambda)|=q. This completes the proof.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K, let sigma:Kbar->C be an embedding, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let T in GL_K(V), and let h be a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((T tensor id)x,(T tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h(x,y) for all x,y. Then T is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue lambda of T in Kbar satisfies |sigma(lambda)| = sqrt(sigma(c)).
proof:
We apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/708de0 with the choice W = V.

Verification of the hypotheses of 708de0:

(1) K is a field of characteristic 0 — given in the target statement.

(2) Kbar is an algebraic closure of K — given.

(3) sigma: Kbar -> C is an embedding — given.

(4) V is a finite-dimensional K-vector space — given.

(5) T in GL_K(V) — given.

(6) c in K^* with sigma(c) > 0 — given.

(7) h is a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = c h(x,y) for all x, y. The target hypothesis states h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h(x,y) for all x, y. Since c in K^* is a scalar and the Hermitian form h takes values in C, the expression c h(x,y) in the statement of 708de0 means the scalar c viewed in C via the embedding sigma|_K: K -> C (the restriction of sigma to K, which is well-defined since K embeds in Kbar), multiplied by h(x,y). This equals sigma(c) h(x,y), which is precisely the condition in the target. So the hypotheses match.

(8) W is a T-stable K-subspace of V. We take W = V. Since T in GL_K(V) is a K-linear automorphism of V, T(V) = V, so V is T-stable. Also, V is trivially a K-subspace of itself. Thus W = V satisfies the requirement.

Conclusion from 708de0: With W = V, the conclusion of 708de0 states that T|_W = T|_V = T is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue of T|_W = T has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c)).

Unpacking the conclusion: "T is diagonalizable over Kbar" means that T is diagonalizable over Kbar, exactly as required. "Every eigenvalue of T has complex absolute value sqrt(sigma(c))" means that for every eigenvalue lambda of T in Kbar, the complex number sigma(lambda) (the image of lambda under the embedding sigma: Kbar -> C) satisfies |sigma(lambda)| = sqrt(sigma(c)), which is exactly the required conclusion.

Therefore, T is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue lambda of T in Kbar satisfies |sigma(lambda)| = sqrt(sigma(c)).

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}, let U=X\Y, and let delta:H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) be the boundary map of the Gysin sequence of the pair Y subset X. Then the image of delta is nondegenerate for the Poincare duality pairing on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1).
proof:
Let V = H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1). We fix a nonzero element of Q_ℓ(1) to identify all Tate twists with Q_ℓ; nondegeneracy is independent of this choice. Under this identification, the Poincaré duality pairing on V is the perfect pairing B: V × V → Q_ℓ given by B(a, b) = tr_Y(a ∪ b), where tr_Y: H^{2d-2}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) → Q_ℓ is the Poincaré duality trace on Y (which has pure dimension d−1). By eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77 (part (b)), this pairing is perfect.

Let S = im(δ) ⊂ V, where δ: H^d_{ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1) is the Gysin boundary. We prove S is nondegenerate for B by showing S ∩ S^⊥ = 0, where S^⊥ = {v ∈ V : B(v, w) = 0 for all w ∈ S}. For a perfect pairing on a finite-dimensional space, a subspace is nondegenerate if and only if its intersection with its orthogonal complement is zero; this is a standard linear-algebra fact (if S ∩ S^⊥ = 0, then dim S + dim S^⊥ = dim V, so the restriction B|_{S×S} has trivial radical).

Step 1: Identify S^⊥ with τ^{-1}(im(i^*)).

Let θ: H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) → H^d_{c,ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) be the connecting homomorphism of the compact-support localization sequence for the pair (X, Y) with U = X \ Y. By Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_localization_les_finite_type, the localization long exact sequence contains the segment
  H^{d-1}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) →^{i^*} H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) →^{θ} H^d_{c,ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) → H^d_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ),
which is exact. Hence ker(θ) = im(i^*).

We now use the standard adjunction between the Gysin boundary δ and the localization boundary θ, which follows from the compatibility of the two long exact sequences (the Gysin sequence for Y ⊂ X and the localization sequence for U ⊂ X) under Poincaré duality on X. Concretely, for u ∈ H^d_{ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) and y ∈ H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) (after the twist identification), one has
  B(δ(u), y) = ⟨u, θ(y)⟩,
where ⟨,⟩: H^d_{ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) × H^d_{c,ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) → Q_ℓ is the Poincaré duality pairing on U. This pairing is perfect because U is a smooth variety of pure dimension d over the algebraically closed field k (Poincaré duality for smooth varieties of finite type with compact supports gives a perfect pairing H^n(U) × H^{2d-n}_c(U) → Q_ℓ for every n; taking n = d gives the pairing used here).

To justify the adjunction: the Gysin sequence (from eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement) and the localization sequence are dual to each other under the perfect Poincaré duality pairings on X, Y, and U. The connecting homomorphisms δ and θ are the dual maps under this identification, which yields B(δ(u), y) = ⟨u, θ(y)⟩. This is the same compatibility that underlies the Gysin projection formula characterisation in eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor, applied to the connecting maps rather than to the maps in the sequences.

Since ⟨,⟩ is perfect, for y ∈ V (identified with H^{d-1}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) via the twist identification τ: V → H^{d-1}(Y_k, Q_ℓ)):
  y ∈ S^⊥  ⇔  B(δ(u), y) = 0 for all u ∈ H^d(U)  ⇔  ⟨u, θ(τ(y))⟩ = 0 for all u  ⇔  θ(τ(y)) = 0  ⇔  τ(y) ∈ ker(θ) = im(i^*).
Therefore S^⊥ = τ^{-1}(im(i^*)).

Step 2: Show S ∩ S^⊥ = 0.

Take y ∈ S ∩ S^⊥. Then:
  (a) y = δ(u) for some u ∈ H^d_{ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ).
  (b) τ(y) = i^*(x) for some x ∈ H^{d-1}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ).

By the Gysin sequence (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_ordinary_gysin_sequence_open_complement), the segment
  H^d_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) →^{j^*} H^d_{ét}(U_k, Q_ℓ) →^{δ} H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1) →^{i_!} H^{d+1}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ)
is exact, so im(δ) = ker(i_!). Since y ∈ S = im(δ), we have i_!(y) = 0.

Now compute i_!(y). The Gysin map i_!: H^{d-1}(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1) → H^{d+1}(X_k, Q_ℓ) is the untwisted Gysin map i_!^0: H^{d-1}(Y_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{d+1}(X_k, Q_ℓ) composed with the twist identification. Thus i_!(y) = i_!^0(τ(y)) = i_!^0(i^*(x)).

By the projection formula (eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_439_gysin_projection_formula_divisor), for every n ≥ 0 and every x ∈ H^n_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ), one has i_!(i^*(x)) = x ∪ ξ, where ξ ∈ H^2_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) is the cycle class of Y under the fixed twist identification. Taking n = d−1, we get
  i_!^0(i^*(x)) = x ∪ ξ =: Lx.
Since i_!(y) = 0, it follows that Lx = 0.

We now invoke the hard Lefschetz theorem, a standard theorem of algebraic geometry: for a smooth projective variety of pure dimension d over a field and an ample divisor class ξ, the map L: H^{d-1} → H^{d+1} given by cup product with ξ is an isomorphism (for every Tate twist). Since Y is very ample, ξ = [Y] is an ample class, so L: H^{d-1}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) → H^{d+1}_{ét}(X_k, Q_ℓ) is an isomorphism, in particular injective. From Lx = 0 we conclude x = 0.

Therefore τ(y) = i^*(x) = i^*(0) = 0, and since τ is an isomorphism (twist identification), y = 0.

This shows S ∩ S^⊥ = 0.

Step 3: Conclusion.

Since B is a perfect pairing on the finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector space V and S ∩ S^⊥ = 0, the restriction of B to S × S is nondegenerate. Hence S = im(δ) is nondegenerate for the Poincaré duality pairing on H^{d-1}_{ét}(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1), as required.

Remark on the edge case d = 2: when d = 2, Y is a smooth curve and V = H^1(Y_k, Q_ℓ)(-1). The Gysin boundary is δ: H^2(U) → H^1(Y)(-1), the localization boundary is θ: H^1(Y) → H^2_c(U), and the hard Lefschetz theorem gives L: H^1(X) → H^3(X) an isomorphism (equivalently, by Poincaré duality on X, L: H^1(X) → H^1(X)(1) is an isomorphism). The argument above applies verbatim without modification.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, suppose F L=q^m L F for L:H^{d-2}->H^d and for L:H^d->H^{d+2}, and put P^d=ker(L:H^d->H^{d+2}). Then H^d is the direct sum of the image of L:H^{d-2}->H^d and P^d as Q_ell[F]-modules.
proof:
All checks confirm the proof is self-contained. The key ingredients are (i) the isomorphism $L^2 = L_d \circ L_{d-2}: H^{d-2} 	o H^{d+2}$, a special case of the hard-Lefschetz hypothesis at $n=d-2$, and (ii) the two Frobenius-commutation relations given in the statement. Both the vector-space decomposition and the $F$-stability of the summands follow directly.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/cb62f7",
  "cited_lemmas": [],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We prove that H^d = im(L_{d-2}) \oplus P^d as Q_ell[F]-modules, where L_{d-2}:H^{d-2}->H^d and L_d:H^d->H^{d+2} are the two cup-product maps with xi, and P^d=ker(L_d). We write F_s for the restriction of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F to H^s.

STEP 0 (the key isomorphism). The hypothesis says L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d. Since d>=2, the index n=d-2 is admissible, and L^{d-(d-2)}=L^2:H^{d-2}->H^{2d-(d-2)}=H^{d+2} is an isomorphism. Concretely L^2 = L_d \circ L_{d-2}:H^{d-2}->H^{d+2} is an isomorphism.

STEP 1 (the two Frobenius commutation relations, made explicit). The hypothesis 'FL=q^m LF for L:H^{d-2}->H^d' reads F_d \circ L_{d-2} = q^m L_{d-2} \circ F_{d-2}. The hypothesis 'FL=q^m LF for L:H^d->H^{d+2}' reads F_{d+2} \circ L_d = q^m L_d \circ F_d. We use both below. Note q^m is a nonzero element of Q_ell (indeed a unit, since q=p^a is a prime power so q^m>=2 is a nonzero rational number).

STEP 2 (sum: H^d = A + P^d). Let A = im(L_{d-2}) \subseteq H^d. Take any x in H^d. Then L_d(x) is in H^{d+2}. Because L^2:H^{d-2}->H^{d+2} is surjective, there exists a unique y in H^{d-2} with L^2(y)=L_d(x). Define z = x - L_{d-2}(y), which lies in H^d. Then L_d(z) = L_d(x) - L_d(L_{d-2}(y)) = L_d(x) - L^2(y) = L_d(x) - L_d(x) = 0. Hence z in ker(L_d)=P^d, and x = L_{d-2}(y) + z with L_{d-2}(y) in A. Thus every x in H^d is a sum of an element of A and an element of P^d, so H^d = A + P^d.

STEP 3 (intersection: A \cap P^d = {0}). Let w in A \cap P^d. Then w = L_{d-2}(y) for some y in H^{d-2}, and L_d(w)=0. Therefore 0 = L_d(w) = L_d(L_{d-2}(y)) = L^2(y). Since L^2 is injective, y=0, hence w = L_{d-2}(0) = 0. So A \cap P^d = {0}.

From Steps 2 and 3, H^d = A \oplus P^d as Q_ell-vector spaces.

STEP 4 (A is F-stable). Let a in A; then a = L_{d-2}(y) for some y in H^{d-2}. By the relation F_d \circ L_{d-2} = q^m L_{d-2} \circ F_{d-2}, F_d(a) = F_d(L_{d-2}(y)) = q^m L_{d-2}(F_{d-2}(y)), which lies in A. Hence F_d(A) \subseteq A.

STEP 5 (P^d is F-stable). Let z in P^d, so L_d(z)=0. By the relation F_{d+2} \circ L_d = q^m L_d \circ F_d, applied to z, we get F_{d+2}(L_d(z)) = q^m L_d(F_d(z)). The left-hand side is F_{d+2}(0)=0, so 0 = q^m L_d(F_d(z)). Since q^m is a nonzero element of Q_ell, L_d(F_d(z))=0, i.e. F_d(z) in P^d. Hence F_d(P^d) \subseteq P^d.

CONCLUSION. H^d = A \oplus P^d as Q_ell-vector spaces, and both summands A = im(L_{d-2}) and P^d = ker(L_d) are stable under F. Therefore H^d is the direct sum of the image of L:H^{d-2}->H^d and P^d as Q_ell[F]-modules."
}

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K, let sigma:Kbar->C be an embedding, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space with a decomposition V=V_1 direct sum V_2, let T be an element of GL_K(V) preserving V_1 and V_2, and let R>0. If for i=1,2 the restriction of T to V_i is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue of that restriction, viewed in Kbar, satisfies |sigma(lambda)|=R, then T is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue of T, viewed in Kbar, satisfies |sigma(lambda)|=R.
proof:
Write T_i := T|_{V_i} for i=1,2. The proof is in five steps; the assumptions char(K)=0 and T in GL_K(V) are not used in the argument, so they are a fortiori compatible with it.

Step 1 (block form of T). Choose a K-basis B_i of V_i (if V_i = 0 take the empty basis) and set B = B_1 ∪ B_2, which is a K-basis of V since V = V_1 ⊕ V_2. For v ∈ V_i we have T v ∈ V_i by hypothesis, hence the coordinates of T v along B_j (j ≠ i) all vanish. Therefore the matrix M_T of T in the basis B is block diagonal, M_T = [[M_1, 0],[0, M_2]], where M_i is the matrix of T_i in the basis B_i.

Step 2 (characteristic polynomial). For a block diagonal matrix the determinant factors: det(tI − M_T) = det(tI_1 − M_1)·det(tI_2 − M_2), because tI − M_T is block triangular with diagonal blocks tI_1 − M_1 and tI_2 − M_2, and the determinant of a block triangular matrix is the product of the determinants of the diagonal blocks. Hence χ_T(t) = χ_{T_1}(t)·χ_{T_2}(t) in K[t] ⊂ Kbar[t].

Step 3 (eigenspace decompositions of the restrictions). For i = 1,2 let Λ_i ⊆ Kbar be the set of eigenvalues of T_i in Kbar (finite, possibly empty; it is empty exactly when V_i = 0). Since T_i is diagonalizable over Kbar, after scalar extension V_i ⊗_K Kbar decomposes as the direct sum of its eigenspaces: V_i ⊗_K Kbar = ⊕_{λ∈Λ_i} E_{i,λ}, where E_{i,λ} = ker_{V_i⊗Kbar}(T_i − λ) and every nonzero vector of E_{i,λ} is an eigenvector of T_i with eigenvalue λ.

Step 4 (T is diagonalizable over Kbar). Scalar extension commutes with finite direct sums, so (V_1 ⊕ V_2) ⊗_K Kbar = (V_1⊗_K Kbar) ⊕ (V_2⊗_K Kbar). Combining with Step 3 gives
V ⊗_K Kbar = ⊕_{λ∈Λ_1 ∪ Λ_2} (E_{1,λ} ⊕ E_{2,λ}),
where E_{i,λ} is read as the zero subspace if λ ∉ Λ_i. Now take v ∈ E_{1,λ} ⊕ E_{2,λ}, v = v_1 + v_2 with v_i ∈ E_{i,λ}. Then (T⊗id)(v) = T_1 v_1 + T_2 v_2 = λ v_1 + λ v_2 = λ v, since each v_i is either zero or an eigenvector of T_i with eigenvalue λ. Thus every vector of E_{1,λ} ⊕ E_{2,λ} is an eigenvector of T⊗id with eigenvalue λ (or is zero). Therefore V⊗_K Kbar is the direct sum of the eigenspaces of T⊗id over Kbar, i.e. T⊗id is diagonalizable over Kbar, which is precisely the statement that T is diagonalizable over Kbar.

Step 5 (eigenvalues of T). By Step 2, χ_T = χ_{T_1}·χ_{T_2}. Since T_i is diagonalizable over Kbar, its characteristic polynomial splits completely over Kbar: χ_{T_i}(t) = ∏_{λ∈Λ_i} (t−λ)^{a_{i,λ}} with integers a_{i,λ} ≥ 1 (the algebraic multiplicities, equal to dim E_{i,λ}). Hence χ_T splits completely over Kbar, and the set of roots of χ_T in Kbar is exactly Λ_1 ∪ Λ_2, since a polynomial over a field has a root λ iff the product of two polynomials does, and the roots of a product are the union of the roots of the factors. The eigenvalues of T in Kbar are precisely the roots of χ_T in Kbar: λ ∈ Kbar is an eigenvalue of T iff det(T − λ·id_V) = 0 iff χ_T(λ) = 0. Consequently the set of eigenvalues of T in Kbar is exactly Λ_1 ∪ Λ_2. By hypothesis, every λ ∈ Λ_i satisfies |σ(λ)| = R; hence every eigenvalue λ of T, viewed in Kbar, satisfies |σ(λ)| = R.

Edge cases. If V_1 = 0 (resp. V_2 = 0), then Λ_1 = ∅ (resp. Λ_2 = ∅), χ_{T_1} = 1 (resp. χ_{T_2} = 1), the hypothesis on that summand is vacuous, and Steps 1–5 reduce to the single nonzero summand, so the conclusion still holds. If V = 0, both summands vanish, T is the identity on the zero space, which is diagonalizable, and the assertion on eigenvalues is vacuously true. In all cases the two conclusions are established: T is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue of T in Kbar satisfies |σ(λ)| = R. QED.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), and let beta be the Poincare pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell). Then P^d is the orthogonal complement of the image of L:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) with respect to beta.
proof: Write H^r for H^r_et(X_k, Q_ell). Let tr: H^{2d}(X_k, Q_ell) -> Q_ell be the Poincare trace after the fixed identification of Tate twists with Q_ell. Since d>=2, we have d+2 <= 2d. By the cited Poincare duality lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_271, applied to X over F_{q^m} with n=d+2, the pairing gamma(u,y)=tr(u cup y) on H^{d+2} x H^{d-2} is perfect. Let I = im(L: H^{d-2} -> H^d). The orthogonal complement of I with respect to beta is the set of x in H^d such that beta(x, L y)=0 for every y in H^{d-2}. If x in P^d, then Lx=0. For any y in H^{d-2}, L y = xi cup y. Because deg xi = 2, x cup xi = xi cup x. Therefore beta(x, L y) = tr(x cup (xi cup y)) = tr((x cup xi) cup y) = tr((L x) cup y) = 0. Hence P^d is contained in the orthogonal complement of I. Conversely, if x in H^d satisfies beta(x, L y)=0 for every y in H^{d-2}, then for every y we have 0 = beta(x, L y) = tr(x cup (xi cup y)) = tr((L x) cup y) = gamma(L x, y). Since gamma is perfect, the only u in H^{d+2} with gamma(u, y)=0 for all y in H^{d-2} is u=0. Taking u=Lx gives Lx=0, so x in P^d. Thus P^d is exactly the orthogonal complement of im(L: H^{d-2} -> H^d) with respect to beta. The hard Lefschetz hypotheses are part of the ambient setup; the orthogonality follows from Poincare duality and the associativity of the cup product.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, set P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), let F be the q^m-power Frobenius, assume FL=q^mLF, and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C. If the restriction of F to P^d is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) and every eigenvalue of the restriction of F to P^d, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{md/2}, then P^d tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=q^{md}h(x,y) for all x,y in P^d tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C.
proof: Let V = P^d = ker(L: H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)). Since H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space, V is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space. Put K = Q_ell. Then K has characteristic 0. Let c = q^{md}. This is a nonzero rational integer, so c in K^*. The embedding sigma fixes Q, hence sigma(c) = q^{md}, which is positive; therefore sqrt(sigma(c)) = q^{md/2}. We now show that V is F-stable. Let x in V. Then Lx = 0. The assumed identity FL = q^m LF is the identity of endomorphisms H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell) -> H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell), so for this x we have (FL)(x) = q^m (LF)(x). Thus 0 = F(Lx) = (FL)(x) = q^m (LF)(x) = q^m L(Fx). Since q^m is nonzero in Q_ell, L(Fx) = 0. Hence Fx in V. Notice that the equality used is (FL)(x) = q^m (LF)(x), which is exactly the stated hypothesis, not the reverse. Therefore the restriction T = F|_V is well defined. The q^m-power Frobenius F is an automorphism of H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), and because V is F-stable, T is an automorphism of V; explicitly its inverse is F^{-1}|_V. Thus T in GL_K(V). By hypothesis, T is diagonalizable over overline(K). For every eigenvalue alpha of T in overline(K), the hypothesis that alpha has Weil absolute value q^{md/2} means that under the given embedding sigma: overline(K) -> C its complex absolute value is q^{md/2}; hence |sigma(alpha)| = q^{md/2} = sqrt(sigma(c)). Now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/ccebfa to K, sigma, c, V, and T. It yields a positive definite Hermitian form h on V tensor_{K,sigma} C such that h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h(x,y) for all x,y in V tensor_{K,sigma} C. Since sigma(c) = q^{md}, this is h((T tensor id)x, (T tensor id)y) = q^{md} h(x,y). Finally, because T is the restriction of F to P^d, T tensor id is exactly F tensor id on P^d tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C. Replacing V by P^d and T by F|_{P^d} gives the required positive definite Hermitian form h on P^d tensor_{Q_ell,sigma} C with h((F tensor id)x, (F tensor id)y) = q^{md} h(x,y) for all x,y.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. Let beta be the Poincare pairing on H^d. Then the restriction of beta to the image of L:H^{d-2}->H^d is nondegenerate.
proof:
I have everything needed. The target lemma is a direct corollary of the proved lemma `Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/ec9fd1`, whose hypotheses are identical to the target's and whose conclusion (β perfect on each summand of `H^d = L(H^{d-2}) ⊕ P^d`) implies β is perfect — hence nondegenerate — on `L(H^{d-2}) = im(L: H^{d-2} → H^d)`.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/27640a",
  "cited_lemmas": ["Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/ec9fd1"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "Let V := H^d = H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell). First I identify the objects in the target statement with those in the proved lemma Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/ec9fd1. The pairing beta in the target is the Poincare duality pairing on H^d, i.e. the Q_ell-bilinear form beta(x,y) = tr_X(x cup y) with tr_X: H^{2d}_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> Q_ell the Poincare duality trace (the fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1) identifies the Tate twist Q_ell(d) with Q_ell, so that beta lands in Q_ell). This is exactly the pairing beta(x,y) = tr_X(x cup y) used in ec9fd1, with V = H^d_et(X_k, Q_ell) and P^d = ker(L: V -> H^{d+2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)). The subspace in the target, the image of L: H^{d-2} -> H^d, is exactly the Q_ell-subspace L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)) appearing in ec9fd1.\n\nNow I check that the hypotheses of the target are precisely the hypotheses of ec9fd1. In both: q = p^a is a prime power, ell != p is prime, m >= 1, k = overline(F_q), X is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d >= 2 over F_{q^m}, a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) is fixed, xi is the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, L is cup product with xi, and L^{d-n}: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^{2d-n}_et(X_k, Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every integer 0 <= n <= d. (The target's hypothesis 'L^{d-n}: H^n -> H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0 <= n <= d' is verbatim the same assumption, and d >= 2 guarantees d-2 >= 0 so that H^{d-2} and the map L: H^{d-2} -> H^d are well defined.) Thus every hypothesis of ec9fd1 is satisfied by the data of the target.\n\nBy ec9fd1, under these common hypotheses, V = L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)) direct-sum P^d, this direct sum is orthogonal for beta, and beta restricts to a perfect pairing on each of the two summands. In particular, beta restricts to a perfect pairing on the summand L(H^{d-2}_et(X_k, Q_ell)) = im(L: H^{d-2} -> H^d).\n\nFinally, a perfect bilinear pairing is, by definition, nondegenerate on both sides. Therefore the restriction of beta to im(L: H^{d-2} -> H^d) x im(L: H^{d-2} -> H^d) is nondegenerate. This is exactly the statement to be proved. QED."
}

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 with embedding sigma:K->C, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let F in GL_K(V), and suppose V=W direct sum Z as F-stable K-subspaces. If W tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_W with h_W((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h_W(x,y), and Z tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_Z with h_Z((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h_Z(x,y), then V tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h(x,y).
proof:
We prove the result by a direct application of the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/550524.

Setup and identification. We are given: a field K of characteristic 0 with an embedding sigma:K->C; a finite-dimensional K-vector space V; an element c in K^* with sigma(c)>0; an operator F in GL_K(V); and a decomposition V = W ⊕ Z into F-stable K-subspaces. Since V is finite-dimensional over K, both W and Z are finite-dimensional K-vector spaces.

Because F preserves W and Z (i.e., F(W) ⊆ W and F(Z) ⊆ Z) and F is invertible on V, the restrictions F|_W : W -> W and F|_Z : Z -> Z are K-linear automorphisms, so T_1 := F|_W ∈ GL_K(W) and T_2 := F|_Z ∈ GL_K(Z). Moreover, with respect to the direct-sum decomposition V = W ⊕ Z, the operator F is precisely the direct sum T_1 ⊕ T_2: for any v ∈ V, write v = w + z with w ∈ W, z ∈ Z (unique by the direct-sum hypothesis); then F(v) = F(w) + F(z) = F|_W(w) + F|_Z(z) = (T_1 ⊕ T_2)(v).

Matching the hypotheses of 550524. We now verify each hypothesis of the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/550524 under the identification V_1 = W, V_2 = Z, T_1 = F|_W, T_2 = F|_Z:

(1) K is a field of characteristic 0. ✓ (given)
(2) sigma:K->C is an embedding. ✓ (given)
(3) c ∈ K^* with sigma(c) > 0. ✓ (given)
(4) V = V_1 ⊕ V_2 is a direct sum of finite-dimensional K-vector spaces. ✓ (V = W ⊕ Z, both finite-dimensional as K-subspaces of the finite-dimensional space V)
(5) T_i ∈ GL_K(V_i) for i = 1,2. ✓ (T_1 = F|_W ∈ GL_K(W), T_2 = F|_Z ∈ GL_K(Z))
(6) For i = 1,2, there is a positive definite Hermitian form h_i on V_i ⊗_{K,sigma} C such that h_i((T_i ⊗ id)x, (T_i ⊗ id)y) = c · h_i(x,y) for all x, y. The target hypothesis gives exactly this: h_W on W ⊗_{K,sigma} C is a positive definite Hermitian form satisfying h_W((F ⊗ id)x, (F ⊗ id)y) = sigma(c) · h_W(x,y) for all x, y ∈ W ⊗_{K,sigma} C. Since F|_W = T_1, this reads h_W((T_1 ⊗ id)x, (T_1 ⊗ id)y) = sigma(c) · h_W(x,y). The equation in 550524 is written as h_i((T_i ⊗ id)x, (T_i ⊗ id)y) = c · h_i(x,y); because h_i is C-valued, the scalar c on the right is understood as its image sigma(c) ∈ C under the given embedding, so the two equations are identical. The same verification applies to h_Z on Z ⊗_{K,sigma} C with T_2 = F|_Z. ✓
(7) T = T_1 ⊕ T_2. ✓ (shown above: F = T_1 ⊕ T_2)

Conclusion. By Miner/16d24b0281973336/550524, there exists a positive definite Hermitian form h on V ⊗_{K,sigma} C such that h((T ⊗ id)x, (T ⊗ id)y) = c · h(x,y) for all x, y ∈ V ⊗_{K,sigma} C, i.e., h((F ⊗ id)x, (F ⊗ id)y) = sigma(c) · h(x,y) for all x, y. This is exactly the desired conclusion.

For explicitness, the form h furnished by 550524 is the direct-sum form h = h_W ⊕ h_Z: under the canonical isomorphism V ⊗_{K,sigma} C ≅ (W ⊗_{K,sigma} C) ⊕ (Z ⊗_{K,sigma} C), one sets h((w, z), (w', z')) = h_W(w, w') + h_Z(z, z'). This is Hermitian (sum of Hermitian forms), positive definite (for (w,z) ≠ 0 at least one component is nonzero, and the sum of two non-negative reals, at least one strictly positive, is strictly positive), and satisfies the scaling identity because each summand does: h((F⊗id)(w,z), (F⊗id)(w',z')) = h_W(Fw, Fw') + h_Z(Fz, Fz') = sigma(c)(h_W(w,w') + h_Z(z,z')) = sigma(c) h((w,z),(w',z')).

This completes the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Write H^s=H^s_et(X_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, and suppose L^{d-n}:H^n->H^{2d-n} is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d, put P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r->H^{2d-r+2}). Then the bilinear form (x,y)->tr_X(L^{d-r}x cup y) on P^r x P^r is nondegenerate, where tr_X is the Poincare trace to Q_ell(-d) identified with Q_ell.
proof:
The hypotheses of the target lemma are exactly the hypotheses of the proved lemma Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_542. Indeed, we have q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=1, X smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, a fixed nonzero element of Q_ell(1), an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor with cycle class xi, L given by cup product with xi, and the hard Lefschetz assumption that L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for every 0<=n<=d. For 0<=r<=d we define P^r=ker(L^{d-r+1}:H^r_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-r+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), exactly as in the cited lemma.

The cited lemma states that, with the same notation, the bilinear form beta_r(x,y)=tr_X(L^{d-r}x cup y) restricts to a perfect pairing on P^r. A perfect bilinear form is, by definition, nondegenerate in each variable: if x in P^r satisfies beta_r(x,y)=0 for every y in P^r, then x=0, and similarly if y satisfies beta_r(x,y)=0 for every x in P^r, then y=0.

The only possible difference between the form in the target statement and the form in the cited lemma is the choice of the identification of Q_ell(-d) with Q_ell. The cited lemma uses a fixed normalized Poincare trace, while the present statement uses the Poincare trace to Q_ell(-d) followed by an identification with Q_ell. Any two such identifications differ by multiplication by a nonzero scalar in Q_ell^*. Multiplying a perfect bilinear form by a nonzero scalar preserves perfectness, hence also preserves nondegeneracy. Therefore the bilinear form (x,y)->tr_X(L^{d-r}x cup y) on P^r x P^r is nondegenerate.

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 with embedding sigma:K->C, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let F in GL_K(V), and let h be a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h(x,y). Let W be an F-stable K-subspace of V, and let W^perp be the set of v in V tensor_{K,sigma} C such that h(v,w)=0 for all w in W tensor_{K,sigma} C. Then W^perp is F-stable.
proof:
We must show that for every v in W^perp, the element (F ⊗ id)(v) also lies in W^perp, i.e., that h((F ⊗ id)(v), w') = 0 for every w' ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C.

Step 1: F|_W is an automorphism of W. Since F ∈ GL_K(V), F is a K-linear automorphism of V. Since W is F-stable (F(W) ⊆ W) and F is invertible with F^{-1} also K-linear, we have W = F(F^{-1}(W)) ⊆ F^{-1}(W) (applying F to the inclusion F^{-1}(W) ⊆ V gives W ⊆ V, but more precisely: for any w ∈ W, write w = F(u) for some u ∈ V since F is surjective; then F^{-1}(w) = u, and since W is F-stable, F(F^{-1}(w)) = w ∈ W, so F^{-1}(w) ∈ F^{-1}(W) ⊆ V; but we need F^{-1}(W) ⊆ W. Take w ∈ W. Since F is surjective, w = F(u) for some u ∈ V. Then F^{-1}(w) = u. Now F(u) = w ∈ W, and since W is F-stable this does not directly give u ∈ W. Instead: since F is an automorphism and F(W) ⊆ W, we have F(W) = W. Indeed, dim_K F(W) = dim_K W (F is injective), and F(W) ⊆ W, so F(W) = W by equal dimension. Hence F|_W : W → W is a K-linear isomorphism.

Step 2: F ⊗ id maps W ⊗_{K,σ} C onto W ⊗_{K,σ} C. The restriction (F|_W) ⊗ id : W ⊗_{K,σ} C → W ⊗_{K,σ} C is a C-linear isomorphism (it is the tensor product of the K-linear isomorphism F|_W with the identity on C, and since F|_W has a K-linear inverse, its tensor product with id has a C-linear inverse). In particular it is surjective: for every w' ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C there exists w ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C such that w' = (F ⊗ id)(w).

Step 3: Verify F-stability of W^perp. Let v ∈ W^perp, meaning h(v, w) = 0 for all w ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C. We claim (F ⊗ id)(v) ∈ W^perp. Take any w' ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C. By Step 2, there exists w ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C with w' = (F ⊗ id)(w). Then by the given hypothesis on h,
h((F ⊗ id)(v), w') = h((F ⊗ id)(v), (F ⊗ id)(w)) = σ(c) · h(v, w) = σ(c) · 0 = 0,
where the first equality is the substitution w' = (F⊗id)(w), the second equality is the hypothesis h((F⊗id)x, (F⊗id)y) = σ(c)h(x,y) applied with x = v and y = w, and the last equality uses v ∈ W^perp and w ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C. Since w' was arbitrary, h((F⊗id)(v), w') = 0 for all w' ∈ W ⊗_{K,σ} C, so (F⊗id)(v) ∈ W^perp.

Step 4: Conclusion. We have shown that for every v ∈ W^perp, (F ⊗ id)(v) ∈ W^perp, i.e., W^perp is invariant under F ⊗ id. Since F ⊗ id is the action of F on V ⊗_{K,σ} C, this means W^perp is F-stable. ∎

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, let X be a smooth projective variety over F_q, and put k=overline(F_q). Suppose there exists an integer m>=1 such that the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(X_{F_{q^m},k},Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every integer i>=0. Then the inverse of the q-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(X_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every integer i>=0.
proof:
Fix the integer m>=1 whose existence is assumed in the hypothesis. Set X_m = X x_{Spec F_q} Spec F_{q^m} = X_{F_{q^m}}. Since k = overline(F_q) is an extension field of F_{q^m}, base change is associative, so (X_m)_k = X_{F_{q^m},k} = X_k, and this identification is canonical. Thus the group H^i_et(X_{F_{q^m},k}, Q_ell) in the hypothesis is the same vector space as H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) for every i>=0.

Step 1 (the q-power arithmetic Frobenius is invertible). For each i>=0 let T_i denote the q-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell), i.e. the pullback map (id_X x Spec sigma)^* induced by the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphism (id_X x Spec sigma): X_k -> X_k, where sigma: k -> k is sigma(c)=c^q. Because k = overline(F_q) is algebraically closed, sigma is an automorphism of k (its inverse is c -> c^{1/q}, well-defined and bijective). Hence id_X x Spec sigma is an automorphism of the scheme X_k, and its pullback T_i on etale cohomology with Q_ell coefficients is an invertible Q_ell-linear endomorphism of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell). In particular T_i is invertible for every i>=0.

Step 2 (the q^m-power Frobenius is the m-th power of the q-power Frobenius). We use the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_44, which states: for every n>=0 there is a canonical Q_ell-linear isomorphism phi_n: H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell) -> H^n_et((X_m)_k, Q_ell) under which the arithmetic Frobenius over F_{q^m} (the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^n_et((X_m)_k, Q_ell)) corresponds to the m-th power of the arithmetic Frobenius over F_q (acting on H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell)). In formulas, if (Frob_{q^m})^* denotes the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^n_et((X_m)_k, Q_ell), then phi_n o T_n^m = (Frob_{q^m})^* o phi_n, i.e. (Frob_{q^m})^* = phi_n o T_n^m o phi_n^{-1}. Thus (Frob_{q^m})^* on H^n_et((X_m)_k, Q_ell) is conjugate to T_n^m on H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell), and therefore (Frob_{q^m})^* is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^n_et((X_m)_k, Q_ell) if and only if T_n^m is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^n_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Step 3 (translate the hypothesis). The hypothesis of the target lemma says that for every i>=0 the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(X_{F_{q^m},k}, Q_ell) = H^i_et((X_m)_k, Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). By the equivalence established in Step 2, it follows that for every i>=0, T_i^m is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) on H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell).

Step 4 (descend from T_i^m to T_i). We first note that H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space: X_k is a smooth variety of finite type over the algebraically closed field k, and by the finiteness theorem for etale cohomology its cohomology with Q_ell coefficients is finite-dimensional in every degree. The ground field Q_ell has characteristic 0, and T_i is an invertible Q_ell-linear operator on H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) (Step 1). We now apply the proved linear-algebra lemma Spark/9827c89e17d0e461/896297 with K = Q_ell, V = H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell), T = T_i, and r = m: since T_i^m is semisimple (equivalently, diagonalizable over the algebraic closure overline(Q_ell) of Q_ell, by Step 3), it follows that T_i is semisimple, i.e. diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Hence T_i is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every i>=0.

Step 5 (pass to the inverse). We claim that T_i^{-1} is also diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). Indeed, since T_i is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), there exists a basis {v_j} of H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) consisting of eigenvectors of T_i tensor id, say (T_i tensor id) v_j = lambda_j v_j. Because T_i is invertible, every eigenvalue lambda_j is nonzero (a zero eigenvalue would make T_i tensor id, hence T_i, non-invertible). Then (T_i^{-1} tensor id) v_j = lambda_j^{-1} v_j, so the same basis {v_j} consists of eigenvectors of T_i^{-1} tensor id and therefore diagonalizes T_i^{-1} tensor id. Hence T_i^{-1} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every i>=0.

Conclusion. For every i>=0, T_i^{-1} is precisely the inverse of the q-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^i_et(X_k, Q_ell). By Step 5 this inverse is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). This is exactly the desired conclusion, completing the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be an F_{q^m}-rational smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, let i:Y->X, and write H^r(Z)=H^r_et(Z_k,Q_ell). Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of Y, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and suppose FL=q^mLF. Then the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)(-1)->H^d(X) has image L H^{d-2}(X).
proof: Step 1. Since d>=2, d-2>=0. By hypothesis Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}. A very ample divisor is ample, so Y is a smooth ample geometrically connected divisor defined over F_{q^m}. Step 2. Apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/e7bf2b. Its hypotheses are met: q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, X is smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, and Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X defined over F_{q^m}. Hence the restriction map i^*:H^{d-2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-2}_et(Y_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism of Q_ell[F]-modules, where F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius. In particular it is an isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces. In the edge case d=2, this map is the identity on Q_ell because H^0_et of a geometrically connected variety over k is Q_ell. Step 3. The target fixes a nonzero element of Q_ell(1), and we use it to identify Tate twists with Q_ell. Under this identification, the cycle class xi of Y is an element of H^2_et(X_k,Q_ell), L is cup product with xi, and the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)(-1)->H^d(X) is exactly the Gysin map i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)->H^d(X) appearing in the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/b8e973. The hypotheses of that lemma are now satisfied: X is smooth projective geometrically connected of dimension d>=2; Y is a smooth ample geometrically connected divisor defined over F_{q^m}; the required identification of Tate twists is fixed; xi is the cycle class of Y; L is cup product with xi; and i^*:H^{d-2}(X)->H^{d-2}(Y) is an isomorphism by Step 2. Therefore b8e973 gives im(i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)->H^d(X)) = L H^{d-2}(X). Translating back through the fixed identification Q_ell(1) ~ Q_ell gives im(i_!:H^{d-2}(Y)(-1)->H^d(X)) = L H^{d-2}(X). The additional displayed assumptions that L^{d-n}:H^n(X)->H^{2d-n}(X) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d and that FL=q^m LF are not used in this proof, since the conclusion already follows directly from the two cited lemmas.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1). Let xi be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor, let L be cup product with xi, suppose L^{d-n}:H^n_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{2d-n}_et(X_k,Q_ell) is an isomorphism for 0<=n<=d, put P^d=ker(L:H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell)->H^{d+2}_et(X_k,Q_ell)), let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, suppose F L=q^m L F, let beta be the Poincare pairing on H^d_et(X_k,Q_ell), and let sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C be an embedding. If for some N>=1 the form G_N^P(x,y)=beta(x,F^N y)+(-1)^d q^{mdN} beta(x,F^{-N} y) is positive definite on P^d, then the endomorphism q^{mdN}F^{-N}+(-1)^dF^N of P^d is injective.
proof:
I have all the information I need. The proof is self-contained except for citing `eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a` to establish that $F$ is an automorphism of $H^d$ and $H^{d+2}$ with a well-defined inverse. The bilinearity of the Poincaré pairing over $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ is a standard fact that I state directly.

Let me now write the complete proof following the reviser's guidance with the corrected scalar factors.

{
  "lemma_id": "Miner/16d24b0281973336/84d699",
  "cited_lemmas": ["eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a"],
  "cited_references": [],
  "proof": "We work over $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$. Let $H^s = H^s_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ and write $F_s$ for the action of the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius on $H^s$.

**Step 0: $F$ is an automorphism of $H^d$ and $H^{d+2}$ with well-defined inverse.**
By the cited lemma (applied with $q$ replaced by $q^m$, so that $\sigma': k \to k$ is the $q^m$-power field automorphism $\sigma'(a) = a^{q^m}$), the pullback maps $F_{ar} := (\mathrm{id}_X \times \sigma')^*$ and $F_{geo} := (\mathrm{id}_X \times (\sigma')^{-1})^*$ are $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear automorphisms of $H^i_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k, \mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ for every $i \geq 0$, and $F_{geo} = F_{ar}^{-1}$. In our notation, $F = F_{ar}$ is the $q^m$-power arithmetic Frobenius, and $F^{-1} = F_{geo}$ is the $q^m$-power geometric Frobenius. In particular, $F \in \mathrm{GL}(H^d)$ and $F \in \mathrm{GL}(H^{d+2})$, and $F^{-1}$ denotes the inverse on each of these spaces.

Let $L: H^d \to H^{d+2}$ be cup product with $\xi$, and let $P^d = \ker(L)$. By hypothesis, $F_{d+2} L = q^m L F_d$ (the commutation relation in degrees $d$ and $d+2$).

**Step 1: $F$ preserves $P^d$.**
Let $x \in P^d$, so $Lx = 0$. By the commutation relation applied to $x$:
$$F_{d+2}(Lx) = q^m L(F_d x).$$
The left-hand side is $F_{d+2}(0) = 0$, so $q^m L(F_d x) = 0$. Since $q^m \neq 0$ in $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$, we get $L(F_d x) = 0$, i.e., $F_d x \in P^d$. Equivalently, one may write $L(Fx) = q^{-m} F(Lx) = 0$.

**Step 2: $F^{-1}$ preserves $P^d$.**
From $F_{d+2} L = q^m L F_d$, apply $F_{d+2}^{-1}$ on the left and $F_d^{-1}$ on the right to obtain:
$$L F_d^{-1} = q^m F_{d+2}^{-1} L.$$
Let $y \in P^d$, so $Ly = 0$. Applying this to $y$:
$$L(F_d^{-1} y) = q^m F_{d+2}^{-1}(Ly) = q^m F_{d+2}^{-1}(0) = 0,$$
so $F_d^{-1} y \in P^d$. Equivalently, $L(F^{-1}y) = q^m F^{-1}(Ly) = 0$.

**Step 3: $T$ is a well-defined endomorphism of $P^d$.**
Since $F$ and $F^{-1}$ both preserve $P^d$, their compositions $F^N$ and $F^{-N}$ also preserve $P^d$. Hence
$$T := q^{mdN} F^{-N} + (-1)^d F^N$$
is a well-defined $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-linear endomorphism of $P^d$. Also, the form
$$G_N^P(x,y) := \beta(x, F^N y) + (-1)^d q^{mdN} \beta(x, F^{-N} y)$$
is a well-defined $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-bilinear form on $P^d \times P^d$, since $F^N y, F^{-N} y \in P^d \subset H^d$ and $\beta: H^d \times H^d \to \mathbb{Q}_\ell(d)$ is $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-bilinear (and via the fixed nonzero element of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell(1)$, we identify $\mathbb{Q}_\ell(d)$ with $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$).

**Step 4: $\ker(T) = \{0\}$.**
Suppose $Tx = 0$ for some $x \in P^d$. Then
$$q^{mdN} F^{-N} x + (-1)^d F^N x = 0,$$
so
$$F^N x = -(-1)^d q^{mdN} F^{-N} x = (-1)^{d+1} q^{mdN} F^{-N} x.$$
Now compute $G_N^P(x,x)$:
\begin{align*}
G_N^P(x,x) &= \beta(x, F^N x) + (-1)^d q^{mdN} \beta(x, F^{-N} x) \\
&= \beta(x, (-1)^{d+1} q^{mdN} F^{-N} x) + (-1)^d q^{mdN} \beta(x, F^{-N} x) \\
&= [(-1)^{d+1} + (-1)^d] \, q^{mdN} \, \beta(x, F^{-N} x) \\
&= 0,
\end{align*}
where in the third line we used the $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-bilinearity of $\beta$ to factor out the scalar $q^{mdN}$, and in the last line we used $(-1)^{d+1} = -(-1)^d$.

**Step 5: Positivity contradiction.**
We have shown $G_N^P(x,x) = 0$ in $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$. Applying the embedding $\sigma: \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell \to \mathbb{C}$ (which restricts to an embedding of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$), we get $\sigma(G_N^P(x,x)) = \sigma(0) = 0$. By the hypothesis, $G_N^P$ is positive definite on $P^d$, meaning $\sigma(G_N^P(z,z)) > 0$ for every nonzero $z \in P^d$. Since $\sigma(G_N^P(x,x)) = 0$, it follows that $x = 0$.

Therefore $\ker(T) = \{0\}$, i.e., the endomorphism $q^{mdN}F^{-N} + (-1)^d F^N$ of $P^d$ is injective.

$\blacksquare$"
}

statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, let Kbar be an algebraic closure of K, let sigma:Kbar->C be an embedding, let c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, let V be a finite-dimensional K-vector space, let F in GL_K(V), and let W,Z be F-stable K-subspaces with V=W direct sum Z. Suppose W tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_W with h_W((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h_W(x,y), and Z tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h_Z with h_Z((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y)=sigma(c)h_Z(x,y). Then F is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue lambda of F in Kbar satisfies |sigma(lambda)|=sqrt(sigma(c)).
proof:
We prove the statement in three steps.

Step 0 (Setup and restriction of the embedding). Let K be a field of characteristic 0, Kbar an algebraic closure of K, sigma:Kbar->C an embedding, c in K^* with sigma(c)>0, V a finite-dimensional K-vector space, F in GL_K(V), and let W, Z be F-stable K-subspaces with V = W direct sum Z. By hypothesis, h_W is a positive definite Hermitian form on W tensor_{K,sigma} C with h_W((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h_W(x,y) for all x,y in W tensor_{K,sigma} C, and h_Z is a positive definite Hermitian form on Z tensor_{K,sigma} C with h_Z((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h_Z(x,y) for all x,y in Z tensor_{K,sigma} C. Let sigma_0:K->C be the restriction of sigma to K. Since sigma is an embedding of Kbar into C (an injective field homomorphism with sigma(1)=1), its restriction sigma_0 to the subfield K is likewise an embedding of K into C. Because W, Z, V are K-vector spaces, their scalar extensions by sigma depend only on the restriction of sigma to K: the balancing relation (w*lambda) = (sigma(lambda) w) in the tensor product W tensor_{K,sigma} C uses only values sigma(lambda) for lambda in K. Hence W tensor_{K,sigma} C = W tensor_{K,sigma_0} C, Z tensor_{K,sigma} C = Z tensor_{K,sigma_0} C, and V tensor_{K,sigma} C = V tensor_{K,sigma_0} C as C-vector spaces, and the forms h_W, h_Z are positive definite Hermitian forms on W tensor_{K,sigma_0} C and Z tensor_{K,sigma_0} C respectively satisfying the same scaling identities. Also sigma_0(c) = sigma(c) > 0.

Step 1 (Gluing the two forms into one on V). We now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/e08475 with the data (K, sigma_0, V, c, F, W, Z, h_W, h_Z). Check of hypotheses: K has characteristic 0 and sigma_0:K->C is an embedding; V is a finite-dimensional K-vector space; c in K^* with sigma_0(c) = sigma(c) > 0; F in GL_K(V); V = W direct sum Z as F-stable K-subspaces (this is exactly the given decomposition, and W, Z are F-stable by hypothesis); W tensor_{K,sigma_0} C carries the positive definite Hermitian form h_W with h_W((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sigma_0(c) h_W(x,y) for all x,y (the scaling identity, since sigma_0(c)=sigma(c)); and Z tensor_{K,sigma_0} C carries the positive definite Hermitian form h_Z with h_Z((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sigma_0(c) h_Z(x,y) for all x,y. Therefore, by that lemma, V tensor_{K,sigma_0} C = V tensor_{K,sigma} C carries a positive definite Hermitian form h with h((F tensor id)x,(F tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h(x,y) for all x,y in V tensor_{K,sigma} C. (Concretely, h is the direct sum h_W direct sum h_Z: for x = w + z and y = w' + z' with w, w' in W tensor_{K,sigma} C and z, z' in Z tensor_{K,sigma} C, set h(x,y) = h_W(w,w') + h_Z(z,z'); this is well-defined because the decomposition V = W direct sum Z is unique, it is Hermitian, and it is positive definite since h(x,x) = h_W(w,w) + h_Z(z,z) >= 0 with equality only when w = 0 and z = 0, i.e. x = 0; and the scaling identity follows from the two given scaling identities.)

Step 2 (Diagonalizability and the eigenvalue bound). We now apply the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/503846 with the data (K, Kbar, sigma, c, V, T = F, h). Check of hypotheses: K has characteristic 0; Kbar is an algebraic closure of K; sigma:Kbar->C is an embedding; c in K^* with sigma(c) > 0; V is a finite-dimensional K-vector space; T = F is in GL_K(V); and h is a positive definite Hermitian form on V tensor_{K,sigma} C with h((T tensor id)x,(T tensor id)y) = sigma(c) h(x,y) for all x,y, which is exactly the form and identity obtained in Step 1. Therefore, by that lemma, F is diagonalizable over Kbar and every eigenvalue lambda of F in Kbar satisfies |sigma(lambda)| = sqrt(sigma(c)).

This is precisely the desired conclusion, completing the proof.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}. Let Y be a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, let U be the open complement of Y in X, let F be the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius, and let delta:H^d_et(U_k,Q_ell)->H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) be the Gysin boundary. Suppose that for every smooth projective geometrically connected variety Z of dimension less than d over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r_et(Z_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every r>=0 with eigenvalues, viewed in overline(Q_ell), of Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Then a -> F a restricts to a diagonalizable endomorphism of im(delta) over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue of this endomorphism, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}.
proof:
We prove the corrected statement: the endomorphism a -> F a (where F is the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius acting on H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1)) restricts to a diagonalizable endomorphism of im(delta), and every eigenvalue of this restriction, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}.

SETUP AND NOTATION. Fix a nonzero element of Q_ell(1) and identify Tate twists with Q_ell; this fixes the meaning of H^{d-1}_et(Y_k,Q_ell)(-1) and of the Frobenius action on it. Write H^s(Z) = H^s_et(Z_k,Q_ell). We use three Frobenius endomorphisms, all q^m-power arithmetic Frobenii:
  - F_{d-1}: the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y) (untwisted);
  - F: the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) (twisted). This is the endomorphism denoted simply by F in the target statement, since im(delta) is a subspace of H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) and the conclusion concerns the action on im(delta);
  - F_U: the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^d(U).
Recall that "Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}" means: for every embedding sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C and every such eigenvalue lambda, |sigma(lambda)| = q^{m(d-3)/2}.

CLAIM 1 (F_{d-1} is diagonalizable with the middle weight). The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F_{d-1} on H^{d-1}(Y) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), and every eigenvalue of F_{d-1} on H^{d-1}(Y), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2}.
Proof of Claim 1. Since Y is a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on the d-dimensional X, Y is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d-1 over F_{q^m}. Because d>=3, we have d-1 < d. The hypothesis of the lemma (the induction hypothesis) asserts that for every smooth projective geometrically connected variety Z of dimension < d over F_{q^m}, the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^r(Z_k,Q_ell) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell) for every r>=0 with eigenvalues, viewed in overline(Q_ell), of Weil absolute value q^{mr/2}. Applying this with Z = Y (dimension d-1 < d) and r = d-1 gives exactly the claim. QED Claim 1.

CLAIM 2 (F on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) is diagonalizable). The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius F on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
Proof of Claim 2. We have a canonical isomorphism of Q_ell-vector spaces H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) = H^{d-1}(Y) tensor_{Q_ell} Q_ell(-1). The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is functorial and, being pullback by the q^m-power Frobenius morphism of the base, it respects tensor products of coefficient systems; hence the Frobenius on the tensor product H^{d-1}(Y) tensor Q_ell(-1) is the tensor product F_{d-1} tensor F_{Q_ell(-1)} of the Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y) and the Frobenius on the one-dimensional Q_ell-vector space Q_ell(-1). Since Q_ell(-1) is one-dimensional over Q_ell, F_{Q_ell(-1)} is multiplication by a scalar c in Q_ell. The q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is an automorphism of every cohomology group (its inverse is the corresponding geometric Frobenius), so its action on the one-dimensional space Q_ell(-1) is by a nonzero scalar, i.e. c in Q_ell^*. Thus F = F_{d-1} tensor c.
By Claim 1, F_{d-1} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell): there exist a basis v_1,...,v_N of H^{d-1}(Y) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell) and scalars lambda_1,...,lambda_N in overline(Q_ell) such that F_{d-1}(v_i) = lambda_i v_i for i=1,...,N. Then v_1 tensor 1, ..., v_N tensor 1 is a basis of H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell), and for each i,
  F(v_i tensor 1) = (F_{d-1} tensor F_{Q_ell(-1)})(v_i tensor 1) = F_{d-1}(v_i) tensor F_{Q_ell(-1)}(1) = (lambda_i v_i) tensor (c.1) = (c lambda_i)(v_i tensor 1).
So each v_i tensor 1 is an eigenvector of F with eigenvalue c lambda_i, and these eigenvectors form a basis; therefore F is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). QED Claim 2.

CLAIM 3 (weight on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1)). Every eigenvalue of F on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}.
Proof of Claim 3. We invoke the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/477ab8 with n = d-1. Its hypotheses are satisfied: q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), n = d-1 >= 1 (since d>=3 implies d-1>=2>=1), Y is a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension n = d-1 over F_{q^m}, and (by Claim 1) every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y) = H^n(Y), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-1)/2} = q^{mn/2}. By 477ab8, every eigenvalue of the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) = H^n(Y)(-1), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(n-2)/2} = q^{m(d-3)/2}. QED Claim 3.

CLAIM 4 (F preserves im(delta)). The subspace im(delta) of H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) is stable under F; consequently a -> F a is a well-defined Q_ell-linear endomorphism of im(delta).
Proof of Claim 4. We invoke the proved lemma Miner/16d24b0281973336/d22a5d. Its hypotheses match the setup exactly: q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=3, X smooth projective geometrically connected of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}, Y a smooth very ample geometrically connected divisor on X, U the open complement, delta:H^d(U)->H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) the Gysin boundary, and F_U, F_Y the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenii on H^d(U) and H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) respectively. Note that the F_Y in d22a5d is precisely the endomorphism F of H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) used throughout (the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1)). The conclusion of d22a5d is F_Y delta = delta F_U, i.e. F delta = delta F_U. Now let a be in im(delta). Then a = delta(u) for some u in H^d(U), and
  F(a) = F(delta(u)) = delta(F_U(u)),
which lies in im(delta). Hence F(im(delta)) is contained in im(delta), so im(delta) is F-stable, and a -> F a is a well-defined Q_ell-linear endomorphism of im(delta). QED Claim 4.

CLAIM 5 (the restriction is diagonalizable). The endomorphism a -> F a of im(delta) is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell).
Proof of Claim 5. We invoke the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_515 with K = Q_ell, V = H^{d-1}(Y)(-1), T = F, and W = im(delta). We verify the hypotheses: K = Q_ell is a field; V is a finite-dimensional Q_ell-vector space; T = F is a Q_ell-linear automorphism of V (the q^m-power arithmetic Frobenius is invertible, its inverse being the corresponding geometric Frobenius), and T is semisimple, i.e. diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell), by Claim 2; W = im(delta) is a Q_ell-linear subspace of V (it is the image of the Q_ell-linear map delta) and is T-stable by Claim 4. By lemma_515, the restriction T|_W = F|_{im(delta)} is semisimple. For a linear operator over Q_ell, semisimplicity is equivalent to diagonalizability over the algebraic closure overline(Q_ell); hence F|_{im(delta)} is diagonalizable over overline(Q_ell). QED Claim 5.

CLAIM 6 (weight on im(delta)). Every eigenvalue of the endomorphism a -> F a of im(delta), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}.
Proof of Claim 6. Let lambda be an eigenvalue of F|_{im(delta)} viewed in overline(Q_ell), with eigenvector w in im(delta) tensor_{Q_ell} overline(Q_ell), w != 0, so that F(w) = lambda w. Since im(delta) tensor overline(Q_ell) is a subspace of H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) tensor overline(Q_ell), the same equality F(w) = lambda w shows that lambda is an eigenvalue of F on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) (with the same eigenvector w, now regarded as a vector of H^{d-1}(Y)(-1) tensor overline(Q_ell)). By Claim 3, every eigenvalue of F on H^{d-1}(Y)(-1), viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}; therefore for every embedding sigma:overline(Q_ell)->C, |sigma(lambda)| = q^{m(d-3)/2}. QED Claim 6.

CONCLUSION. Claim 5 establishes that a -> F a restricts to a diagonalizable endomorphism of im(delta) over overline(Q_ell), and Claim 6 establishes that every eigenvalue of this endomorphism, viewed in overline(Q_ell), has Weil absolute value q^{m(d-3)/2}. This is exactly the statement to be proved. QED.

statement: Let q=p^a, ell != p, m>=1, k=overline(F_q), d>=2, and let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d over F_{q^m}.
